abandon: 1. To give up or relinquish control of, to surrender or to give oneself over, or to yield to one's emotions. 2. To desist in doing, practicing, following, holding, or adhering to; to turn away from; to permit to lapse; to renounce; to discontinue.
ability: 1. Suitableness. 2. The quality or state of being able; capacity to do or of doing something; having the necessary power.
airport: An airfield (an area designated for the takeoff and landing of aircraft), including one or more runways and (for commercial airports) one or more passenger terminals.
absolute: 1. That which is independent of context-dependent interpretation, inviolate, fundamental. 2. Anything that is absolute.
academic: 1. (usually capitalized) A follower of Plato, a Platonist. 2. A senior member of an academy, college, or university; a person who attends an academy; a person engaged in scholarly pursuits; one who is academic in practice.
accept: 1. To receive, especially with a consent, with favour, or with approval. 2. To admit to a place or a group.
accident: 1. An unexpected event with negative consequences occurring without the intention of the one suffering the consequences. 2. Especially, a collision or similar unintended event that causes damage or death.
account: 1. A registry of pecuniary transactions; a written or printed statement of business dealings or debts and credits, and also of other things subjected to a reckoning or review. 2. A sum of money deposited at a bank and subject to withdrawal.
accurate: 1. Telling the truth or giving a true result; exact; not defective or faulty 2. Deviating only slightly or within acceptable limits.
active: 1. A person or thing that is acting or capable of acting. 2. Any component that is not passive. See Passivity (engineering).
actual: 1. An actual, real one; notably: 2. Relating to a person's acts or deeds; active, practical
advance: 1. A forward move; improvement or progression. 2. An amount of money or credit, especially given as a loan, or paid before it is due; an advancement.
advice: 1. An opinion offered in an effort to be helpful. 2. Deliberate consideration; knowledge.
afraid: 1. (usually used predicatively, not attributively, be afraid) Impressed with fear or apprehension; in fear. 2. Regretful, sorry.
agency: 1. The capacity, condition, or state of acting or of exerting power. 2. The capacity of individuals to act independently and to make their own free choices.
agenda: 1. A temporally organized plan for matters to be attended to. 2. A list of matters to be taken up (as at a meeting).
agreement: 1. An understanding between entities to follow a specific course of conduct. 2. A state whereby several parties share a view or opinion; the state of not contradicting one another.
amount: 1. The total, aggregate or sum of material (not applicable to discrete numbers or units or items in standard English). 2. A quantity or volume.
animal: 1. In scientific usage, a multicellular organism that is usually mobile, whose cells are not encased in a rigid cell wall (distinguishing it from plants and fungi) and which derives energy solely from the consumption of other organisms (distinguishing it from plants). 2. In non-scientific usage, any member of the kingdom Animalia other than a human.
answer: 1. A response or reply; something said or done in reaction to a statement or question. 2. A solution to a problem.
appear: 1. To come or be in sight; to be in view; to become visible. 2. To come before the public.
approach: 1. The act of drawing near; a coming or advancing near. 2. An access, or opportunity of drawing near.
arrange: 1. To set up; to organize; to put into an orderly sequence or arrangement. 2. To plan; to prepare in advance.
article: 1. A piece of nonfictional writing such as a story, report, opinion piece, or entry in a newspaper, magazine, journal, dictionary, encyclopedia, etc. 2. An object, a member of a group or class.
artist: 1. A person who creates art. 2. A person who is skilled at some activity.
aspect: 1. Any specific feature, part, or element of something. 2. The way something appears when viewed from a certain direction or perspective.
attack: 1. An attempt to cause damage, injury to, or death of opponent or enemy. 2. An attempt to detract from the worth or credibility of, a person, position, idea, object, or thing, by physical, verbal, emotional, or other assault.
attempt: 1. The action of trying at something. 2. An assault or attack, especially an assassination attempt.
attend: 1. To listen to (something or someone); to pay attention to; regard; heed. 2. To listen (to, unto).
author: 1. The originator or creator of a work, especially of a literary composition. 2. Someone who writes books for a living.
average: 1. The arithmetic mean. 2. Any measure of central tendency, especially any mean, the median, or the mode.
avoid: 1. To try not to meet or communicate with (a person); to shun 2. To keep away from; to keep clear of; to stay away from
balance: 1. A state in which opposing forces harmonise; equilibrium. 2. Mental equilibrium; mental health; calmness, a state of remaining clear-headed and unperturbed.
battle: 1. A contest, a struggle. 2. A general action, fight, or encounter, in which all the divisions of an army are or may be engaged; a combat, an engagement.
beauty: 1. The quality of being (especially visually) attractive, pleasing, fine or good-looking; comeliness. 2. Someone who is beautiful.
belief: 1. Mental acceptance of a claim as true. 2. Faith or trust in the reality of something; often based upon one's own reasoning, trust in a claim, desire of actuality, and/or evidence considered.
belong: 1. To have its proper place. 2. (followed by to) To be part of, or the property of.
benefit: 1. An advantage; help or aid from something. 2. A payment made in accordance with an insurance policy or a public assistance scheme.
border: 1. The outer edge of something. 2. A decorative strip around the edge of something.
bottle: 1. A container, typically made of glass or plastic and having a tapered neck, used primarily for holding liquids. 2. The contents of such a container.
bottom: 1. The lowest part of anything. 2. Character, reliability, staying power, dignity, integrity or sound judgment.
boundary: 1. The dividing line or location between two areas. 2. (often in the plural) The bounds, confines, or limits between immaterial things (such as one’s comfort zone, privacy, or professional sphere and the realm beyond).
branch: 1. The woody part of a tree arising from the trunk and usually dividing. 2. Any of the parts of something that divides like the branch of a tree.
breath: 1. The act or process of breathing. 2. A single act of breathing in or out; a breathing of air.
bridge: 1. A construction or natural feature that spans a divide. 2. An arch or superstructure.
broken: 1. To separate into two or more pieces, to fracture or crack, by a process that cannot easily be reversed for reassembly. 2. To divide (something, often money) into smaller units.
budget: 1. The amount of money or resources earmarked for a particular institution, activity or time-frame. 2. An itemized summary of intended expenditure; usually coupled with expected revenue.
building: 1. The act or process by which something is built; construction. 2. A closed structure with walls and a roof.
burden: 1. A heavy load. 2. A responsibility, onus.
button: 1. One who adjusts, especially for the insurance industry's employment title "loss adjuster" (or "claims adjuster" in the United States). 2. A knob or disc that is passed through a loop or (buttonhole), serving as a fastener.
cabinet: 1. A storage closet either separate from, or built into, a wall. 2. A cupboard.
camera: 1. A device for taking still or moving pictures or photographs. 2. The viewpoint in a three-dimensional game or simulation.
campus: 1. The grounds or property of a school, college, university, business, church, or hospital, often understood to include buildings and other structures. 2. An institution of higher education and its ambiance.
cancel: 1. A cancellation (US); (nonstandard in some kinds of English). 2. An enclosure; a boundary; a limit.
cancer: 1. A disease in which the cells of a tissue undergo uncontrolled (and often rapid) proliferation. 2. Something damaging that spreads throughout something else.
candle: 1. A light source consisting of a wick embedded in a solid, flammable substance such as wax, tallow, or paraffin. 2. The protruding, removable portion of a filter, particularly a water filter.
canvas: 1. A type of coarse cloth, woven from hemp, useful for making sails and tents or as a surface for paintings. 2. A piece of canvas cloth stretched across a frame on which one may paint.
capacity: 1. The ability to hold, receive or absorb 2. A measure of such ability; volume
capital: 1. Already-produced durable goods available for use as a factor of production, such as steam shovels (equipment) and office buildings (structures). 2. Money and wealth. The means to acquire goods and services, especially in a non-barter system.
captain: 1. A chief or leader. 2. The person lawfully in command of a ship or other vessel.
capture: 1. An act of capturing; a seizing by force or stratagem. 2. The securing of an object of strife or desire, as by the power of some attraction.
career: 1. One's calling in life; a person's occupation; one's profession. 2. General course of action or conduct in life, or in a particular part of it.
careful: 1. Taking care; attentive to potential danger, error or harm; cautious. 2. Conscientious and painstaking; meticulous.
carrier: 1. A person or object that carries someone or something else. 2. A carrier pigeon.
castle: 1. A large building that is fortified and contains many defences; in previous ages often inhabited by a nobleman or king. 2. An instance of castling.
casual: 1. A worker who is only working for a company occasionally, not as its permanent employee. 2. A soldier temporarily at a place of duty, usually en route to another place of duty.
cattle: 1. Domesticated bovine animals (cows, bulls, steers etc). 2. Certain other livestock, such as sheep, pigs or horses.
caught: 1. (heading) To capture, overtake. 2. (heading) To seize hold of.
center: 1. The point in the interior of a circle that is equidistant from all points on the circumference. 2. The point in the interior of a sphere that is equidistant from all points on the circumference.
central: 1. Being in the centre. 2. Having or containing the centre of something.
century: 1. A period of 100 consecutive years; often specifically a numbered period with conventional start and end dates, e.g., the twentieth century, which stretches from (strictly) 1901 through 2000, or (informally) 1900 through 1999. The first century AD was from 1 to 100. 2. A unit in ancient Roman army, originally of 100 army soldiers as part of a cohort, later of more varied sizes (but typically containing 60 to 70 or 80) soldiers or other men (guards, police, firemen), commanded by a centurion.
certain: 1. (with "the") Something certain. 2. Sure, positive, not doubting.
chamber: 1. A room or set of rooms, particularly: 2. A chamberpot.
chance: 1. An opportunity or possibility. 2. Random occurrence; luck.
change: 1. The process of becoming different. 2. Small denominations of money given in exchange for a larger denomination.
channel: 1. The physical confine of a river or slough, consisting of a bed and banks. 2. The natural or man-made deeper course through a reef, bar, bay, or any shallow body of water.
chapter: 1. (authorship) One of the main sections into which the text of a book is divided. 2. A section of a social or religious body.
charge: 1. The amount of money levied for a service. 2. A ground attack against a prepared enemy.
charity: 1. An organization, the objective of which is to carry out a charitable purpose. 2. The goods or money given to those in need.
charter: 1. A document issued by some authority, creating a public or private institution, and defining its purposes and privileges. 2. A similar document conferring rights and privileges on a person, corporation etc.
cheese: 1. A dairy product made from curdled or cultured milk. 2. Any particular variety of cheese.
choice: 1. An option; a decision; an opportunity to choose or select something. 2. The power to choose.
choose: 1. To pick; to make the choice of; to select. 2. To elect.
circle: 1. A two-dimensional geometric figure, a line, consisting of the set of all those points in a plane that are equally distant from a given point (center). 2. A two-dimensional geometric figure, a disk, consisting of the set of all those points of a plane at a distance less than or equal to a fixed distance (radius) from a given point.
citizen: 1. A resident of a city or town, especially one with legally-recognized rights or duties. 2. A legally-recognized member of a state, with associated rights and obligations; a person considered in terms of this role.
classic: 1. A perfect and/or early example of a particular style. 2. An artistic work of lasting worth, such as a film or song.
climate: 1. An area of the earth's surface between two parallels of latitude. 2. A region of the Earth.
closest: 1. (physical) To remove a gap. 2. (social) To finish, to terminate.
clothes: 1. A woven fabric such as used in dressing, decorating, cleaning or other practical use. 2. Specifically, a tablecloth, especially as spread before a meal or removed afterwards.
coastal: Relating to the coast; on or near the coast, as a coastal town, a coastal breeze
collect: 1. To gather together; amass. 2. To get; particularly, get from someone.
college: 1. A corporate group; a group of colleagues. 2. (in some proper nouns) A group sharing common purposes or goals.
column: 1. A solid upright structure designed usually to support a larger structure above it, such as a roof or horizontal beam, but sometimes for decoration. 2. A vertical line of entries in a table, usually read from top to bottom.
combat: 1. A battle, a fight (often one in which weapons are used). 2. A struggle for victory
comfort: 1. Contentment, ease. 2. Something that offers comfort.
command: 1. An order to do something. 2. The right or authority to order, control or dispose of; the right to be obeyed or to compel obedience.
comment: 1. A spoken or written remark. 2. A remark embedded in source code in such a way that it will be ignored by the compiler or interpreter, typically to help people to understand the code.
common: 1. Mutual good, shared by more than one. 2. A tract of land in common ownership; common land.
company: 1. A team; a group of people who work together professionally. 2. A small group of birds or animals.
compare: 1. Comparison. 2. An instruction or command that compares two values.
compass: 1. A magnetic or electronic device used to determine the cardinal directions (usually magnetic or true north). 2. A pair of compasses (a device used to draw an arc or circle).
complex: 1. A network of interconnected systems. 2. A collection of buildings with a common purpose, such as a university or military base.
concept: 1. An abstract and general idea; an abstraction. 2. Understanding retained in the mind, from experience, reasoning and imagination; a generalization (generic, basic form), or abstraction (mental impression), of a particular set of instances or occurrences (specific, though different, recorded manifestations of the concept).
concern: 1. That which affects one’s welfare or happiness. A matter of interest to someone. The adposition before the matter of interest is usually over, about or for. 2. The expression of solicitude, anxiety, or compassion toward a thing or person.
concert: 1. Agreement in a design or plan; union formed by mutual communication of opinions and views; accordance in a scheme; harmony; simultaneous action. 2. Musical accordance or harmony; concord.
conduct: 1. The act or method of controlling or directing 2. Skillful guidance or management; leadership
connect: 1. (of an object) To join (to another object): to attach, or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to another object. 2. (of two objects) To join: to attach, or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to each other.
contact: 1. The act of touching physically; being in close association. 2. The establishment of communication (with).
contain: 1. To hold inside. 2. To include as a part.
content: 1. (except in phrases) Satisfaction, contentment; pleasure. 2. To give contentment or satisfaction; to satisfy; to make happy.
contest: 1. Controversy; debate. 2. Struggle for superiority; combat.
context: 1. The surroundings, circumstances, environment, background or settings that determine, specify, or clarify the meaning of an event or other occurrence. 2. The text in which a word or passage appears and which helps ascertain its meaning.
control: 1. Influence or authority over something. 2. A separate group or subject in an experiment against which the results are compared where the primary variable is low or non-existent.
convert: 1. A person who has converted to a religion. 2. A person who is now in favour of something that he or she previously opposed or disliked.
correct: 1. Free from error; true; accurate. 2. With good manners; well behaved; conforming with accepted standards of behaviour.
council: 1. A committee that leads or governs (e.g. city council, student council). 2. Discussion or deliberation.
counsel: 1. The exchange of opinions and advice especially in legal issues; consultation. 2. Exercise of judgment; prudence.
counter: 1. One who counts 2. A reckoner; someone who collects data by counting; an enumerator.
courage: 1. The quality of being confident, not afraid or easily intimidated, but without being incautious or inconsiderate. 2. The ability to overcome one's fear, do or live things which one finds frightening.
course: 1. A sequence of events. 2. A path that something or someone moves along.
crystal: 1. A solid composed of an array of atoms or molecules possessing long-range order and arranged in a pattern which is periodic in three dimensions. 2. A piece of glimmering, shining mineral resembling ice or glass.
culture: 1. The arts, customs, lifestyles, background, and habits that characterize a particular society or nation. 2. The beliefs, values, behaviour and material objects that constitute a people's way of life.
current: 1. The generally unidirectional movement of a gas or fluid. 2. The part of a fluid that moves continuously in a certain direction, especially short for ocean current.
custom: 1. Frequent repetition of the same behavior; way of behavior common to many; ordinary manner; habitual practice; method of doing, living or behaving. 2. Traditional beliefs or rituals
damage: 1. Injury or harm; the condition or measure of something not being intact. 2. Cost or expense.
danger: 1. Exposure to likely harm; peril. 2. An instance or cause of likely harm.
darker: 1. Having an absolute or (more often) relative lack of light. 2. (of colour) Dull or deeper in hue; not bright or light.
debate: 1. An argument, or discussion, usually in an ordered or formal setting, often with more than two people, generally ending with a vote or other decision. 2. An informal and spirited but generally civil discussion of opposing views.
decade: 1. A group, set, or series of ten , particularly: 2. A set of resistors, capacitors, etc. connected so as to provide even increments between one and ten times a base electrical resistance.
decide: 1. To resolve (a contest, problem, dispute, etc.); to choose, determine, or settle 2. To make a judgment, especially after deliberation
declare: 1. To make clear, explain, interpret. 2. To make a declaration.
decline: 1. Downward movement, fall. 2. A sloping downward, e.g. of a hill or road.
default: 1. The condition of failing to meet an obligation. 2. The original software programming settings as set by the factory
defend: 1. To ward off attacks against; to fight to protect; to guard. 2. To support by words or writing; to vindicate, talk in favour of.
degree: 1. A stage of proficiency or qualification in a course of study, now especially an award bestowed by a university or, in some countries, a college, as a certification of academic achievement. (In the United States, can include secondary schools.) 2. A unit of measurement of angle equal to 1/360 of a circle's circumference.
deliver: 1. To set free from restraint or danger. 2. (process) To do with birth.
demand: 1. The desire to purchase goods and services. 2. The amount of a good or service that consumers are willing to buy at a particular price.
density: 1. A measure of the mass of matter contained by a unit volume. 2. The ratio of one quantity, representing something of interest, to another quantity representing space, area, or extent in which the thing of interest is distributed.
depend: 1. (followed by on or upon, formerly also by of) To be contingent or conditioned; to have something as a necessary condition; to hinge on. 2. (followed by on or upon) To trust; to have confidence; to rely.
deposit: 1. Sediment or rock that is not native to its present location or is different from the surrounding material. Sometimes refers to ore or gems. 2. That which is placed anywhere, or in anyone's hands, for safekeeping; something entrusted to the care of another.
deserve: 1. To be entitled to, as a result of past actions; to be worthy to have. 2. To earn, win.
design: 1. A specification of an object or process, referring to requirements to be satisfied and thus conditions to be met for them to solve a problem. 2. A plan (with more or less detail) for the structure and functions of an artifact, building or system.
desire: 1. Someone or something wished for. 2. Strong attraction, particularly romantic or sexual.
detail: 1. Something small enough to escape casual notice. 2. A profusion of details.
detect: 1. To discover or find by careful search, examination, or probing 2. Detected.
device: 1. Any piece of equipment made for a particular purpose, especially a mechanical or electrical one. 2. A peripheral device; an item of hardware.
devote: 1. To give one's time, focus one's efforts, commit oneself, etc. entirely for, on, or to a certain matter 2. To consign over; to doom
diamond: 1. A glimmering glass-like mineral that is an allotrope of carbon in which each atom is surrounded by four others in the form of a tetrahedron. 2. A gemstone made from this mineral.
differ: 1. Not to have the same traits or characteristics; to be unalike or distinct. 2. (people, groups, etc.) To have diverging opinions, disagree.
digital: 1. A digital option. 2. Digital equipment or technology.
dignity: 1. The state of being dignified or worthy of esteem: elevation of mind or character. 2. Decorum, formality, stateliness.
direct: 1. To manage, control, steer. 2. To aim (something) at (something else).
disease: 1. An abnormal condition of a human, animal or plant that causes discomfort or dysfunction; distinct from injury insofar as the latter is usually instantaneously acquired. 2. (by extension) Any abnormal or harmful condition, as of society, people's attitudes, way of living etc.
display: 1. A show or spectacle. 2. A piece of work to be presented visually.
distant: 1. Far off (physically, logically or mentally). 2. Emotionally unresponsive or unwilling to express genuine feelings.
divide: 1. A thing that divides. 2. An act of dividing.
doctor: 1. A physician; a member of the medical profession; one who is trained and licensed to heal the sick or injured. The final examination and qualification may award a doctor degree in which case the post-nominal letters are D.O., DPM, M.D., DMD, DDS, in the US or MBBS in the UK. 2. A person who has attained a doctorate, such as a Ph.D. or Th.D. or one of many other terminal degrees conferred by a college or university.
double: 1. Twice the number, amount, size, etc. 2. A person who resembles and stands in for another person, often for safety purposes
driver: 1. One who drives something, in any sense of the verb to drive. 2. Something that drives something, in any sense of the verb to drive.
easily: 1. Comfortably, without discomfort or anxiety. 2. Without difficulty.
effect: 1. The result or outcome of a cause. 2. Impression left on the mind; sensation produced.
effort: 1. The work involved in performing an activity; exertion. 2. An endeavour.
either: 1. (after a negative) As well. 2. One or other of two people or things.
element: 1. One of the simplest or essential parts or principles of which anything consists, or upon which the constitution or fundamental powers of anything are based. 2. A small part of the whole.
emerge: 1. To come into view. 2. To come out of a situation, object or a liquid.
empire: 1. (furniture) Following or imitating a style popular during the First French Empire (1804–1814). 2. (of wine) Produced in a dependency of the British Empire or Commonwealth of Nations.
employ: 1. The state of being an employee; employment. 2. The act of employing someone or making use of something; employment.
empty: 1. (usually plural) A container, especially a bottle, whose contents have been used up, leaving it empty. 2. To make empty; to void; to remove the contents of.
enable: 1. To make somebody able (to do, or to be, something); to give sufficient ability or power to do or to be; to give strength or ability to. 2. To affirm; to make firm and strong.
energy: 1. The impetus behind all motion and all activity. 2. The capacity to do work.
engine: 1. A large construction used in warfare, such as a battering ram, catapult etc. 2. A tool; a utensil or implement.
enough: 1. Sufficiently. 2. Fully; quite; used to express slight augmentation of the positive degree, and sometimes equivalent to very.
ensure: 1. To make a pledge to (someone); to promise, guarantee (someone of something); to assure. 2. To make sure or certain of something (usually some future event or condition).
entire: 1. The whole of something; the entirety. 2. An uncastrated horse; a stallion.
escape: 1. The act of leaving a dangerous or unpleasant situation. 2. Leakage or outflow, as of steam or a liquid, or an electric current through defective insulation.
estate: 1. The collective property and liabilities of someone, especially a deceased person. 2. State; condition.
ethnic: 1. An ethnic person, especially a foreigner or member of an immigrant community. 2. An ethnic minority.
exceed: 1. To be larger, greater than (something). 2. To be better than (something).
except: 1. To exclude; to specify as being an exception. 2. To take exception, to object (to or against).
expand: 1. To change (something) from a smaller form and/or size to a larger one; to spread out or lay open. 2. To increase the extent, number, volume or scope of (something).
expect: 1. To predict or believe that something will happen 2. To consider obligatory or required.
expert: 1. A person with extensive knowledge or ability in a given subject. 2. A player ranking just below master.
export: 1. Something that is exported 2. The act of exporting
extend: 1. To increase in extent. 2. To possess a certain extent; to cover an amount of space.
extent: 1. A range of values or locations. 2. The space, area, volume, etc., to which something extends.
fabric: 1. An edifice or building. 2. The act of constructing, construction, fabrication.
factor: 1. A doer, maker; a person who does things for another person or organization. 2. An agent or representative.
failed: 1. To be unsuccessful. 2. Not to achieve a particular stated goal. (Usage note: The direct object of this word is usually an infinitive.)
fairly: 1. (manner) In a fair manner; fair; not biased or skewed or favouring a certain party 2. Favorably; auspiciously; commodiously.
famous: 1. To make famous; to bring renown to. 2. Well known.
father: 1. A (generally human) male who begets a child. 2. A male ancestor more remote than a parent; a progenitor; especially, a first ancestor.
feature: 1. One's structure or make-up: form, shape, bodily proportions. 2. An important or main item.
fellow: 1. A colleague or partner. 2. A companion; a comrade.
female: 1. One of the female (feminine) sex or gender. 2. Belonging to the sex which typically produces eggs (ova), or to the gender which is typically associated with it.
figure: 1. A drawing or diagram conveying information. 2. The representation of any form, as by drawing, painting, modelling, carving, embroidering, etc.; especially, a representation of the human body.
finger: 1. A slender jointed extremity of the human hand, exclusive of the thumb. 2. Similar or similar-looking extremities in other animals, particularly:
finish: 1. An end; the end of anything. 2. A protective coating given to wood or metal and other surfaces.
flight: 1. The act of flying. 2. An instance of flying.
flower: 1. A colorful, conspicuous structure associated with angiosperms, frequently scented and attracting various insects, and which may or may not be used for sexual reproduction. 2. A reproductive structure in angiosperms (flowering plants), often conspicuously colourful and typically including sepals, petals, and either or both stamens and/or a pistil.
follow: 1. (sometimes attributive) In billiards and similar games, a stroke causing a ball to follow another ball after hitting it. 2. The act of following another user's online activity.
forest: 1. A dense uncultivated tract of trees and undergrowth, larger than woods. 2. Any dense collection or amount.
forget: 1. To lose remembrance of. 2. To unintentionally not do, neglect.
format: 1. The layout of a publication or document. 2. (hence) The form of presentation of something.
former: 1. Previous. 2. First of aforementioned two items. Used with the, often without a noun.
fourth: 1. (not used in the plural) The person or thing in the fourth position. 2. (chiefly American) A quarter, one of four equal parts of a whole.
friend: 1. A person other than a family member, spouse or lover whose company one enjoys and towards whom one feels affection. 2. An associate who provides assistance.
frozen: 1. Especially of a liquid, to become solid due to low temperature. 2. To lower something's temperature to the point that it freezes or becomes hard.
future: 1. The time ahead; those moments yet to be experienced. 2. Something that will happen in moments yet to come.
gallery: 1. An institution, building, or room for the exhibition and conservation of works of art. 2. An establishment that buys, sells, and displays works of art.
garden: 1. An outdoor area containing one or more types of plants, usually plants grown for food or ornamental purposes. 2. The grounds at the front or back of a house.
gather: 1. A plait or fold in cloth, made by drawing a thread through it; a pucker. 2. The inclination forward of the axle journals to keep the wheels from working outward.
gender: 1. Class; kind. 2. (grammar) A division of nouns and pronouns (and sometimes of other parts of speech) into masculine or feminine, and sometimes other categories like neuter or common, and animate or inanimate.
general: 1. A general fact or proposition; a generality. 2. The holder of a senior military title, originally designating the commander of an army and now a specific rank falling under field marshal (in the British army) and below general of the army or general of the air force in the US army and air forces.
genius: 1. Someone possessing extraordinary intelligence or skill; especially somebody who has demonstrated this by a creative or original work in science, music, art etc. 2. Extraordinary mental capacity.
gentle: 1. A person of high birth. 2. A maggot used as bait by anglers.
global: 1. A globally scoped identifier. 2. Concerning all parts of the world.
golden: 1. Kyphosus vaigiensis, a fish found in southeast Asia. 2. Made of, or relating to, gold.
ground: 1. The surface of the Earth, as opposed to the sky or water or underground. 2. Terrain.
growth: 1. An increase in size, number, value, or strength. 2. The act of growing, getting bigger or higher.
guilty: 1. A plea by a defendant who does not contest a charge. 2. A verdict of a judge or jury on a defendant judged to have committed a crime.
habitat: 1. Conditions suitable for an organism or population of organisms to live. 2. A place or type of site where an organism or population naturally occurs.
handle: 1. The part of an object which is (designed to be) held in the hand when used or moved. 2. An instrument for effecting a purpose (either literally or figuratively); a tool, or an opportunity or pretext.
happen: 1. To occur or take place. 2. To happen to; to befall.
hardly: 1. (manner) Firmly, vigorously, with strength or exertion. 2. (manner) Harshly, severely; in a hard manner.
health: 1. The state of being free from physical or psychological disease, illness, or malfunction; wellness. 2. A state of well-being or balance, often physical but sometimes also mental and social; the overall level of function of an organism from the cellular (micro) level to the social (macro) level.
hearing: 1. (stative) To perceive sounds through the ear. 2. (stative) To perceive (a sound, or something producing a sound) with the ear, to recognize (something) in an auditory way.
heaven: 1. The sky, specifically: 2. The abode of God or the gods, traditionally conceived as beyond the sky; especially:
heavily: 1. In a heavy manner. 2. With a great weight.
hidden: 1. Located or positioned out of sight; not visually apparent. 2. Obscure.
highly: 1. In a high or esteemed manner. 2. Extremely; greatly; very much.
history: 1. The aggregate of past events. 2. The branch of knowledge that studies the past; the assessment of notable events.
hollow: 1. A small valley between mountains. 2. A sunken area or unfilled space in something solid; a cavity, natural or artificial.
honest: 1. To adorn or grace; to honour; to make becoming, appropriate, or honourable. 2. (of a person or institution) Scrupulous with regard to telling the truth; not given to swindling, lying, or fraud; upright.
horror: 1. An intense distressing emotion of fear or repugnance. 2. Something horrible; that which excites horror.
hunger: 1. A need or compelling desire for food. 2. (by extension) Any strong desire.
ignore: 1. To deliberately not listen or pay attention to. 2. To pretend to not notice someone or something.
impact: 1. The striking of one body against another; collision. 2. The force or energy of a collision of two objects.
import: 1. Something brought in from an exterior source, especially for sale or trade. 2. The practice of importing.
impose: 1. To establish or apply by authority. 2. To be an inconvenience (on or upon)
impress: 1. The act of impressing. 2. An impression; an impressed image or copy of something.
improve: 1. To make (something) better; to increase the value or productivity (of something). 2. To become better.
include: 1. A piece of source code or other content that is dynamically retrieved for inclusion in another item. 2. To bring into a group, class, set, or total as a (new) part or member.
income: 1. Money one earns by working or by capitalising on the work of others. 2. Money coming in to a fund, account, or policy.
index: 1. An alphabetical listing of items and their location. 2. The index finger; the forefinger.
inform: 1. To instruct, train (usually in matters of knowledge). 2. To communicate knowledge to.
initial: 1. The first letter of a word or a name. 2. In plural, the first letter of each word of a person's full name considered as a unit.
injury: 1. Damage to the body of a human or animal. 2. The violation of a person's reputation, rights, property, or interests.
inside: 1. The interior or inner part. 2. The left-hand side of a road if one drives on the left, or right-hand side if one drives on the right.
insist: 1. (with on or upon or (that + ordinary verb form)) To hold up a claim emphatically. 2. (sometimes with on or upon or (that + subjunctive)) To demand continually that something happen or be done.
install: 1. Installer. A software utility that installs an application. 2. An installation. (Usage originated as a truncated form of the word installation.)
instance: 1. Urgency of manner or words; an urgent request; insistence. 2. A token; a sign; a symptom or indication.
intend: 1. (usually followed by the particle "to") To hope; to wish (something, or something to be accomplished); be intent upon 2. To fix the mind on; attend to; take care of; superintend; regard.
invent: 1. To design a new process or mechanism. 2. To create something fictional for a particular purpose.
invest: 1. To spend money, time, or energy on something, especially for some benefit or purpose; used with in. 2. To clothe or wrap (with garments).
invite: 1. To ask for the presence or participation of someone or something. 2. To request formally.
island: 1. A contiguous area of land, smaller than a continent, totally surrounded by water. 2. An entity surrounded by other entities that are very different from itself.
issue: 1. The action or an instance of flowing or coming out, an outflow, particularly: 2. Someone or something that flows out or comes out, particularly:
itself: 1. (reflexive pronoun) it; A thing as the object of a verb or preposition that also appears as the subject 2. It; used to intensify the subject, especially to emphasize that it is the only participant in the predicate
jacket: 1. A piece of clothing worn on the upper body outside a shirt or blouse, often waist length to thigh length. 2. A piece of a person's suit, beside trousers and, sometimes, waistcoat; coat (US)
journey: 1. A set amount of travelling, seen as a single unit; a discrete trip, a voyage. 2. Any process or progression likened to a journey, especially one that involves difficulties or personal development.
justice: 1. The state or characteristic of being just or fair. 2. The ideal of fairness, impartiality, etc., especially with regard to the punishment of wrongdoing.
justify: 1. To provide an acceptable explanation for. 2. To be a good, acceptable reason for; warrant.
keeper: 1. One who keeps something. 2. A person or thing worth keeping.
kidney: 1. An organ in the body that filters the blood, producing urine. 2. This organ (of an animal) cooked as food.
kitchen: 1. A room or area for preparing food. 2. Cuisine.
ladder: 1. A frame, usually portable, of wood, metal, or rope, used for ascent and descent, consisting of two side pieces to which are fastened rungs (cross strips or rounds acting as steps). 2. A series of stages by which one progresses to a better position.
larger: 1. Of considerable or relatively great size or extent. 2. Abundant; ample.
latest: 1. Near the end of a period of time. 2. Specifically, near the end of the day.
lawyer: 1. A professional person qualified (as by a law degree or bar exam) and authorized to practice law, i.e. represent parties in lawsuits or trials and give legal advice. 2. (by extension) A legal layman who argues points of law.
leader: 1. Any person that leads or directs 2. An animal that leads
league: 1. A group or association of cooperating members. 2. An organization of sports teams which play against one another for a championship.
legacy: 1. Money or property bequeathed to someone in a will. 2. Something inherited from a predecessor or the past.
legend: 1. An unrealistic story depicting past events. 2. A person related to a legend or legends.
lesson: 1. A section of learning or teaching into which a wider learning content is divided. 2. A learning task assigned to a student; homework.
letter: 1. A symbol in an alphabet. 2. A written or printed communication, generally longer and more formal than a note.
level: 1. A tool for finding whether a surface is level, or for creating a horizontal or vertical line of reference. 2. A distance relative to a given reference elevation.
likely: 1. Something or somebody considered likely. 2. Probable; having a greater-than-even chance of occurring
limit: 1. A restriction; a bound beyond which one may not go. 2. A value to which a sequence converges. Equivalently, the common value of the upper limit and the lower limit of a sequence: if the upper and lower limits are different, then the sequence has no limit (i.e., does not converge).
liquid: 1. A substance that is flowing, and keeping no shape, such as water; a substance of which the molecules, while not tending to separate from one another like those of a gas, readily change their relative position, and which therefore retains no definite shape, except that determined by the containing receptacle; an inelastic fluid. 2. A class of consonant sounds that includes l and r.
listen: 1. An instance of listening. 2. To pay attention to a sound or speech.
living: 1. To be alive; to have life. 2. To have permanent residence somewhere, to inhabit, to reside.
locate: 1. To place; to set in a particular spot or position. 2. To find out where something is located.
logical: 1. In agreement with the principles of logic. 2. Reasonable.
machine: 1. A device that directs and controls energy, often in the form of movement or electricity, to produce a certain effect. 2. A vehicle operated mechanically, such as an automobile or an airplane.
mainly: 1. Forcefully, vigorously. 2. Of the production of a sound: loudly, powerfully.
manage: 1. The act of managing or controlling something. 2. (horseriding) Manège.
manner: 1. Mode of action; way of performing or doing anything 2. Characteristic mode of acting or behaving; bearing
manual: 1. A handbook. 2. A booklet that instructs on the usage of a particular machine or product.
margin: 1. The edge of the paper, typically left blank when printing but sometimes used for annotations etc. 2. The edge or border of any flat surface.
marker: 1. An object used to mark a location. 2. Someone or something that marks.
market: 1. A gathering of people for the purchase and sale of merchandise at a set time, often periodic. 2. City square or other fairly spacious site where traders set up stalls and buyers browse the merchandise.
master: 1. Someone who has control over something or someone. 2. The owner of an animal or slave.
hyena: 1. Any of the medium-sized to large feliform carnivores of the subfamily Hyaeninae (genera Hyaena and Crocuta), native to Africa and Asia and noted for the sound similar to laughter which they can make if excited. 2. (Sub-Saharan Africa) A man that performs ritualized sex acts with recently widowed women and menarchal girls.
tortoise: Any of various land-dwelling reptiles, of the family Testudinidae or the order Testudines , whose body is enclosed in a shell (carapace plus plastron). The animal can withdraw its head and four legs partially into the shell, providing some protection from predators.
antelope: 1. Any of several African mammals of the family Bovidae distinguished by hollow horns, which, unlike deer, they do not shed. 2. The pronghorn, Antilocapra americana.
chimpanzee: A species of great ape in the genus Pan, native to Africa, and believed by biologists to be the closest extant relative to humans.
gorilla: 1. The largest of the apes, native to the forests of central Africa, and known for their trait of knuckle-walking. 2. A big and brutish man or a thug; a goon or ruffian.
porcupine: Any of several rodents of either of the taxonomic families Hystricidae (Old World porcupines) or Erethizontidae (New World porcupines), both from the infraorder Hystricognathi, noted for their sharp spines or quills, which are raised when the animal is attacked or surprised.
ostrich: 1. A large flightless bird (Struthio camelus) native to Africa. 2. One who buries one's head in the sand instead of acknowledging problems
python: 1. A type of large constricting snake. 2. Penis
crocodile: 1. Any of the predatory amphibious reptiles of the family Crocodylidae; a crocodilian, any species of the order Crocodilia, which also includes the alligators, caimans and gavials. 2. A long line or procession of people (especially children) walking together.
hippopotamus: A large, semi-aquatic, herbivorous (plant-eating) African mammal (Hippopotamus amphibius)
rhinoceros: Any of several large herbivorous pachyderms native to Africa and Asia of the five extant species in the three extant genera in the family Rhinocerotidae, with thick, gray skin and one or two horns on their snouts.
giraffe: 1. A ruminant, of the genus Giraffa, of the African savannah with long legs and highly elongated neck, which make it the tallest living animal; yellow fur patterned with dark spots, often in the form of a network; and two or more short, skin-covered horns, so-called; strictly speaking the horn-like projections are ossicones. 2. A giraffe unicycle.
zebra: 1. Any of three species of genus Equus: E. grevyi, E. quagga, or E. zebra, all with black and white stripes and native to Africa. 2. A referee.
squirrel: 1. Any of the rodents of the family Sciuridae distinguished by their large bushy tail. 2. A person, usually a freezoner, who applies L. Ron Hubbard's technology in a heterodox manner.
pigeon: 1. One of several birds of the family Columbidae, which consists of more than 300 species. 2. The meat from this bird.
parrot: 1. A kind of bird, many species of which are colourful and able to mimic human speech, of the order Psittaciformes or (narrowly) of the family Psittacidae. 2. A parroter; a person who repeats the words or ideas of others.
owl: 1. Any of various birds of prey of the order Strigiformes that are primarily nocturnal and have forward-looking, binocular vision, limited eye movement, and good hearing. 2. (by extension) A person seen as having owl-like characteristics, especially appearing wise or serious, or being nocturnally active.
vulture: 1. Any of several carrion-eating birds of the families Accipitridae and Cathartidae. 2. A person who profits from the suffering of others.
termite: 1. A white-bodied, wood-consuming insect of the infraorder Isoptera, in the order Blattodea. 2. Of a chimpanzee: to catch termites by inserting a stick or vine into their nest and waiting for them to climb up it.
centipede: Any arthropod of class Chilopoda, which have a segmented body with one pair of legs per segment and from about 20 to 300 legs in total.
millipede: Any of many elongated arthropods, of the class Diplopoda, with cylindrical bodies that have two pairs of legs for each one of their 20 to 100 or more body segments.
scorpion: 1. Any of various arachnids of the order Scorpiones, related to the spiders, characterised by two large front pincers and a curved tail with a venomous sting in the end. 2. An ancient military engine for hurling stones and other missiles.
mongoose: 1. Any of several species of generalist predatory Carnivores in the family Herpestidae; the various species range in size from rats to large cats. The Indian mongoose is noted as a predator of venomous snakes, though other mongoose species have similar habits. 2. Any species of Malagasy mongoose; only distantly related to the Herpestidae, these are members of the family Eupleridae; they resemble mongooses in appearance and habits, but have larger ears and ringed tails.
jackal: 1. Any of certain wild canids of the genus Canis, native to the tropical Old World and smaller than a wolf. 2. A person who performs menial/routine tasks, a dogsbody.
baboon: 1. An Old World monkey of the genus Papio, having dog-like muzzles and large canine teeth, cheek pouches, a short tail, and naked callosities on the buttocks. 2. A foolish or boorish person.
pangolin: The scaly anteater; any of several long-tailed, scale-covered mammals of the order Pholidota of tropical Africa and Asia, the sole extant genus of which is Manis.
chameleon: 1. A small to mid-size reptile, of the family Chamaeleonidae, and one of the best known lizard families able to change color and project its long tongue. 2. A person with inconstant behavior; one able to quickly adjust to new circumstances.
stork: 1. A large wading bird with long legs and a long beak of the family Ciconiidae. 2. (children's folklore) The mythical bringer of babies to families, or good news.
gazelle: An antelope of either of the genera Gazella (mostly native to Africa) or Procapra (native to Asia), capable of running at high speeds for long periods.
matter: 1. Substance, material. 2. A condition, subject or affair, especially one of concern.
mature: 1. Fully developed; grown up in terms of physical appearance, behaviour or thinking; ripe. 2. Brought to a state of complete readiness.
absorb: 1. To include so that it no longer has separate existence; to overwhelm; to cause to disappear as if by swallowing up; to incorporate; to assimilate; to take in and use up. 2. To engulf, as in water; to swallow up.
accent: 1. A higher-pitched or stronger articulation of a particular syllable of a word or phrase in order to distinguish it from the others or to emphasize it. 2. Emphasis or importance in general.
access: 1. A way or means of approaching or entering; an entrance; a passage. 2. The act of approaching or entering; an advance.
accord: 1. Agreement or concurrence of opinion, will, or action. 2. A harmony in sound, pitch and tone; concord.
action: 1. Something done so as to accomplish a purpose. 2. A way of motion or functioning.
adjust: 1. To modify. 2. To improve or rectify.
afford: 1. To incur, stand, or bear without serious detriment, as an act which might under other circumstances be injurious;—with an auxiliary, as can, could, might, etc.; to be able or rich enough. 2. To offer, provide, or supply, as in selling, granting, expending, with profit, or without loss or too great injury.
almost: 1. Something or someone that doesn't quite make it. 2. Very close to, not quite.
always: 1. At all times; throughout all time; since the beginning. 2. Constantly during a certain period, or regularly at stated intervals (opposed to sometimes or occasionally).
anchor: 1. A tool used to moor a vessel to the bottom of a sea or river to resist movement. 2. An iron device so shaped as to grip the bottom and hold a vessel at her berth by the chain or rope attached. (FM 55-501).
annual: 1. An annual publication; a book, periodical, journal, report, comic book, yearbook, etc., which is published serially once a year, which may or may not be in addition to regular weekly or monthly publication. 2. An annual plant; a plant with a life span of just one growing season; a plant which naturally germinates, flowers and dies in one year. Compare biennial, perennial.
appeal: 1. An application for the removal of a cause or suit from an inferior to a superior judge or court for re-examination or review. 2. The mode of proceeding by which such removal is effected.
arrest: 1. A check, stop, an act or instance of arresting something. 2. The condition of being stopped, standstill.
arrive: 1. To reach; to get to a certain place. 2. To obtain a level of success or fame; to succeed.
assist: 1. A helpful action or an act of giving. 2. The act of helping another player score points or goals
assume: 1. To authenticate by means of belief; to surmise; to suppose to be true, especially without proof 2. To take on a position, duty or form
assure: 1. To make sure and secure. 2. (followed by that or of) To give (someone) confidence in the trustworthiness of (something).
attach: 1. To fasten, to join to (literally and figuratively). 2. To adhere; to be attached.
autumn: 1. Traditionally the third of the four seasons, when deciduous trees lose their leaves; typically regarded as being from September 24 to December 22 in parts of the Northern Hemisphere, and the months of March, April and May in the Southern Hemisphere. 2. (by extension) The time period when someone or something is past its prime.
avenue: 1. A broad street, especially one bordered by trees. 2. A way or opening for entrance into a place; a passage by which a place may be reached; a way of approach or of exit.
backup: 1. A reserve or substitute. 2. A copy of a file or record, stored separately from the original, that can be used to recover the original if it is destroyed or damaged.
banner: 1. A flag or standard used by a military commander, monarch or nation. 2. (by extension) The military unit under such a flag or standard.
barely: 1. (degree) By a small margin. 2. (degree) Almost not at all.
barrel: 1. A round vessel or cask, of greater length than breadth, and bulging in the middle, made of staves bound with hoops, and having flat ends or heads. Sometimes applied to a similar cylindrical container made of metal, usually called a drum. 2. The quantity which constitutes a full barrel: the volume or weight this represents varies by local law and custom.
basket: 1. A lightweight container, generally round, open at the top, and tapering toward the bottom. 2. A wire or plastic container similar in shape to a basket, used for carrying articles for purchase in a shop.
beacon: 1. A signal fire to notify of the approach of an enemy, or to give any notice, commonly of warning. 2. A signal or conspicuous mark erected on an eminence near the shore, or moored in shoal water, as a guide to mariners.
behave: 1. To conduct (oneself) well, or in a given way. 2. To act, conduct oneself in a specific manner; used with an adverbial of manner.
behind: 1. The rear, back-end 2. Butt, the buttocks, bottom
beside: 1. Otherwise; else. 2. Next to; at the side of.
better: 1. An entity, usually animate, deemed superior to another; one who has a claim to precedence; a superior. 2. Greater in amount or quantity
bitter: 1. (usually in the plural bitters) A liquid or powder, made from bitter herbs, used in mixed drinks or as a tonic. 2. A type of beer heavily flavored with hops.
bounce: 1. A change of direction of motion after hitting the ground or an obstacle. 2. A movement up and then down (or vice versa), once or repeatedly.
breeze: 1. A light, gentle wind. 2. Any activity that is easy, not testing or difficult.
bright: 1. An artist's brush used in oil and acrylic painting with a long ferrule and a flat, somewhat tapering bristle head. 2. Splendour; brightness
bronze: 1. A naturally occurring or man-made alloy of copper, usually in combination with tin, but also with one or more other metals. 2. A reddish-brown colour, the colour of bronze.
browse: 1. Young shoots and twigs. 2. Fodder for cattle and other animals.
bubble: 1. A spherically contained volume of air or other gas, especially one made from soapy liquid. 2. A small spherical cavity in a solid material.
bucket: 1. A container made of rigid material, often with a handle, used to carry liquids or small items. 2. The amount held in this container.
bullet: 1. A projectile, usually of metal, shot from a gun at high speed. 2. An entire round of unfired ammunition for a firearm, including the projectile, the cartridge casing, the propellant charge, etc.
butter: 1. A soft, fatty foodstuff made by churning the cream of milk (generally cow's milk). 2. Any of various foodstuffs made from other foods or oils, similar in consistency to, eaten like or intended as a substitute for butter (preceded by the name of the food used to make it).
bypass: 1. A road that passes around something, such as a residential area 2. A circumvention
cabin: 1. A small dwelling characteristic of the frontier, especially when built from logs with simple tools and not constructed by professional builders, but by those who meant to live in it. 2. A chalet or lodge, especially one that can hold large groups of people.
cable: 1. (material) A long object used to make a physical connection. 2. (communications) A system for transmitting television or Internet services over a network of coaxial or fibreoptic cables.
canopy: 1. A high cover providing shelter, such as a cloth supported above an object, particularly over a bed. 2. Any overhanging or projecting roof structure, typically over entrances or doors.
canyon: A valley, especially a long, narrow, steep valley, cut in rock by a river.
carbon: 1. The chemical element (symbol C) with an atomic number of 6. It can be found in pure form for example as graphite, a black, shiny and very soft material, or diamond, a colourless, transparent, crystalline solid and the hardest known material. 2. An atom of this element, in reference to a molecule containing it.
carpet: 1. A fabric used as a complete floor covering. 2. Any surface or cover resembling a carpet or fulfilling its function.
carrot: 1. A vegetable with a nutritious, juicy, sweet root that is often orange in colour, Daucus carota, especially the subspecies sativus in the family Apiaceae. 2. A shade of orange similar to the flesh of most carrots (also called carrot orange).
carton: 1. An inexpensive, disposable box-like container fashioned from either paper, paper with wax-covering (wax paper), or other lightweight material. 2. A pack of cigarettes, usually ten, wrapped in cellophane or packed in a light cardboard box.
casino: 1. A public building or room for entertainment, especially gambling. 2. A card game for two to four players.
cavern: 1. A large cave. 2. An underground chamber.
celery: 1. A European herb (Apium graveolens) of the carrot family. 2. The stalks of this herb eaten as a vegetable.
cellar: 1. An enclosed underground space, often under a building, used for storage or shelter. 2. A wine collection, especially when stored in a cellar.
cement: 1. A powdered substance produced by firing (calcining) calcium carbonate (limestone) and clay that develops strong cohesive properties when mixed with water. The main ingredient of concrete. 2. The paste-like substance resulting from mixing such a powder with water, or the rock-like substance that forms when it dries.
cereal: 1. A type of grass (such as wheat, rice or oats) cultivated for its edible grains. 2. The grains of such a grass.
cherry: 1. A small fruit, usually red, black or yellow, with a smooth hard seed and a short hard stem. 2. Prunus subg. Cerasus, trees or shrubs that bear cherries.
chosen: 1. To pick; to make the choice of; to select. 2. To elect.
church: 1. A Christian house of worship; a building where Christian religious services take place. 2. Christians collectively seen as a single spiritual community; Christianity.
cinema: 1. A movie theatre, a movie house 2. Films collectively.
circus: 1. A traveling company of performers that may include acrobats, clowns, trained animals, and other novelty acts, that gives shows usually in a circular tent. 2. A round open space in a town or city where multiple streets meet.
clause: 1. (grammar) A verb, its necessary grammatical arguments, and any adjuncts affecting them. 2. (grammar) A verb along with its subject and their modifiers. If a clause provides a complete thought on its own, then it is an independent (superordinate) clause; otherwise, it is (subordinate) dependent.
clever: 1. Nimble with hands or body; skillful; adept. 2. Resourceful, sometimes to the point of cunning.
client: 1. A customer, a buyer or receiver of goods or services. 2. The role of a computer application or system that requests and/or consumes the services provided by another having the role of server.
clinic: 1. A medical facility, such as a hospital, especially one for the treatment and diagnosis of outpatients. 2. (by extension) A hospital session to diagnose or treat patients.
closed: 1. (physical) To remove a gap. 2. (social) To finish, to terminate.
closet: 1. Any private area, (particularly) bowers in the open air. 2. Any private or inner room, (particularly):
cloudy: 1. Covered with or characterised by clouds; overcast. 2. Not transparent or clear.
clutch: 1. The claw of a predatory animal or bird. 2. (by extension) A grip, especially one seen as rapacious or evil.
coffee: 1. A beverage made by infusing the beans of the coffee plant in hot water. 2. A serving of this beverage.
collar: 1. Anything that encircles the neck. 2. A piece of meat from the neck of an animal.
comedy: 1. A choric song of celebration or revel, especially in Ancient Greece. 2. A light, amusing play with a happy ending.
commit: 1. The act of committing (e.g. a database transaction or source code into a source control repository), making it a permanent change. 2. To give in trust; to put into charge or keeping; to entrust; to consign; used with to or formerly unto.
compel: 1. To drive together, round up 2. To overpower; to subdue.
comply: 1. To yield assent; to accord; to acquiesce, agree, consent; to adapt oneself, to conform. 2. To accomplish, to fulfil.
concur: 1. To unite or agree (in action or opinion); to have a common opinion; to coincide; to correspond. 2. To meet in the same point; to combine or conjoin; to contribute or help towards a common object or effect.
confer: 1. To grant as a possession; to bestow. 2. To talk together, to consult, discuss; to deliberate.
cookie: 1. A small, flat, baked good which is either crisp or soft but firm. 2. A sweet baked good (as in the previous sense) usually having chocolate chips, fruit, nuts etc. baked into it.
corner: 1. The point where two converging lines meet; an angle, either external or internal. 2. An edge or extremity; the part farthest from the center; hence, any quarter or part, or the direction in which it lies.
corpus: 1. A collection of writings, often on a specific topic, of a specific genre, from a specific demographic or a particular author, etc. 2. (specifically) Such a collection in form of an electronic database used for linguistic analyses.
cotton: 1. Gossypium, a genus of plant used as a source of cotton fiber. 2. Any plant that encases its seed in a thin fiber that is harvested and used as a fabric or cloth.
county: 1. The land ruled by a count or a countess. 2. An administrative region of various countries, including Bhutan, Canada, China, Croatia, Ireland, Japan, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Romania, South Korea, Sweden, the United Kingdom, and 48 of the 50 United States (excluding Alaska and Louisiana).
couple: 1. Two partners in a romantic or sexual relationship. 2. Two of the same kind connected or considered together.
coupon: 1. A section of a ticket, showing the holder to be entitled to some specified accommodation or service, as to a passage over a designated line of travel, a particular seat in a theater, a discount, etc. 2. A voucher issued by a manufacturer or retailer which offers a discount on a particular product.
cousin: 1. The child of a person's uncle or aunt; a first cousin. 2. Any relation who is not a direct ancestor or descendant but part of one's extended family; one more distantly related than an uncle, aunt, granduncle, grandaunt, nephew, niece, grandnephew, grandniece, etc.
cradle: 1. A bed or cot for a baby, oscillating on rockers or swinging on pivots. 2. The place of origin, or in which anything is nurtured or protected in the earlier period of existence.
crater: 1. A hemispherical pit created by the impact of a meteorite or other object. 2. The basin-like opening or mouth of a volcano, through which the chief eruption comes; similarly, the mouth of a geyser, about which a cone of silica is often built up.
credit: 1. Reliance on the truth of something said or done; faith; trust. 2. Recognition and respect.
crease: 1. A line or mark made by folding or doubling any pliable substance; hence, a similar mark, however produced. 2. One of the white lines drawn on the pitch to show different areas of play; especially the popping crease, but also the bowling crease and the return crease.
create: 1. To bring into existence; (sometimes in particular:) 2. To cause, to bring (a non-object) about by an action, behavior, or event, to occasion.
crisis: 1. A crucial or decisive point or situation; a turning point. 2. An unstable situation, in political, social, economic or military affairs, especially one involving an impending abrupt change.
critic: 1. A person who appraises the works of others. 2. A specialist in judging works of art.

child: 1. A person who has not yet reached adulthood, whether natural (puberty), cultural (initiation), or legal (majority) 2. (specifically) A female child, a girl.
coat: 1. An outer garment covering the upper torso and arms.Wp 2. A covering of material, such as paint.Wp
corn: 1. The main cereal plant grown for its grain in a given region, such as oats in parts of Scotland and Ireland, and wheat or barley in England and Wales. 2. Maize, a grain crop of the species Zea mays.
cow: 1. (properly) An adult female of the species Bos taurus, especially one that has calved. 2. (formerly inexact but now common) Any member of the species Bos taurus regardless of sex or age, including bulls and calves.
day: 1. Any period of 24 hours. 2. A period from midnight to the following midnight.
dog: 1. A mammal, Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris, that has been domesticated for thousands of years, of highly variable appearance due to human breeding. 2. Any member of the Family Canidae, including domestic dogs, wolves, coyotes, jackals, foxes, and their relatives (extant and extinct); canid.
doll: 1. A toy in the form of a human. 2. (sometimes offensive) An attractive young woman
door: 1. A portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle, consisting of a rigid plane movable on a hinge. Doors are frequently made of wood or metal. May have a handle to help open and close, a latch to hold the door closed and a lock that ensures the door cannot be opened without the key. 2. Any flap, etc. that opens like a door.
duck: 1. To quickly lower the head or body in order to prevent it from being struck by something. 2. To quickly lower (the head) in order to prevent it from being struck by something.
egg: 1. An approximately spherical or ellipsoidal body produced by birds, reptiles, insects and other animals, housing the embryo during its development. 2. The egg of a domestic fowl (especially a hen) or its contents, used as food.
eye: 1. An organ through which animals see (perceive surroundings via light). 2. The visual sense.
farm: 1. A place where agricultural and similar activities take place, especially the growing of crops or the raising of livestock. 2. A tract of land held on lease for the purpose of cultivation.
feet: 1. A biological structure found in many animals that is used for locomotion and that is frequently a separate organ at the terminal part of the leg. 2. Specifically, a human foot, which is found below the ankle and is used for standing and walking.
fire: 1. A (usually self-sustaining) chemical reaction involving the bonding of oxygen with carbon or other fuel, with the production of heat and the presence of flame or smouldering. 2. An instance of this chemical reaction, especially when intentionally created and maintained in a specific location to a useful end (such as a campfire or a hearth fire).
fish: 1. A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills. 2. Any animal (or any vertebrate) that lives exclusively in water.
floor: 1. The interior bottom or surface of a house or building; the supporting surface of a room. 2. Ground (surface of the Earth, as opposed to the sky or water or underground).
game: 1. A playful or competitive activity. 2. A video game.
girl: 1. A female child, adolescent, or a young woman. 2. A young female animal.
grass: 1. Any plant of the family Poaceae, characterized by leaves that arise from nodes in the stem and leaf bases that wrap around the stem, especially those grown as ground cover rather than for grain. 2. Various plants not in family Poaceae that resemble grasses.
hand: 1. The part of the forelimb below the forearm or wrist in a human, and the corresponding part in many other animals. 2. That which resembles, or to some extent performs the office of, a human hand.
head: 1. The part of the body of an animal or human which contains the brain, mouth and main sense organs. 2. The topmost, foremost, or leading part.
hill: 1. An elevated location smaller than a mountain. 2. A sloping road.
home: 1. A dwelling. 2. One’s native land; the place or country in which one dwells; the place where one’s ancestors dwell or dwelt.
horse: 1. Any of several animals related to Equus ferus caballus. 2. Equipment with legs.
house: 1. A structure built or serving as an abode of human beings. 2. The people who live in a house; a household.
kitty: 1. A kitten or young cat. 2. (sometimes capitalized) A pet name for a cat.
leg: 1. A limb or appendage that an animal uses for support or locomotion. 2. In humans, the lower limb extending from the groin to the ankle.
man: 1. An adult male human. 2. (collective) All human males collectively: mankind.
men: 1. An adult male human. 2. (collective) All human males collectively: mankind.
milk: 1. A white liquid produced by the mammary glands of female mammals to nourish their young. From certain animals, especially cows, it is also called dairy milk and is a common food for humans as a beverage or used to produce various dairy products such as butter, cheese, and yogurt. 2. A white (or whitish) liquid obtained from a vegetable source such as almonds, coconuts, oats, rice, and/or soy beans. Also called non-dairy milk.
money: 1. A legally or socially binding conceptual contract of entitlement to wealth, void of intrinsic value, payable for all debts and taxes, and regulated in supply. 2. A generally accepted means of exchange and measure of value.
morning: 1. The part of the day from dawn to noon. 2. The part of the day between midnight and noon.
mother: 1. A (human) female who has given birth to a baby 2. A human female who parents an adopted or fostered child
name: 1. Any nounal word or phrase which indicates a particular person, place, class, or thing. 2. Reputation.
nest: 1. A structure built by a bird as a place to incubate eggs and rear young. 2. A place used by another mammal, fish, amphibian or insect, for depositing eggs and hatching young.
night: 1. The period between sunset and sunrise, when a location faces far away from the sun, thus when the sky is dark. 2. (Astronomy) The period of darkness beginning at the end of evening astronomical twilight when the sun is 18 degrees below the horizon, and ending at the beginning of morning astronomical twilight.
paper: 1. A sheet material used for writing on or printing on (or as a non-waterproof container), usually made by draining cellulose fibres from a suspension in water. 2. A newspaper or anything used as such (such as a newsletter or listing magazine).
party: 1. A person or group of people constituting a particular side in a contract or legal action. 2. A person.
picture: 1. A representation of anything (as a person, a landscape, a building) upon canvas, paper, or other surface, by drawing, painting, printing, photography, etc. 2. An image; a representation as in the imagination.
pig: 1. Any of several intelligent mammalian species of the genus Sus, having cloven hooves, bristles and a nose adapted for digging; especially the domesticated animal Sus scrofa. 2. (specifically) A young swine, a piglet (contrasted with a hog, an adult swine).
rabbit: 1. A mammal of the family Leporidae, with long ears, long hind legs and a short, fluffy tail. 2. The meat from this animal.
rain: 1. Condensed water falling from a cloud. 2. Any matter moving or falling, usually through air, and especially if liquid or otherwise figuratively identifiable with raindrops.
ring: 1. (physical) A solid object in the shape of a circle. 2. (physical) A group of objects arranged in a circle.
robin: 1. Any of various passerine birds (about 100 species) of the families Muscicapidae, Turdidae and Petroicidae (formerly Eopsaltriidae), typically with a red breast. 2. A trimming in front of a dress.
school: 1. (collective) A group of fish or a group of marine mammals such as porpoises, dolphins, or whales. 2. A multitude.
seed: 1. A fertilized and ripened ovule, containing an embryonic plant. 2. Any small seed-like fruit.
sheep: 1. A woolly ruminant of the genus Ovis. 2. A timid, shy person who is easily led by others.
shoe: 1. A protective covering for the foot, with a bottom part composed of thick leather or plastic sole and often a thicker heel, and a softer upper part made of leather or synthetic material. Shoes generally do not extend above the ankle, as opposed to boots, which do. 2. A piece of metal designed to be attached to a horse's foot as a means of protection; a horseshoe.
sister: 1. A daughter of the same parents as another person; a female sibling. 2. A female member of a religious order; especially one devoted to more active service; (informally) a nun.
snow: 1. The frozen, crystalline state of water that falls as precipitation. 2. Any similar frozen form of a gas or liquid.
song: 1. A musical composition with lyrics for voice or voices, performed by singing. 2. (by extension) Any musical composition.
stick: 1. An elongated piece of wood or similar material, typically put to some use, for example as a wand or baton. 2. Any roughly cylindrical (or rectangular) unit of a substance.
street: 1. A paved part of road, usually in a village or a town. 2. A road as above but including the sidewalks (pavements) and buildings.
sun: 1. A star, especially when seen as the centre of any single solar system. 2. The light and warmth which is received from the sun.
table: 1. Furniture with a top surface to accommodate a variety of uses. 2. A two-dimensional presentation of data.
thing: 1. That which is considered to exist as a separate entity, object, quality or concept. 2. A word, symbol, sign, or other referent that can be used to refer to any entity.
time: 1. The inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events. 2. A duration of time.
top: 1. The highest or uppermost part of something. 2. A child’s spinning toy; a spinning top.
toy: 1. Something to play with, especially as intended for use by a child. 2. A thing of little importance or value; a trifle.
tree: 1. Fast growing function based on Kruskal's tree theorem. 2. A perennial woody plant, not exactly defined, but differentiated from a shrub by its larger size (typically over a few meters in height) or growth habit, usually having a single (or few) main axis or trunk unbranched for some distance above the ground and a head of branches and foliage.
watch: 1. A portable or wearable timepiece. 2. The act of guarding and observing someone or something.
water: 1. A substance (of molecular formula H₂O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid; it is present naturally as rain, and found in rivers, lakes and seas; its solid form is ice and its gaseous form is steam. 2. The aforementioned liquid, considered one of the Classical elements or basic elements of alchemy.
way: 1. (heading) To do with a place or places. 2. A method or manner of doing something; a mannerism.
wind: 1. Real or perceived movement of atmospheric air usually caused by convection or differences in air pressure. 2. Air artificially put in motion by any force or action.
window: 1. The inedible parts of a grain-producing plant. 2. Straw or hay cut up fine for the food of cattle.
wood: 1. The substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree. Used as a material for construction, to manufacture various items, etc. or as fuel. 2. The wood of a particular species of tree.
about: 1. Moving around; astir. 2. In existence; being in evidence; apparent.
bring: 1. (ditransitive) To transport toward somebody/somewhere. 2. To supply or contribute.
carry: 1. A manner of transporting or lifting something; the grip or position in which something is carried. 2. A tract of land over which boats or goods are carried between two bodies of navigable water; a portage.
clean: 1. Removal of dirt. 2. The first part of the event clean and jerk in which the weight is brought from the ground to the shoulders.
cut: 1. The act of cutting. 2. The result of cutting.
done: 1. (auxiliary) A syntactic marker. 2. To perform; to execute.
draw: 1. The result of a contest that neither side has won; a tie. 2. The procedure by which the result of a lottery is determined.
drink: 1. To consume (a liquid) through the mouth. 2. (metonymic) To consume the liquid contained within (a bottle, glass, etc.).
eight: 1. The digit/figure 8. 2. Any of the four cards in a normal deck with the value eight.
fall: 1. The act of moving to a lower position under the effect of gravity. 2. A reduction in quantity, pitch, etc.
far: 1. Distant; remote in space. 2. Remote in time.
full: 1. Containing the maximum possible amount that can fit in the space available. 2. Complete; with nothing omitted.
got: 1. (ditransitive) To obtain; to acquire. 2. To receive.
grow: 1. To become larger, to increase in magnitude. 2. To appear or sprout.
hold: 1. A grasp or grip. 2. An act or instance of holding.
hot: 1. (with up) To heat; to make or become hot. 2. (with up) To become lively or exciting.
hurt: 1. An emotional or psychological humiliation or bad experience. 2. A bodily injury causing pain; a wound or bruise.
if: 1. An uncertainty, possibility, condition, doubt etc. 2. Supposing that, assuming that, in the circumstances that; used to introduce a condition or choice.
keep: 1. The main tower of a castle or fortress, located within the castle walls. 2. The food or money required to keep someone alive and healthy; one's support, maintenance.
kind: 1. A type, race or category; a group of entities that have common characteristics such that they may be grouped together. 2. A makeshift or otherwise atypical specimen.
laugh: 1. An expression of mirth particular to the human species; the sound heard in laughing; laughter. 2. Something that provokes mirth or scorn.
light: 1. Visible electromagnetic radiation. The human eye can typically detect radiation (light) in the wavelength range of about 400 to 750 nanometers. Nearby shorter and longer wavelength ranges, although not visible, are commonly called ultraviolet and infrared light. 2. A source of illumination.
long: 1. A long vowel. 2. A long syllable.
myself: 1. (reflexive pronoun) Me, as direct or indirect object the speaker as the object of a verb or preposition, when the speaker is also the subject. 2. Personally, for my part; used in apposition to I, sometimes for simple emphasis and sometimes with implicit exclusion of any others performing the activity described.
never: 1. At no time; on no occasion; in no circumstance. 2. Not at any other time; not on any other occasion; not previously.
only: 1. An only child. 2. Alone in a category.
own: 1. Belonging to; possessed; proper to. Often marks a possessive determiner as reflexive, referring back to the subject of the clause or sentence. 2. Not shared
pick: 1. A tool used for digging; a pickaxe. 2. A tool for unlocking a lock without the original key; a lock pick, picklock.
seven: 1. The digit/figure 7 or an occurrence thereof. 2. A card bearing seven pips.
shall: 1. (modal, auxiliary verb, defective) Used before a verb to indicate the simple future tense in the first person singular or plural. 2. Used similarly to indicate determination or obligation in the second and third persons singular or plural.
show: 1. A play, dance, or other entertainment. 2. An exhibition of items.
six: 1. The digit or figure 6. 2. (by ellipsis of six o'clock) Rear, behind (rear side of something).
small: 1. Any part of something that is smaller or slimmer than the rest, now usually with anatomical reference to the back. 2. To make little or less.
start: 1. The beginning of an activity. 2. A sudden involuntary movement.
ten: 1. A set or group with ten elements. 2. A card in a given suit with a value of ten.
today: 1. A current day or date. 2. From 6am to 6pm on the current day.
together: 1. Coherent; well organized. 2. At the same time, in the same place; in close association or proximity.
try: 1. An attempt. 2. An act of tasting or sampling.
