warm: 1. Having a temperature slightly higher than usual, but still pleasant; mildly hot. 2. Caring and friendly, of relations to another person.
around: 1. (with the verb "to be") Present in the vicinity. 2. (with the verb "to be") Alive; existing.
because: 1. For the reason (that). 2. On account (of), for sake (of).
been: A flying insect, of the clade Anthophila within the hymenopteran superfamily Apoidea, known for its organised societies (though only a minority have them), for collecting pollen and (in some species) producing wax and honey.
before: 1. At an earlier time. 2. In advance.
best: 1. The supreme effort one can make, or has made. 2. One's best behavior.
both: 1. Each of the two, or of the two kinds. 2. Including both of (used with and).
buy: 1. Something which is bought; a purchase. 2. To obtain (something) in exchange for money or goods
call: 1. A telephone conversation. 2. A short visit, usually for social purposes.
cold: 1. (of a thing) Having a low temperature. 2. (of the weather) Causing the air to be cold.
does: 1. (auxiliary) A syntactic marker. 2. To perform; to execute.
fast: 1. A train that calls at only some stations it passes between its origin and destination, typically just the principal stations 2. Firmly or securely fixed in place; stable.
first: 1. The person or thing in the first position. 2. The first gear of an engine.
five: 1. The digit/figure 5. 2. A banknote with a denomination of five units of currency. See also fiver.
found: 1. To encounter or discover by accident; to happen upon. 2. To encounter or discover something being searched for; to locate.
gave: 1. (ditransitive) To move, shift, provide something abstract or concrete to someone or something or somewhere. 2. (ditransitive) To estimate or predict (a duration or probability) for (something).
goes: 1. The act of going. 2. A turn at something, or in something (e.g. a game).
green: 1. Having green as its color. 2. (of people) Sickly, unwell.
its: 1. One who is neither a he nor a she; a creature; a dehumanized being. 2. The person who chases and tries to catch the other players in the playground game of tag.
many: 1. A multitude; a great aggregate; a mass of people; the generality; the common herd. 2. A considerable number.
off: 1. (usually in phrases such as 'from the off', 'at the off', etc.) Beginning; starting point. 2. To kill.
or: 1. Connects at least two alternative words, phrases, clauses, sentences, etc. each of which could make a passage true. In English, this is the "inclusive or." The "exclusive or" is formed by "either [...] or". 2. An operator denoting the disjunction of two propositions or truth values. There are two forms, the inclusive or and the exclusive or.
pull: 1. An act of pulling (applying force) 2. An attractive force which causes motion towards the source
read: 1. A reading or an act of reading, especially an actor's part of a play. 2. (in combination) Something to be read; a written work.
right: 1. Straight, not bent. 2. Of an angle, having a size of 90 degrees, or one quarter of a complete rotation; the angle between two perpendicular lines.
sing: 1. A gathering at which people sing songs. 2. To produce musical or harmonious sounds with one’s voice.
sit: 1. Subsidence of the roof of a coal mine. 2. An event, usually lasting one full day or more, where the primary goal is to sit in meditation.
sleep: 1. To rest in a state of reduced consciousness. 2. (of a spinning top or yo-yo) To spin on its axis with no other perceptible motion.
tell: 1. A reflexive, often habitual behavior, especially one occurring in a context that often features attempts at deception by persons under psychological stress (such as a poker game or police interrogation), that reveals information that the person exhibiting the behavior is attempting to withhold. 2. That which is told; a tale or account.
these: The thing, item, etc. being indicated.
those: 1. (demonstrative) The thing, person, idea, quality, event, action or time indicated or understood from context, especially if more remote geographically, temporally or mentally than one designated as "this", or if expressing distinction. 2. The known (thing); used to refer to something just said.
upon: 1. Being the target of an action. 2. Physically above and in contact with.
us: 1. (personal) Me and at least one other person; the objective case of we. 2. (chiefly with give) Me.
use: 1. The act of using. 2. The act of consuming alcohol or narcotics.
very: 1. True, real, actual. 2. The same; identical.
wash: 1. The process or an instance of washing or being washed by water or other liquid. 2. A liquid used for washing.
which: 1. (interrogative) What one or ones (of those mentioned or implied). 2. The/Any ones that; whichever.
why: 1. Reason 2. For what cause, reason, or purpose (interrogative adverb).
wish: 1. A desire, hope, or longing for something or for something to happen. 2. An expression of such a desire, often connected with ideas of magic and supernatural power.
would: Something that would happen, or would be the case, under different circumstances; a potentiality.
write: 1. The act or style of writing. 2. The operation of storing data, as in memory or onto disk.
after: 1. Later; second (of two); next, following, subsequent 2. (where the frame of reference is within the ship) At or towards the stern of a ship.
again: 1. Another time; once more. 2. Over and above a factor of one.
any: 1. To even the slightest extent, at all. 2. Any thing(s) or person(s).
as: 1. To such an extent or degree; to the same extent or degree. 2. Considered to be, in relation to something else; in the relation (specified).
ask: 1. An act or instance of asking. 2. Something asked or asked for.
by: 1. A flying insect, of the clade Anthophila within the hymenopteran superfamily Apoidea, known for its organised societies (though only a minority have them), for collecting pollen and (in some species) producing wax and honey. 2. A contest, especially for spelling; see spelling bee.
could: 1. (auxiliary verb, defective) To know how to; to be able to. 2. (modal auxiliary verb, defective) May; to be permitted or enabled to.
fly: 1. Any insect of the order Diptera; characterized by having two wings (except for some wingless species), also called true flies. 2. (non-technical) Especially, any of the insects of the family Muscidae, such as the common housefly (other families of Diptera include mosquitoes and midges).
from: 1. Used to indicate source or provenance. 2. Originating at (a year, time, etc.)
give: 1. The amount of bending that something undergoes when a force is applied to it; a tendency to yield under pressure; resilence. 2. (ditransitive) To move, shift, provide something abstract or concrete to someone or something or somewhere.
going: 1. To move: 2. (chiefly of a machine) To work or function (properly); to move or perform (as required).
had: 1. To possess, own. 2. To hold, as something at someone's disposal.
has: 1. To possess, own. 2. To hold, as something at someone's disposal.
her: 1. A female person or animal. 2. The form of she used after a preposition or as the object of a verb; that woman, that ship, etc.
him: 1. Honorific alternative letter-case form of him, sometimes used when referring to God or another important figure who is understood from context. 2. A male person.
his: 1. Honorific alternative letter-case form of his, sometimes used when referring to God or another important figure who is understood from context. 2. That which belongs to him; the possessive case of he, used without a following noun.
how: 1. The means by which something is accomplished. 2. To what degree.
just: 1. Factually right, correct; factual. 2. Rationally right, correct.
know: 1. Knowledge; the state of knowing. 2. To perceive the truth or factuality of; to be certain of or that.
let: 1. The allowing of possession of a property etc. in exchange for rent. 2. To allow to, not to prevent (+ infinitive, but usually without to).
live: 1. To be alive; to have life. 2. To have permanent residence somewhere, to inhabit, to reside.
may: 1. To be strong; to have power (over). 2. (auxiliary) To be able; can.
of: 1. Expressing distance or motion. 2. Expressing separation.
old: 1. (with the, invariable plural only) People who are old; old beings; the older generation, taken as a group. 2. (in combination) One of a specified age.
once: 1. (frequency) One and only one time. 2. (temporal location) Formerly; during some period in the past.
open: 1. Not closed 2. Not physically drawn together, closed, folded or contracted; extended
over: 1. A set of six legal balls bowled. 2. Any surplus amount of money, goods delivered, etc.
put: 1. A right to sell something at a predetermined price. 2. A contract to sell a security at a set price on or before a certain date.
round: 1. So as to form a circle or trace a circular path, or approximation thereof. 2. So as to surround or be near.
some: 1. Of a measurement: approximately, roughly. 2. A certain number, at least two.
stop: 1. A (usually marked) place where buses, trams or trains halt to let passengers get on and off, usually smaller than a station. 2. An action of stopping; interruption of travel.
take: 1. The or an act of taking. 2. Something that is taken; a haul.
thank: An expression of appreciation; a thought.
them: 1. (plural) Those ones. 2. (singular) Him, her, or it; that one.
then: 1. Used in comparisons, to introduce the basis of comparison. 2. (obsolete outside dialectal, usually used with for) Because; for.
think: 1. An act of thinking; consideration (of something). 2. To ponder, to go over in one's head.
walk: 1. To move on the feet by alternately setting each foot (or pair or group of feet, in the case of animals with four or more feet) forward, with at least one foot on the ground at all times. Compare run. 2. To "walk free", i.e. to win, or avoid, a criminal court case, particularly when actually guilty.
were: 1. A man, a husband 2. A fine for slaying a man; weregild.
when: 1. The time at which something happens. 2. (interrogative) At what time? At which time? Upon which occasion or circumstance? Used to introduce direct or indirect questions about time.
all: 1. (with a possessive pronoun) Everything that one is capable of. 2. The totality of one's possessions.
are: An accepted (but deprecated and rarely used) SI unit of area equal to 100 square metres, or a former unit of approximately the same extent. Symbol: a.
at: 1. To reply to or talk to someone, either online or face-to-face. (from the practice of targeting a message or reply to someone online by writing @name) 2. The at sign (@).
ate: 1. To ingest; to be ingested. 2. To use up.
black: 1. The colour/color perceived in the absence of light, but also when no light is reflected, but rather absorbed. 2. A black dye or pigment.
brown: 1. A colour like that of chocolate or coffee. 2. One of the colour balls used in snooker, with a value of 4 points.
but: 1. An instance or example of using the word "but". 2. The outer room of a small two-room cottage.
came: 1. Used to indicate that the following event, period, or change in state occurred in the past, after a time of waiting, enduring, or anticipation 2. To move from further away to nearer to.
did: 1. (auxiliary) A syntactic marker. 2. To perform; to execute.
do: 1. A party, celebration, social function. 2. A hairdo.
eat: 1. Something to be eaten; a meal; a food item. 2. To ingest; to be ingested.
four: 1. The digit or figure 4; an occurrence thereof. 2. Anything measuring four units, as length.
have: 1. A wealthy or privileged person. 2. One who has some (contextually specified) thing.
he: 1. The game of tag, or it, in which the player attempting to catch the others is called "he". 2. The player attempting to catch the others in this game.
into: 1. To or towards the inside of. 2. To or towards the region of.
like: 1. (usually in the plural) Something that a person likes (prefers). 2. An individual vote showing support for, or approval of, something posted on the Internet.
must: 1. Something that is mandatory or required. 2. (modal auxiliary, defective) To do with certainty; indicates that the speaker is certain that the subject will have executed the predicate.
new: 1. Things that are new. 2. A kind of light beer.
no: 1. A negating expression; an answer that shows disagreement or disapproval 2. A vote not in favor, or opposing a proposition
now: 1. The present time. 2. (often with "the") The state of not paying attention to the future or the past.
on: 1. To switch on 2. In the state of being active, functioning or operating.
out: 1. A means of exit, escape, reprieve, etc. 2. A state in which a member of the batting team is removed from play due to the application of various rules of the game such as striking out, hitting a fly ball which is caught by the fielding team before bouncing, etc.
please: 1. To make happy or satisfy; to give pleasure to. 2. To desire; to will; to be pleased by.
pretty: 1. A pretty person; a term of address to a pretty person. 2. Something that is pretty.
ride: 1. An instance of riding. 2. A vehicle.
saw: 1. A tool with a toothed blade used for cutting hard substances, in particular wood or metal 2. A musical saw.
say: 1. A chance to speak; the right or power to influence or make a decision. 2. To pronounce.
she: 1. A female. 2. (personal) The female person or animal previously mentioned or implied.
so: 1. True, accurate. 2. In that state or manner; with that attribute. A proadjective that replaces the aforementioned adjective phrase.
soon: 1. Short in length of time from the present. 2. Early
that: 1. Something being indicated that is there; one of those. 2. (degree) To a given extent or degree.
there: 1. That place. 2. That status; that position.
they: 1. (the third-person plural) A group of people, animals, plants or objects previously mentioned. 2. (the third-person singular, sometimes proscribed) A single person, previously mentioned, especially if of unknown or non-binary gender, but typically not if previously named and identified as male or female.
this: 1. Something being indicated that is here; one of these. 2. Referring to the current context in a programming environment in C-like languages.
under: 1. Being lower; being beneath something. 2. Under anesthesia, especially general anesthesia; sedated.
want: 1. A desire, wish, longing. 2. (often followed by of) Lack, absence.
went: 1. To move: 2. (chiefly of a machine) To work or function (properly); to move or perform (as required).
what: 1. (Singlish) Used to contradict an underlying assumption held by the interlocutor. 2. Something; thing; stuff.
white: 1. The color/colour of snow or milk; the colour of light containing equal amounts of all visible wavelengths. 2. A person of European descent with light-coloured skin.
who: 1. A person under discussion; a question of which person. 2. (interrogative) What person or people; which person or people; asks for the identity of someone. (used in a direct or indirect question)
will: 1. (now uncommon or literary) To wish, desire (something). 2. (nowadays rare) To wish or desire (that something happen); to intend (that).
with: 1. Along, together with others, in a group, etc. 2. Against.
yes: 1. An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance. 2. A vote of support or in favor/favour of something.
big: 1. Someone or something that is large in stature 2. An important or powerful person; a celebrity; a big name.
blue: 1. The colour of the clear sky or the deep sea, between green and violet in the visible spectrum, and one of the primary additive colours for transmitted light; the colour obtained by subtracting red and green from white light using magenta and cyan filters; or any colour resembling this. 2. A blue dye or pigment.
can: 1. (auxiliary verb, defective) To know how to; to be able to. 2. (modal auxiliary verb, defective) May; to be permitted or enabled to.
down: 1. A negative aspect; a downer. 2. A grudge (on someone).
find: 1. Anything that is found (usually valuable), as objects on an archeological site or a person with talent. 2. The act of finding.
go: 1. The act of going. 2. A turn at something, or in something (e.g. a game).
help: 1. Action given to provide assistance; aid. 2. (usually uncountable) Something or someone which provides assistance with a task.
here: 1. (abstract) This place; this location. 2. (abstract) This time, the present situation.
in: 1. A position of power or influence, or a way to get it. 2. (chiefly in the plural) One who, or that which, is in; especially, one who is in office.
it: 1. One who is neither a he nor a she; a creature; a dehumanized being. 2. The person who chases and tries to catch the other players in the playground game of tag.
jump: 1. The act of jumping; a leap; a spring; a bound. 2. An effort; an attempt; a venture.
little: 1. A small amount. 2. Small in size.
make: 1. Brand or kind; model. 2. Manner or style of construction (style of how a thing is made); form.
me: 1. As the direct object of a verb. 2. Myself; as a reflexive direct object of a verb.
my: Used to express surprise, shock or amazement.
not: 1. A unary operation on logical values that changes true to false, and false to true. 2. Negates the meaning of the modified verb.
one: 1. The digit or figure 1. 2. The neutral element with respect to multiplication in a ring.
play: 1. Activity for amusement only, especially among the young. 2. Similar activity in young animals, as they explore their environment and learn new skills.
red: 1. Any of a range of colours having the longest wavelengths, 670 nm, of the visible spectrum; a primary additive colour for transmitted light: the colour obtained by subtracting green and blue from white light using magenta and yellow filters; the colour of blood, ripe strawberries, etc. 2. A revolutionary socialist or (most commonly) a Communist; (usually capitalized) a Bolshevik, a supporter of the Bolsheviks in the Russian Civil War.
run: 1. To run. 2. Act or instance of running, of moving rapidly using the feet.
see: 1. (stative) To perceive or detect with the eyes, or as if by sight. 2. To form a mental picture of.
the: 1. With a comparative or with more and a verb phrase, establishes a correlation with one or more other such comparatives. 2. With a comparative, and often with for it, indicates a result more like said comparative. This can be negated with none. See none the.
up: 1. The direction opposed to the pull of gravity. 2. A positive thing.
where: 1. The place in which something happens. 2. Interrogative adverb, used in either a direct or indirect question: at what place; to what place; what place.
goat: 1. A mammal, Capra aegagrus hircus, and similar species of the genus Capra. 2. A lecherous man.
elephant: 1. A mammal of the order Proboscidea, having a trunk, and two large ivory tusks jutting from the upper jaw. 2. Anything huge and ponderous.
catfish: 1. Any fish of the order Siluriformes, mainly found in fresh water, lacking scales, and having barbels like whiskers around the mouth 2. To fish for catfish
ant: 1. Any of various insects in the family Formicidae in the order Hymenoptera, typically living in large colonies composed almost entirely of flightless females. 2. A Web spider.
mosquito: 1. A small flying insect of the family Culicidae, the females of which bite humans and animals and suck blood, leaving an itching bump on the skin, and sometimes carrying diseases like malaria and yellow fever. 2. To fly close to the ground, seemingly without a course.
butterfly: 1. A flying insect of the order Lepidoptera, distinguished from moths by their diurnal activity and generally brighter colouring. 2. A use of surgical tape, cut into thin strips and placed across an open wound to hold it closed.
ram: 1. A male sheep, typically uncastrated 2. A battering ram; a heavy object used for breaking through doors.
camel: 1. A beast of burden, much used in desert areas, of the genus Camelus. 2. A light brownish color, like that of a camel (also called camel brown).
eagle: 1. Any of several large carnivorous and carrion-eating birds in the family Accipitridae, having a powerful hooked bill and keen vision. 2. A gold coin with a face value of ten dollars, formerly used in the United States.
turkey: 1. The guinea fowl (family Numididae). 2. A bird in the genus Meleagris with a fan-shaped tail and wattled neck, especially the wild turkey (Meleagris gallopavo, now domesticated).
monkey: 1. Any member of the clade Simiiformes not also of the clade Hominoidea containing humans and apes, from which they are usually, but not universally, distinguished by smaller size, a tail, and cheek pouches. 2. Any nonhuman simian primate, including apes.
rat: 1. A medium-sized rodent belonging to the genus Rattus. 2. Any of the numerous members of several rodent families (e.g. voles and mice) that resemble true rats in appearance, usually having a pointy snout, a long, bare tail, and body length greater than about 12 cm, or 5 inches.
bat: 1. Any of the flying mammals of the order Chiroptera, usually small and nocturnal, insectivorous or frugivorous. 2. An old woman.
snake: 1. A legless reptile of the sub-order Serpentes with a long, thin body and a fork-shaped tongue. 2. A treacherous person.
lizard: 1. Any reptile of the order Squamata that is not a snake, usually having four legs, external ear openings, movable eyelids and a long slender body and tail. 2. (chiefly in attributive use) Lizard skin, the skin of these reptiles.
toad: 1. An amphibian, a kind of frog (order Anura) with shorter hindlegs and a drier, wartier skin, many in family Bufonidae. 2. A contemptible or unpleasant person.
frog: 1. A small tailless amphibian of the order Anura that typically hops. 2. The part of a violin bow (or that of other similar string instruments such as the viola, cello and contrabass) located at the end held by the player, to which the horsehair is attached.
snail: 1. Any of very many animals (either hermaphroditic or nonhermaphroditic), of the class Gastropoda, having a coiled shell. 2. (by extension) A slow person; a sluggard.
spider: 1. Any of various eight-legged, predatory arthropods, of the order Araneae, most of which spin webs to catch prey. 2. A program which follows links on the World Wide Web in order to gather information.
bee: A flying insect, of the clade Anthophila within the hymenopteran superfamily Apoidea, known for its organised societies (though only a minority have them), for collecting pollen and (in some species) producing wax and honey.
crab: 1. A crustacean of the infraorder Brachyura, having five pairs of legs, the foremost of which are in the form of claws, and a carapace. 2. The meat of this crustacean, served as food; crabmeat
grasshopper: 1. A mostly herbivorous insect of the order Orthoptera, noted for its ability to jump long distances and for the habit of some species communicating by stridulation; they are related to but distinct from crickets. 2. A cocktail made with crème de menthe and optionally with crème de cacao.
cockroach: 1. A black or brown straight-winged insect of the order Blattodea. 2. A person or a member of a group of people regarded as undesirable and rapidly procreating.
add: 1. An act or instance of adding. 2. An additional enemy that joins a fight after the primary target.
age: 1. The whole duration of a being, whether animal, plant, or other kind, being alive. 2. The number of full years, months, days, hours, etc., that someone, or something, has been alive.
air: 1. The substance constituting earth's atmosphere, particularly: 2. (usually with the) The apparently open space above the ground which this substance fills, formerly thought to be limited by the firmament but now considered to be surrounded by the near vacuum of outer space.
arm: 1. The portion of the upper human appendage, from the shoulder to the wrist and sometimes including the hand. 2. The extended portion of the upper limb, from the shoulder to the elbow.
art: 1. The conscious production or arrangement of sounds, colours, forms, movements, or other elements in a manner that affects the senses and emotions, usually specifically the production of the beautiful in a graphic or plastic medium. 2. The creative and emotional expression of mental imagery, such as visual, auditory, social, etc.
ash: 1. The solid remains of a fire. 2. The nonaqueous remains of a material subjected to any complete oxidation process.
bad: 1. Error, mistake. 2. An item (or kind of item) of merchandise with negative value; an unwanted good.
bag: 1. A flexible container made of cloth, paper, plastic, etc. 2. A handbag
bar: 1. A solid, more or less rigid object of metal or wood with a uniform cross-section smaller than its length. 2. A solid metal object with uniform (round, square, hexagonal, octagonal or rectangular) cross-section; in the US its smallest dimension is 1/4 inch or greater, a piece of thinner material being called a strip.
beg: 1. The act of begging; an imploring request. 2. To request the help of someone, often in the form of money.
bet: 1. A wager, an agreement between two parties that a stake (usually money) will be paid by the loser to the winner (the winner being the one who correctly forecast the outcome of an event). 2. A degree of certainty.
bit: 1. A piece of metal placed in a horse's mouth and connected to the reins to direct the animal. 2. A rotary cutting tool fitted to a drill, used to bore holes.
bug: 1. An insect of the order Hemiptera (the “true bugs”). 2. Any of various species of marine or freshwater crustaceans; e.g. a Morton Bay bug, mudbug.
bus: 1. A motor vehicle for transporting large numbers of people along roads. 2. An electrical conductor or interface serving as a common connection for two or more circuits or components.
cab: 1. A taxi; a taxicab. 2. Compartment at the front of a truck or train for the driver
cap: 1. A close-fitting hat, either brimless or peaked. 2. A special hat to indicate rank, occupation, etc.
cot: 1. A simple bed, especially one for portable or temporary purposes. 2. A bed for infants or small children, with high, often slatted, often moveable sides.
cry: 1. A shedding of tears; the act of crying. 2. A shout or scream.
cub: 1. A young fox. 2. (by extension) The young of certain other animals, including the bear, wolf, lion and tiger.
cup: 1. A concave vessel for drinking from, usually made of opaque material (as opposed to a glass) and with a handle. 2. The contents of said vessel; a cupful.
dad: 1. A father, a male parent. 2. (familiar) Used to address one's father
den: 1. A small cavern or hollow place in the side of a hill, or among rocks; especially, a cave used by a wild animal for shelter or concealment. 2. A squalid or wretched place; a haunt.
dig: 1. An archeological or paleontological investigation, or the site where such an investigation is taking place. 2. A plodding and laborious student.
dim: 1. Dimness. 2. To make something less bright.
dip: 1. A lower section of a road or geological feature. 2. Inclination downward; direction below a horizontal line; slope; pitch.
dot: 1. A small, round spot. 2. (grammar) A punctuation mark used to indicate the end of a sentence or an abbreviated part of a word; a full stop; a period.
dry: 1. The process by which something is dried. 2. A prohibitionist (of alcoholic beverages).
ear: 1. The organ of hearing, consisting of the pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, malleus, incus, stapes and cochlea. 2. The external part of the organ of hearing, the auricle.
elf: 1. A luminous spirit presiding over nature and fertility and dwelling in the world of Álfheim (Elfland). Compare angel, nymph, fairy. 2. Any from a race of mythical, supernatural beings resembling but seen as distinct from human beings. They are usually delicate-featured and skilled in magic or spellcrafting; sometimes depicted as clashing with dwarves, especially in modern fantasy literature.
elk: Any of various large species of deer such as the red deer, moose or wapiti (see usage notes).
elm: 1. A tree of the genus Ulmus of the family Ulmaceae, large deciduous trees with alternate stipulate leaves and small apetalous flowers. 2. (usually attributive) Wood from an elm tree.
end: 1. The terminal point of something in space or time. 2. (by extension) The cessation of an effort, activity, state, or motion.
fan: 1. A hand-held device consisting of concertinaed material, or slats of material, gathered together at one end, that may be opened out into the shape of a sector of a circle and waved back and forth in order to move air towards oneself and cool oneself. 2. An electrical or mechanical device for moving air, used for cooling people, machinery, etc.
fat: 1. A specialized animal tissue with a high oil content, used for long-term storage of energy. 2. A refined substance chemically resembling the oils in animal fat.
fee: 1. (feudal law) A right to the use of a superior's land, as a stipend for services to be performed; also, the land so held; a fief. 2. An inheritable estate in land held of a feudal lord on condition of the performing of certain services.
fig: 1. A fruit-bearing tree or shrub of the genus Ficus that is native mainly to the tropics. 2. The fruit of the fig tree, pear-shaped and containing many small seeds.
fin: 1. One of the appendages of a fish, used to propel itself and to manoeuvre/maneuver. 2. A similar appendage of a cetacean or other marine animal.
fit: 1. The degree to which something fits. 2. Conformity of elements one to another.
fog: 1. A thick cloud that forms near the ground; the obscurity of such a cloud. 2. A mist or film clouding a surface.
fox: 1. A red fox, small carnivore (Vulpes vulpes), related to dogs and wolves, with red or silver fur and a bushy tail. 2. Any of numerous species of small wild canids resembling the red fox. In the taxonomy they form the tribe Vulpini within the family Canidae, consisting of nine genera (see the Wikipedia article on the fox).
fry: 1. (usually in the plural, fries) A fried strip of potato. 2. A meal of fried sausages, bacon, eggs, etc.
fun: 1. Amusement, enjoyment or pleasure 2. Playful, often noisy, activity.
gap: 1. An opening in anything made by breaking or parting. 2. An opening allowing passage or entrance.
gas: 1. Matter in a state intermediate between liquid and plasma that can be contained only if it is fully surrounded by a solid (or in a bubble of liquid) (or held together by gravitational pull); it can condense into a liquid, or can (rarely) become a solid directly. 2. A chemical element or compound in such a state.
gem: 1. A precious stone, usually of substantial monetary value or prized for its beauty or shine. 2. Any precious or highly valued thing or person.
gig: 1. A performing engagement by a musical group; or, generally, any job or role, especially for a musician or performer. 2. (by extension) Any job; especially one that is temporary; or alternately, one that is very desirable.
gum: 1. (often in the plural) The flesh around the teeth. 2. To chew, especially of a toothless person or animal.
gun: 1. A device for projecting a hard object very forcefully; a firearm or cannon. 2. A device operated by a trigger and acting in a manner similar to a firearm.
gut: 1. The alimentary canal, especially the intestine. 2. The abdomen of a person, especially one that is enlarged
gym: 1. A sports facility specialized for lifting weights and exercise. 2. Physical education class
ham: 1. The region back of the knee joint; the popliteal space; the hock. 2. A thigh and buttock of an animal slaughtered for meat.
hat: 1. A covering for the head, often in the approximate form of a cone or a cylinder closed at its top end, and sometimes having a brim and other decoration. 2. A particular role or capacity that a person might fill.
hay: 1. Grass cut and dried for use as animal fodder. 2. Any mix of green leafy plants used for fodder.
hen: 1. A female chicken (Gallus gallus), particularly a sexually mature one kept for its eggs. 2. A female of other bird species, particularly a sexually mature female fowl.
hid: 1. To put (something) in a place where it will be harder to discover or out of sight. 2. To put oneself in a place where one will be harder to find or out of sight.
hip: 1. The outward-projecting parts of the pelvis and top of the femur and the overlying tissue. 2. The inclined external angle formed by the intersection of two sloping roof planes.
hit: 1. A blow; a punch; a striking against; the collision of one body against another; the stroke that touches anything. 2. Something very successful, such as a song, film, or video game, that receives widespread recognition and acclaim.
hog: 1. Any animal belonging to the Suidae family of mammals, especially the pig, the warthog, and the boar. 2. (specifically) An adult swine (contrasted with a pig, a young swine).
hop: 1. A short jump. 2. A jump on one leg.
hug: 1. A close embrace, especially when charged with such an emotion as represented by: affection, joy, relief, lust, anger, agression, compassion, and the like, as opposed to being characterized by formality, equivocation or ambivalence (a half-embrace or "little hug"). 2. A particular grip in wrestling.
hum: 1. Indicating thinking or pondering. 2. A demand for an answer to a question.
hut: 1. A small, simple one-storey dwelling or shelter, often with just one room, and generally built of readily available local materials. 2. A small wooden shed.
ice: 1. Water in frozen (solid) form. 2. Any frozen volatile chemical, such as ammonia or carbon dioxide.
ill: 1. (often pluralized) Trouble; distress; misfortune; adversity. 2. Harm or injury.
ink: 1. A pigment (or dye)-based fluid used for writing, printing etc. 2. A particular type, color or container of this fluid.
inn: 1. Any establishment where travellers can procure lodging, food, and drink. 2. A tavern.
jam: 1. A sweet mixture of fruit boiled with sugar and allowed to congeal. Often spread on bread or toast or used in jam tarts. 2. A difficult situation.
jar: 1. An earthenware container, either with two or no handles, for holding oil, water, wine, etc., or used for burial. 2. A small, approximately cylindrical container, normally made of clay or glass, for holding fruit, preserves, etc., or for ornamental purposes.
jaw: 1. One of the bones, usually bearing teeth, which form the framework of the mouth. 2. The part of the face below the mouth.
jet: 1. A collimated stream, spurt or flow of liquid or gas from a pressurized container, an engine, etc. 2. A spout or nozzle for creating a jet of fluid.
job: 1. A task. 2. An economic role for which a person is paid.
jog: 1. An energetic trot, slower than a run, often used as a form of exercise. 2. A sudden push or nudge.
joy: 1. A feeling of extreme happiness or cheerfulness, especially related to the acquisition or expectation of something good. 2. Anything that causes such a feeling.
jug: 1. A serving vessel or container, typically circular in cross-section and typically higher than it is wide, with a relatively small mouth or spout, an ear handle and often a stopper or top. 2. The amount that a jug can hold.
jut: 1. Something that sticks out. 2. To stick out.
keg: 1. A round, traditionally wooden container of lesser capacity than a barrel, often used to store beer. 2. To store in a keg.
key: 1. An object designed to open and close a lock. 2. An object designed to fit between two other objects (such as a shaft and a wheel) in a mechanism and maintain their relative orientation.
kid: 1. A young goat. 2. Of a female goat, the state of being pregnant: in kid.
kin: 1. Race; family; breed; kind. 2. Persons of the same race or family; kindred.
kit: 1. A circular wooden vessel, made of hooped staves. 2. A kind of basket made especially from straw of rushes, especially for holding fish; by extension, the contents of such a basket or similar container, used as a measure of weight.
lab: 1. A laboratory. 2. (chiefly in the plural) Laboratory experiment, test, investigation or result.
lag: 1. A gap, a delay; an interval created by something not keeping up; a latency. 2. Delay; latency.
lap: 1. The loose part of a coat; the lower part of a garment that plays loosely; a skirt; an apron. 2. An edge; a border; a hem, as of cloth.
law: 1. The body of binding rules and regulations, customs and standards established in a community by its legislative and judicial authorities. 2. A binding regulation or custom established in a community in this way.
lay: 1. Arrangement or relationship; layout. 2. A share of the profits in a business.
lid: 1. A thin skin membrane that covers and moves over an eye. 2. The top or cover of a container.
lip: 1. Either of the two fleshy protrusions around the opening of the mouth. 2. A part of the body that resembles a lip, such as the edge of a wound or the labia.
log: 1. The trunk of a dead tree, cleared of branches. 2. Any bulky piece as cut from the above, used as timber, fuel etc.
lot: 1. A large quantity or number; a great deal. 2. A separate portion; a number of things taken collectively.
mad: 1. To be or become mad. 2. To madden, to anger, to frustrate.
map: 1. A visual representation of an area, whether real or imaginary. 2. A graphical representation of the relationships between objects, components or themes.
mat: 1. A flat piece of coarse material used for wiping one’s feet, or as a decorative or protective floor covering. 2. A small flat piece of material used to protect a surface from anything hot or rough; a coaster.
met: 1. To make contact (with) while in proximity. 2. (Of groups) To come together.
mix: 1. To stir together. 2. To combine (items from two or more sources normally kept separate).
mob: 1. A large or disorderly group of people; especially one bent on riotous or destructive action. 2. A group of animals such as horses or cattle.
mom: 1. (familiar) mother. 2. An adult female owner of a pet.
mop: 1. An implement for washing floors, or the like, made of a piece of cloth, or a collection of thrums, or coarse yarn, fastened to a handle. 2. A wash with a mop; the act of mopping
mud: 1. A mixture of water and soil or fine grained sediment. 2. A plaster-like mixture used to texture or smooth drywall.
mug: 1. A large cup for hot liquids, usually having a handle and used without a saucer. 2. The face, often used deprecatingly.
nap: 1. A short period of sleep, especially one during the day. 2. To have a nap; to sleep for a short period of time, especially during the day.
nod: 1. An instance of inclining the head up and down, as to indicate agreement, or as a cursory greeting. 2. A reference or allusion to something.
nut: 1. A hard-shelled seed. 2. A piece of metal, usually square or hexagonal in shape, with a hole through it having machined internal threads, intended to be screwed onto a bolt or other threaded shaft.
oak: 1. A deciduous tree with distinctive deeply lobed leaves, acorns, and notably strong wood, typically of England and northeastern North America, included in genus Quercus. 2. The wood of the oak.
oat: 1. Widely cultivated cereal grass, typically Avena sativa. 2. Any of the numerous species, varieties, or cultivars of any of several similar grain plants in genus Avena.
odd: 1. (diminutive) An odd number. 2. Something left over, not forming part of a set.
oil: 1. Liquid fat. 2. Petroleum-based liquid used as fuel or lubricant.
pad: 1. A flattened mass of anything soft, to sit or lie on. 2. A cushion used as a saddle without a tree or frame.
pal: 1. A friend, buddy, mate, cobber; someone to hang around with. 2. An informal term of address, often used ironically in a hostile way.
pan: 1. A wide, flat receptacle used around the house, especially for cooking. 2. The contents of such a receptacle.
paw: 1. The soft foot of a mammal or other animal, generally a quadruped, that has claws or nails; comparable to a human hand or foot. 2. A hand.
pay: 1. Money given in return for work; salary or wages. 2. To give money or other compensation to in exchange for goods or services.
peg: 1. A cylindrical wooden or metal object used to fasten or as a bearing between objects. 2. Measurement between the pegs: after killing an animal hunters used the distance between a peg near the animal's nose and one near the end of its tail to measure its body length.
pen: 1. An enclosure (enclosed area) used to contain domesticated animals, especially sheep or cattle. 2. A prison cell.
pet: 1. An animal kept as a companion. 2. (by extension) Something kept as a companion, including inanimate objects. (pet rock, pet plant, etc.)
pie: 1. A type of pastry that consists of an outer crust and a filling. 2. Any of various other, non-pastry dishes that maintain the general concept of a shell with a filling.
pin: 1. A needle without an eye (usually) made of drawn-out steel wire with one end sharpened and the other flattened or rounded into a head, used for fastening. 2. A small nail with a head and a sharp point.
pit: 1. A hole in the ground. 2. An area at a racetrack used for refueling and repairing the vehicles during a race.
pod: 1. A seed case for legumes (e.g. peas, beans, peppers); a seedpod. 2. A small vehicle, especially used in emergency situations.
pop: 1. A loud, sharp sound as of a cork coming out of a bottle. 2. (Midwest US) An effervescent or fizzy drink, most frequently nonalcoholic; soda pop.
pot: 1. A flat-bottomed vessel (usually metal) used for cooking food. 2. Various similar open-topped vessels, particularly
pub: 1. A public house where beverages, primarily alcoholic, may be bought and consumed, also providing food and sometimes entertainment such as live music or television. 2. A public server.
pug: 1. A small dog of an ancient breed originating in China, having a snub nose, wrinkled face, squarish body, short smooth hair, and curled tail. 2. A bargeman.
pup: 1. A young dog, wolf, fox, seal, or shark, or the young of certain other animals. 2. A young, inexperienced person.
rag: 1. (in the plural) Tattered clothes. 2. A piece of old cloth; a tattered piece of cloth; a shred, a tatter.
raw: 1. (sugar refining, sugar trade) An unprocessed sugar; a batch of such. 2. A galled place; an inveterate sore.
ray: 1. A beam of light or radiation. 2. A rib-like reinforcement of bone or cartilage in a fish's fin.
rib: 1. Any of a series of long curved bones occurring in 12 pairs in humans and other animals and extending from the spine to or toward the sternum 2. A part or piece, similar to a rib, and serving to shape or support something
rim: 1. An edge around something, especially when circular. 2. A wheelrim.
rip: 1. A tear (in paper, etc.). 2. A type of tide or current.
rod: 1. A straight, round stick, shaft, bar, cane, or staff. 2. A longitudinal pole used for forming part of a framework such as an awning or tent.
rot: 1. The process of becoming rotten; putrefaction. 2. Decaying matter.
row: 1. A line of objects, often regularly spaced, such as seats in a theatre, vegetable plants in a garden etc. 2. A line of entries in a table, etc., going from left to right, as opposed to a column going from top to bottom.
rub: 1. An act of rubbing. 2. A difficulty or problem.
rug: 1. A partial covering for a floor. 2. A (usually thick) piece of fabric used for warmth (especially on a bed); a blanket.
rum: 1. A distilled spirit derived from fermented cane sugar and molasses. 2. A serving of rum.
rut: 1. Sexual desire or oestrus of cattle, and various other mammals. 2. The noise made by deer during sexual excitement.
sad: 1. To make melancholy; to sadden or grieve (someone). 2. (heading) Emotionally negative.
sap: 1. The juice of plants of any kind, especially the ascending and descending juices or circulating fluid essential to nutrition. 2. The sapwood, or alburnum, of a tree.
sea: 1. A large body of salt water. 2. A lake, especially if large or if salty or brackish.
set: 1. To put (something) down, to rest. 2. To attach or affix (something) to something else, or in or upon a certain place.
sew: 1. To use a needle to pass thread repeatedly through (pieces of fabric) in order to join them together. 2. To use a needle to pass thread repeatedly through pieces of fabric in order to join them together.
sin: 1. A violation of God's will or religious law. 2. A misdeed.
sip: 1. To ooze or pass slowly through pores or other small openings, and in overly small quantities; said of liquids, etc. 2. To enter or penetrate slowly; to spread or diffuse.
sir: 1. A man of a higher rank or position. 2. A respectful term of address to a man of higher rank or position, particularly:
ski: 1. One of a pair of long flat runners designed for gliding over snow or water 2. One of a pair of long flat runners under some flying machines, used for landing
sky: 1. The atmosphere above a given point, especially as visible from the ground during the day. 2. The part of the sky which can be seen from a specific place or at a specific time; its condition, climate etc.
sob: 1. A cry with a short, sudden expulsion of breath. 2. Sound of sob
son: 1. One's male offspring. 2. A male adopted person in relation to his adoptive parents.
sow: 1. A female pig. 2. A female bear, she-bear.
spy: 1. A person who secretly watches and examines the actions of other individuals or organizations and gathers information on them (usually to gain an advantage). 2. To act as a spy.
sub: 1. A submarine. 2. A submarine sandwich: a sandwich made on a long bun.
sum: 1. A quantity obtained by addition or aggregation. 2. (often plural) An arithmetic computation, especially one posed to a student as an exercise (not necessarily limited to addition).
tab: 1. A small flap or strip of material attached to something, for holding, manipulation, identification, opening etc. 2. An ear.
tag: 1. A small label. 2. A children's chasing game in which one player (known as "it") attempts to touch another, who then becomes "it".
tan: 1. A yellowish-brown colour. 2. A darkening of the skin resulting from exposure to sunlight or similar light sources.
tap: 1. A tapering cylindrical pin or peg used to stop the vent in a cask. 2. A device used to dispense liquids.
tar: 1. (usually uncountable) A black, oily, sticky, viscous substance, consisting mainly of hydrocarbons derived from organic materials such as wood, peat, or coal. 2. Coal tar.
tax: 1. Money paid to the government other than for transaction-specific goods and services. 2. A burdensome demand.
tea: 1. A drug smoked or ingested for euphoric effect, cannabis. 2. The hemp plant itself, Cannabis sativa.
tie: 1. A knot; a fastening. 2. A knot of hair, as at the back of a wig.
tin: 1. A malleable, ductile, metallic element, resistant to corrosion, with atomic number 50 and symbol Sn. 2. An airtight container, made of tin or another metal, used to preserve food.
tip: 1. The tip of the external ear. 2. A small earpiece or earplug.
toe: 1. Each of the five digits on the end of the foot. 2. An equivalent part in an animal.
tub: 1. A flat-bottomed vessel, of width similar to or greater than its height, used for storing or packing things, or for washing things in. 2. The contents or capacity of such a vessel.
tug: 1. A sudden powerful pull. 2. A tugboat.
van: 1. A covered vehicle used for carrying goods or people, usually roughly cuboid in shape, longer and higher than a car but smaller than a truck/lorry. 2. An enclosed railway vehicle for transport of goods.
vat: 1. A large tub, such as is used for making wine or for tanning. 2. A square, hollow place on the back of a calcining furnace, where tin ore is laid to dry.
vow: 1. A solemn promise to perform some act, or behave in a specified manner, especially a promise to live and act in accordance with the rules of a religious order. 2. A declaration or assertion.
wag: 1. An oscillating movement. 2. A witty person.
war: 1. Organized, large-scale, armed conflict between countries or between national, ethnic, or other sizeable groups, usually involving the engagement of military forces. 2. A particular conflict of this kind.
web: 1. The World Wide Web. 2. The silken structure which a spider builds using silk secreted from the spinnerets at the caudal tip of its abdomen; a spiderweb.
wig: 1. A head of real or synthetic hair worn on the head to disguise baldness, for cultural or religious reasons, for fashion, or by actors to help them better resemble the character they are portraying. 2. (among fishermen) An old seal.
win: 1. To conquer, defeat. 2. To reach some destination or object, despite difficulty or toil (now usually intransitive, with preposition or locative adverb).
wok: 1. A large, oriental, round-bottomed cooking pan. 2. To prepare oriental cuisine using a wok.
won: 1. To conquer, defeat. 2. To reach some destination or object, despite difficulty or toil (now usually intransitive, with preposition or locative adverb).
wow: 1. Anything exceptionally surprising, unbelievable, outstanding, etc. 2. To amaze or awe.
yak: An ox-like mammal native to the Himalayas, Mongolia, Burma, and Tibet with dark, long, and silky hair, a horse-like tail, and a full, bushy mane.
yam: 1. Any climbing vine of the genus Dioscorea in the Eastern and Western hemispheres, usually cultivated. 2. The edible, starchy, tuberous root of that plant, a tropical staple food.
yap: 1. The high-pitched bark of a small dog, or similar. 2. Casual talk; chatter.
yip: 1. A sharp, high-pitched bark 2. To bark with a sharp, high-pitched voice
yum: 1. Delicious. 2. Yellowdog Updater, Modified, a popular package manager in Linux
zag: 1. One of a series of sharp turns or reversals. 2. Twist in a storyline
zip: 1. A twist or fold. 2. Any of the folds on the surface of the brain.
zoo: 1. A park where live animals are exhibited. 2. Any place that is wild, crowded, or chaotic.
bake: 1. The act of cooking food by baking. 2. Any of various baked dishes resembling casserole.
bare: 1. (‘the bare’) The surface, the (bare) skin. 2. Surface; body; substance.
bark: 1. The short, loud, explosive sound uttered by a dog, a fox, and some other animals. 2. An abrupt loud vocal utterance.
base: 1. Something from which other things extend; a foundation. 2. The starting point of a logical deduction or thought; basis.
bean: 1. A reusable software component written in Java. 2. Any plant of several genera of the taxonomic family Fabaceae that produces large edible seeds or edible seedpods.
beat: 1. A stroke; a blow. 2. A pulsation or throb.
beef: 1. The meat from a cow, bull or other bovine. 2. (plural: beefs) A grudge; dislike (of something or someone); lack of faith or trust (in something or someone); a reason for a dislike or grudge. (often + with)
beep: 1. The sound produced by the horn of a car, or any similar sound. 2. A short, electronically produced tone.
belt: 1. A band worn around the waist to hold clothing to one's body (usually pants), hold weapons (such as a gun or sword), or serve as a decorative piece of clothing. 2. A band used as a restraint for safety purposes, such as a seat belt.
bend: 1. A curve. 2. Any of the various knots which join the ends of two lines.
bike: 1. A vehicle that has two wheels, one behind the other, a steering handle, and a saddle seat or seats and is usually propelled by the action of a rider’s feet upon pedals. 2. A traveling block used on a cable in skidding logs.
bite: 1. The act of biting. 2. The wound left behind after having been bitten.
blow: 1. A strong wind. 2. A chance to catch one’s breath.
bone: 1. A composite material consisting largely of calcium phosphate and collagen and making up the skeleton of most vertebrates. 2. Any of the components of an endoskeleton, made of bone.
book: 1. A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc. 2. A long work fit for publication, typically prose, such as a novel or textbook, and typically published as such a bound collection of sheets, but now sometimes electronically as an e-book.
boot: 1. A heavy shoe that covers part of the leg. 2. A blow with the foot; a kick.
boss: 1. A person who oversees and directs the work of others; a supervisor. 2. A person in charge of a business or company.
bowl: 1. A roughly hemispherical container used to hold, mix or present food, such as salad, fruit or soup, or other items. 2. As much as is held by a bowl.
bump: 1. A light blow or jolting collision. 2. The sound of such a collision.
burn: 1. A physical injury caused by heat, cold, electricity, radiation or caustic chemicals. 2. A sensation resembling such an injury.
bush: 1. A woody plant distinguished from a tree by its multiple stems and lower height, being usually less than six metres tall; a horticultural rather than strictly botanical category. 2. A shrub cut off, or a shrublike branch of a tree.
busy: 1. A police officer. 2. To make somebody busy or active; to occupy.
camp: 1. An outdoor place acting as temporary accommodation in tents or other temporary structures. 2. An organised event, often taking place in tents or temporary accommodation.
card: 1. A playing card. 2. (in the plural) Any game using playing cards; a card game.
care: 1. Grief, sorrow. 2. Close attention; concern; responsibility.
cash: 1. Money in the form of notes/bills and coins, as opposed to cheques/checks or electronic transactions. 2. Liquid assets, money that can be traded quickly, as distinct from assets that are invested and cannot be easily exchanged.
cave: 1. A large, naturally-occurring cavity formed underground or in the face of a cliff or a hillside. 2. A hole, depression, or gap in earth or rock, whether natural or man-made.
chat: 1. Informal conversation. 2. A conversation to stop an argument or settle situations.
chew: 1. The act of chewing; mastication with the mouth. 2. Level of chewiness.
chin: 1. The bottom of a face, (specifically) the typically jutting jawline below the mouth. 2. Talk.
chip: 1. A small piece broken from a larger piece of solid material. 2. A damaged area of a surface where a small piece has been broken off.
chop: 1. A cut of meat, often containing a section of a rib. 2. A blow with an axe, cleaver, or similar utensil.
clam: 1. A bivalve mollusk of many kinds, especially those that are edible; for example the soft-shell clam (Mya arenaria), the hard clam (Mercenaria mercenaria), the sea clam or hen clam (Spisula solidissima), and other species. The name is said to have been given originally to the Tridacna gigas, a huge East Indian bivalve. 2. Strong pincers or forceps.
clap: 1. The act of striking the palms of the hands, or any two surfaces, together. 2. The explosive sound of thunder.
claw: 1. A curved, pointed horny nail on each digit of the foot of a mammal, reptile, or bird. 2. A foot equipped with such.
clay: 1. A mineral substance made up of small crystals of silica and alumina, that is ductile when moist; the material of pre-fired ceramics. 2. An earth material with ductile qualities.
club: 1. An association of members joining together for some common purpose, especially sports or recreation. 2. A heavy stick intended for use as a weapon or plaything.
clue: 1. A strand of yarn etc. as used to guide one through a labyrinth; something which points the way, a guide. 2. Information which may lead one to a certain point or conclusion.
coal: 1. A black rock formed from prehistoric plant remains, composed largely of carbon and burned as a fuel. 2. A piece of coal used for burning (this use is less common in American English)
coin: 1. (money) A piece of currency, usually metallic and in the shape of a disc, but sometimes polygonal, or with a hole in the middle. 2. A token used in a special establishment like a casino.
cook: 1. A person who prepares food. 2. The head cook of a manor house
cool: 1. A moderate or refreshing state of cold; moderate temperature of the air between hot and cold; coolness. 2. A calm temperament.
copy: 1. The result of copying; an identical duplicate of an original. 2. An imitation, sometimes of inferior quality.
cord: 1. A harmonic set of three or more notes that is heard as if sounding simultaneously. 2. A straight line between two points of a curve.
core: 1. The central part of fruit, containing the kernels or seeds. 2. The heart or inner part of a physical thing
cork: 1. The bark of the cork oak, which is very light and porous and used for making bottle stoppers, flotation devices, and insulation material. 2. A bottle stopper made from this or any other material.
cost: 1. To incur a charge of; to require payment of a (specified) price. 2. To cause something to be lost; to cause the expenditure or relinquishment of.
crew: 1. To make the shrill sound characteristic of a rooster; to make a sound in this manner, either in gaiety, joy, pleasure, or defiance. 2. To shout in exultation or defiance; to brag.
crop: 1. A plant, especially a cereal, grown to be harvested as food, livestock fodder or fuel or for any other economic purpose. 2. The natural production for a specific year, particularly of plants.
crow: 1. A bird, usually black, of the genus Corvus, having a strong conical beak, with projecting bristles; it has a harsh, croaking call. 2. The cry of the rooster.
cube: 1. A regular polyhedron having six identical square faces. 2. Any object more or less in the form of a cube.
cure: 1. A method, device or medication that restores good health. 2. Act of healing or state of being healed; restoration to health after a disease, or to soundness after injury.
cute: 1. Possessing physical features, behaviors, personality traits or other properties that are mainly attributed to infants and small or cuddly animals; e.g. fair, dainty, round, and soft physical features, disproportionately large eyes and head, playfulness, fragility, helplessness, curiosity or shyness, innocence, affectionate behavior. 2. Generally, attractive or pleasing, especially in a youthful, dainty, quaint or fun-spirited way.
damp: 1. Moisture; humidity; dampness. 2. Fog; fogginess; vapor.
dark: 1. Having an absolute or (more often) relative lack of light. 2. (of colour) Dull or deeper in hue; not bright or light.
dart: 1. A pointed missile weapon, intended to be thrown by the hand, for example a short lance or javelin 2. Any sharp-pointed missile weapon, such as an arrow.
dash: 1. Any of the following symbols: ‒ (figure dash), – (en dash), — (em dash), or ― (horizontal bar). 2. (by extension) The longer of the two symbols of Morse code.
date: 1. The fruit of the date palm, Phoenix dactylifera, somewhat in the shape of an olive, containing a soft, sweet pulp and enclosing a hard kernel. 2. The date palm.
dawn: 1. The morning twilight period immediately before sunrise. 2. The rising of the sun.
deaf: 1. A deaf person. 2. (with "the") Those who are deaf, taken as a group.
deal: 1. A division, a portion, a share. 2. (often followed by of) An indefinite quantity or amount; a lot (now usually qualified by great or good).
dear: 1. A very kind, loving person. 2. A beloved person.
deck: 1. Any raised flat surface that can be walked on: a balcony; a porch; a raised patio; a flat rooftop. 2. The floorlike covering of the horizontal sections, or compartments, of a ship. Small vessels have only one deck; larger ships have two or three decks.
deep: 1. (with "the") The deep part of a lake, sea, etc. 2. (with "the") A silent time; quiet isolation.
deer: 1. A ruminant mammal with antlers and hooves of the family Cervidae, or one of several similar animals from related families of the order Artiodactyla 2. (in particular) one of the smaller animals of this family, distinguished from a moose or elk
desk: 1. A table, frame, or case, in past centuries usually with a sloping top but now usually with a flat top, for the use of writers and readers. It often has a drawer or repository underneath. 2. A reading table or lectern to support the book from which the liturgical service is read, differing from the pulpit from which the sermon is preached; also (especially in the United States), a pulpit. Hence, used symbolically for the clerical profession.
dial: 1. A graduated, circular scale over which a needle moves to show a measurement (such as speed). 2. A clock face.
dice: 1. Gaming with one or more dice. 2. A die.
diet: 1. The food and beverage a person or animal consumes. 2. A controlled regimen of food and drink, as to gain or lose weight or otherwise influence health.
dirt: 1. Soil or earth. 2. A stain or spot (on clothes etc); any foreign substance that worsens appearance.
dish: 1. A vessel such as a plate for holding or serving food, often flat with a depressed region in the middle. 2. The contents of such a vessel.
dive: 1. A jump or plunge into water. 2. A headfirst jump toward the ground or into another substance.
dock: 1. Any of the genus Rumex of coarse weedy plants with small green flowers related to buckwheat, especially common dock, and used as potherbs and in folk medicine, especially in curing nettle rash. 2. A burdock plant, or the leaves of that plant.
dome: 1. A structural element resembling the hollow upper half of a sphere; a cupola 2. Anything shaped like an upset bowl, often used as a cover
drag: 1. Resistance of the air (or some other fluid) to something moving through it. 2. (foundry) The bottom part of a sand casting mold.
drop: 1. A small quantity of liquid, just large enough to hold its own round shape via surface tension, especially one that falls from a source of liquid. 2. A very small quantity of liquid, or (by extension) of anything.
drum: 1. A percussive musical instrument spanned with a thin covering on at least one end for striking, forming an acoustic chamber, affecting what materials are used to make it; a membranophone. 2. Any similar hollow, cylindrical object.
dual: 1. Of an item that is one of a pair, the other item in the pair. 2. Of a regular polyhedron with V vertices and F faces, the regular polyhedron having F vertices and V faces.
dust: 1. Fine particles 2. The act of cleaning by dusting.
duty: 1. That which one is morally or legally obligated to do. 2. The state of being at work and responsible for or doing a particular task.
each: 1. (operations) An individual item: the least quantitative unit in a grouping. 2. For one; apiece; per.
earn: 1. To gain (success, reward, recognition) through applied effort or work. 2. To receive payment for work.
east: 1. One of the four principal compass points, specifically 90°, conventionally directed to the right on maps; the direction of the rising sun at an equinox. Abbreviated as E. 2. Situated or lying in or towards the east; eastward.
easy: 1. Something that is easy 2. Comfortable; at ease.
edge: 1. The boundary line of a surface. 2. A one-dimensional face of a polytope. In particular, the joining line between two vertices of a polygon; the place where two faces of a polyhedron meet.
epic: 1. An extended narrative poem in elevated or dignified language, celebrating the feats of a deity, demigod (heroic epic), other legend or traditional hero. 2. A series of events considered appropriate to an epic.
even: 1. (diminutive) An even number. 2. To make flat and level.
evil: 1. Moral badness; wickedness; malevolence; the forces or behaviors that are the opposite or enemy of good. 2. Something which impairs the happiness of a being or deprives a being of any good; something which causes suffering of any kind to sentient beings; harm; injury; mischief.
exam: 1. The act of examining. 2. Particularly, an inspection by a medical professional to establish the extent and nature of any sickness or injury.
exit: 1. An act of going out or going away, or leaving; a departure. 2. A way out.
face: 1. The front part of the head of a human or other animal, featuring the eyes, nose and mouth, and the surrounding area. 2. One's facial expression.
fact: 1. Something actual as opposed to invented. 2. Something which is real.
fade: 1. A golf shot that (for the right-handed player) curves intentionally to the right. See slice, hook, draw. 2. A haircut where the hair is short or shaved on the sides of the head and longer on top. See also high-top fade and low fade.
fail: 1. Poor quality; substandard workmanship. 2. A failure (condition of being unsuccessful)
fake: 1. Something which is not genuine, or is presented fraudulently. 2. A trick; a swindle.
fame: 1. What is said or reported; gossip, rumour. 2. One's reputation.
fang: 1. A long, pointed canine tooth used for biting and tearing flesh 2. (in snakes) a long pointed tooth for injecting venom
fare: 1. A going; journey; travel; voyage; course; passage. 2. Money paid for a transport ticket.
fear: 1. A strong, uncontrollable, unpleasant emotion or feeling caused by actual or perceived danger or threat. 2. A phobia, a sense of fear induced by something or someone.
feed: 1. Food given to (especially herbivorous) animals. 2. Something supplied continuously.
feel: 1. A quality of an object experienced by touch. 2. A vague mental impression.
file: 1. A collection of papers collated and archived together. 2. A roll or list.
aberration: 1. The act of wandering; deviation from truth, moral rectitude; abnormal; divergence from the straight, correct, proper, normal, or from the natural state. 2. The convergence to different foci, by a lens or mirror, of rays of light emanating from one and the same point, or the deviation of such rays from a single focus; a defect in a focusing mechanism that prevents the intended focal point.
abstruse: 1. Difficult to comprehend or understand. 2. Concealed or hidden out of the way; secret.
accolade: 1. An expression of approval; praise. 2. A special acknowledgment; an award.
acerbic: 1. Tasting sour or bitter. 2. Sharp, harsh, biting.
acumen: 1. Quickness of perception or discernment; penetration of mind; the faculty of nice discrimination. 2. A sharp, tapering point extending from a plant.
hedgehog: 1. A small mammal, of the family Erinaceidae or subfamily Erinaceinae (spiny hedgehog, the latter characterized by their spiny back and often by the habit of rolling up into a ball when attacked.) 2. Any of several spiny mammals, such as the porcupine, that are similar to the hedgehog.
adamant: 1. An imaginary rock or mineral of impenetrable hardness; a name given to the diamond and other substances of extreme hardness. 2. An embodiment of impregnable hardness.
aegis: 1. A mythological shield associated with the Greek deities Zeus and Athena (and their Roman counterparts Jupiter and Minerva) shown as a short cloak made of goatskin worn on the shoulders, more as an emblem of power and protection than a military shield. The aegis of Athena or Minerva is usually shown with a border of snakes and with the head of Medusa in the center. 2. Usually as under the aegis: guidance, protection; endorsement, sponsorship.
aesthetic: 1. The study of art or beauty. 2. That which appeals to the senses.
affable: 1. Receiving others kindly and conversing with them in a free and friendly manner; friendly, courteous, sociable. 2. Mild; benign.
alleviate: To make less severe, as a pain or difficulty.
amalgamate: 1. To merge, to combine, to blend, to join. 2. To make an alloy of a metal and mercury.
ambiguous: 1. Open to multiple interpretations. 2. Vague and unclear.
ambivalence: 1. The coexistence of opposing attitudes or feelings (such as love and hate) towards a person, object or idea. 2. A state of uncertainty or indecisiveness.
ameliorate: 1. To make better, or improve, something perceived to be in a negative condition. 2. To become better; improve.
anachronism: 1. A chronological mistake; the erroneous dating of an event, circumstance, or object. 2. A person or thing which seems to belong to a different time or period of time.
anathema: 1. A ban or curse pronounced with religious solemnity by ecclesiastical authority, often accompanied by excommunication; something denounced as accursed. 2. (by extension) Something which is vehemently disliked by somebody.
animosity: Violent hatred leading to active opposition; active enmity; energetic dislike.
anomaly: 1. A deviation from a rule or from what is regarded as normal; an outlier. 2. Something or someone that is strange or unusual.
antediluvian: 1. One who lived prior to Noah's Flood. 2. Ancient or antiquated.
antipathy: 1. A feeling of dislike (normally towards someone, less often towards something); repugnance or distaste. 2. Natural contrariety or incompatibility
apathy: Lack of emotion or motivation; lack of interest or enthusiasm towards something; disinterest (in something).
apocryphal: 1. Of, or pertaining to, the Apocrypha. 2. (by extension) Of doubtful authenticity, or lacking authority; not regarded as canonical.
appease: 1. To make quiet; to calm; to reduce to a state of peace; to dispel (anger or hatred). 2. To come to terms with; to adapt to the demands of.
apprehension: 1. The physical act of seizing or taking hold of (something); seizing. 2. The act of seizing or taking by legal process; arrest.
arcane: 1. Understood by only a few. 2. (by extension) Obscure, mysterious.
archaic: 1. (usually capitalized) A general term for the prehistoric period intermediate between the earliest period (‘Paleo-Indian’, ‘Paleo-American’, ‘American‐paleolithic’, &c.) of human presence in the Western Hemisphere, and the most recent prehistoric period (‘Woodland’, etc.). 2. (paleoanthropology) (A member of) an archaic variety of Homo sapiens.
arduous: 1. Needing or using up much energy; testing powers of endurance. 2. Burning; ardent
articulate: 1. An animal of the subkingdom Articulata. 2. Clear; effective.
ascetic: 1. One who is devoted to the practice of self-denial, either through seclusion or stringent abstinence. 2. Of or relating to ascetics
asperity: 1. Roughness as of stone or weather. 2. Harshness, as of temper.
assuage: 1. To lessen the intensity of, to mitigate or relieve (hunger, emotion, pain etc.). 2. To pacify or soothe (someone).
astute: 1. Quickly and critically discerning. 2. Shrewd or crafty.
attenuate: 1. To reduce in size, force, value, amount, or degree. 2. To make thinner, as by physically reshaping, starving, or decaying.
audacious: 1. Showing willingness to take bold risks; recklessly daring. 2. Impudent.
augment: 1. (grammar) In some Indo-European languages, a prefix e- (a- in Sanskrit) indicating a past tense of a verb. 2. (grammar) In some Bantu languages, an additional vowel prepended to the noun prefix.
auspicious: 1. Of good omen; indicating future success. 2. Conducive to success.
austere: 1. Grim or severe in manner or appearance 2. Lacking decoration; trivial; not extravagant or gaudy
avarice: 1. Excessive or inordinate desire of gain; greed for wealth 2. Inordinate desire for some supposed good.
banal: 1. Common in a boring way, to the point of being predictable; containing nothing new or fresh. 2. (history) Relating to a type of feudal jurisdiction or service.
bellicose: 1. Warlike in nature; aggressive; hostile. 2. Showing or having the impulse to be combative.
belligerent: 1. A state or other armed participant in warfare 2. Engaged in warfare, warring.
benevolent: 1. Having a disposition to do good. 2. Possessing or manifesting love for mankind.
benign: 1. Kind; gentle; mild. 2. (of a climate or environment) mild and favorable
blandishment: Flattering speech or actions designed to persuade or influence.
blatant: 1. Bellowing; disagreeably clamorous; sounding loudly and harshly. 2. Obvious, on show; unashamed; loudly obtrusive or offensive.
bolster: 1. A large cushion or pillow. 2. A pad, quilt, or anything used to hinder pressure, support part of the body, or make a bandage sit easy upon a wounded part; a compress.
bombastic: 1. (of a person, their language or writing) showy in speech and given to using flowery or elaborate terms; grandiloquent; pompous 2. High-sounding but with little meaning.
boorish: Behaving as a boor; rough in manners.
bucolic: 1. Rustic, pastoral, country-styled. 2. Relating to the pleasant aspects of rustic country life.
burgeon: 1. A bud, sprout, shoot. 2. To grow or expand.
cacophony: A mix of discordant sounds; dissonance.
cajole: To persuade someone to do something which they are reluctant to do, especially by flattery or promises; to coax.
calumny: 1. A false accusation or charge brought to tarnish another's reputation or standing. 2. Falsifications or misrepresentations intended to disparage or discredit another.
camaraderie: 1. Close friendship in a group of friends or teammates. 2. A spirit of familiarity and closeness
candid: 1. A spontaneous or unposed photograph. 2. Impartial and free from prejudice.
capricious: Impulsive and unpredictable; determined by chance, impulse, or whim
captious: 1. That captures; especially, (of an argument, words etc.) designed to capture or entrap in misleading arguments; sophistical. 2. Having a disposition to find fault unreasonably or to raise petty objections; cavilling, nitpicky.
castigate: 1. To punish or reprimand someone severely. 2. To execrate or condemn something in a harsh manner, especially by public criticism.
catalyst: 1. A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed in the process. 2. Someone or something that encourages progress or change.
cathartic: 1. A laxative. 2. Purgative; inducing (mental or physical) catharsis
caustic: 1. Any substance or means which, applied to animal or other organic tissue, burns, corrodes, or destroys it by chemical action; an escharotic. 2. The envelope of reflected or refracted rays of light for a given surface or object.
censure: 1. The act of blaming, criticizing, or condemning as wrong; reprehension. 2. An official reprimand.
charlatan: 1. A mountebank, someone who addresses crowds in the street; (especially), an itinerant seller of medicines or drugs. 2. A malicious trickster; a fake person, especially one who deceives for personal profit.
chicanery: 1. Deception by use of trickery, quibbling, or subterfuge. 2. A slick performance by a lawyer.
choleric: 1. A person with a choleric temperament. 2. A person suffering from cholera (infectious disease).
circumlocution: 1. A roundabout or indirect way of speaking; the use of more words than necessary to express an idea. 2. A roundabout expression.
circumspect: Carefully aware of all circumstances; considerate of all that is pertinent.
clandestine: 1. Done or kept in secret, sometimes to conceal an illicit or improper purpose. 2. (of a person or lodge) Not recognized as a regular member.
clemency: 1. The gentle or kind exercise of power; leniency, mercy; compassion in judging or punishing. 2. A pardon, commutation, or similar reduction, removal, or postponement of legal penalties by an executive officer of a state.
cloying: 1. To fill up or choke up; to stop up. 2. To clog, to glut, or satisfy, as the appetite; to satiate.
coalesce: 1. (of separate elements) To join into a single mass or whole. 2. (of a whole or a unit) To form from different pieces or elements.
cogent: 1. Reasonable and convincing; based on evidence. 2. Appealing to the intellect or powers of reasoning.
cognizant: Aware; fully informed; having understanding of a fact
coherent: 1. Unified; sticking together; making up a whole. 2. Orderly, logical and consistent.
collusion: A secret agreement for an illegal purpose; conspiracy.
commensurate: 1. To reduce to a common measure. 2. To proportionate; to adjust.
compelling: 1. To drive together, round up 2. To overpower; to subdue.
complacent: 1. Uncritically satisfied with oneself or one's achievements; smug. 2. Apathetic with regard to an apparent need or problem.
compliant: 1. Willing to comply; submissive; willing to do what someone wants. 2. Compatible with or following guidelines, specifications, rules, or laws.
comprehensive: 1. A comprehensive school. 2. Broadly or completely covering; including a large proportion of something.
conciliatory: Willing to conciliate, or to make concessions.
concise: 1. To make concise; to abridge or summarize. 2. Brief, yet including all important information
condescend: 1. To come down from one's superior position; to deign (to do something). 2. To treat (someone) as though inferior; to be patronizing (toward someone); to talk down (to someone).
condone: 1. To forgive, excuse or overlook (something that is considered morally wrong, offensive, or generally disliked). 2. To allow, accept or permit (something that is considered morally wrong, offensive, or generally disliked).
conflagration: 1. A large fire extending to many objects, or over a large space; a general burning. 2. A large-scale conflict.
conflate: 1. (biblical criticism) A conflate text, one which conflates multiple version of a text together. 2. To bring (things) together and fuse (them) into a single entity.
confound: 1. A confounding variable. 2. To perplex or puzzle.
congenial: 1. Having the same or very similar nature, personality, tastes, habits or interests. 2. Friendly or sociable.
conjecture: 1. A statement or an idea which is unproven, but is thought to be true; a guess. 2. A supposition based upon incomplete evidence; a hypothesis.
consensus: 1. A process of decision-making that seeks widespread agreement among group members. 2. General agreement among the members of a given group or community, each of which exercises some discretion in decision-making and follow-up action.
consummate: 1. To bring (a task, project, goal etc.) to completion; to accomplish. 2. To make perfect, achieve, give the finishing touch.
contentious: 1. Marked by heated arguments or controversy. 2. Given to struggling with others out of jealousy or discord.
contrite: 1. A contrite person; a penitent. 2. Sincerely penitent or feeling regret or sorrow, especially for one’s own actions; apologetic.
contumacious: 1. Contemptuous of authority; willfully disobedient; rebellious. 2. Willfully disobedient to the summons or orders of a court.
conundrum: 1. A difficult question or riddle, especially one using a play on words in the answer. 2. A difficult choice or decision that must be made.
convoluted: 1. To make unnecessarily complex. 2. To fold or coil into numerous overlapping layers.
copious: 1. Vast in quantity or number, profuse, abundant; taking place on a large scale. 2. Having an abundant supply.
corroborate: 1. To confirm or support something with additional evidence; to attest or vouch for. 2. To make strong; to strengthen.
cosmopolitan: 1. A cosmopolitan person; a cosmopolite. 2. A cocktail containing vodka, triple sec, lime juice and cranberry juice.
credulous: 1. Excessively ready to believe things; gullible. 2. Believed too readily.
cryptic: 1. A cryptic crossword. 2. Having hidden meaning.
culpable: Meriting condemnation, censure or blame, especially as something wrong, harmful or injurious; blameworthy.
cumbersome: 1. Burdensome or hindering, as a weight or drag; vexatious 2. Not easily managed or handled; awkward; clumsy.
cursory: 1. Hasty; superficial; careless 2. Running about; not stationary.
cynical: 1. Of or relating to the belief that human actions are motivated only or primarily by base desires or selfishness. 2. Skeptical of the integrity, sincerity, or motives of others.
dearth: 1. A period or condition when food is rare and hence expensive; famine. 2. (by extension) Scarcity; a lack or short supply.
debacle: 1. An event or enterprise that ends suddenly and disastrously, often with humiliating consequences. 2. A breaking up of a natural dam, usually made of ice, by a river and the ensuing rush of water.
decorum: 1. Appropriate social behavior. 2. A convention of social behavior.
deference: 1. Great respect. 2. The willingness to carry out the wishes of others.
deleterious: 1. Harmful often in a subtle or unexpected way. 2. Having lower fitness.
delineate: 1. To sketch out, draw or trace an outline. 2. To depict, represent with pictures.
