demagogue: 1. A political orator or leader who gains favor by pandering to or exciting the passions and prejudices of the audience rather than by using rational argument. 2. A leader of the people.
demur: 1. Stop; pause; hesitation as to proceeding; suspense of decision or action; scruple. 2. To linger; to stay; to tarry
denigrate: 1. To criticise so as to besmirch; traduce, disparage or defame. 2. To treat as worthless; belittle, degrade or disparage.
deprecate: 1. To belittle or express disapproval of. 2. To declare something obsolescent; to recommend against a function, technique, command, etc. that still works but has been replaced.
derivative: 1. Something derived. 2. A word that derives from another one.
desiccate: 1. A substance which has been dessicated, that is, had its moisture removed. 2. To remove moisture from; to dry.
despot: 1. A ruler with absolute power; a tyrant. 2. A title awarded to senior members of the imperial family in the late Byzantine Empire, and claimed by various independent or semi-autonomous rulers in the Balkans (12th to 15th centuries)
desultory: 1. Jumping, or passing, from one thing or subject to another, without order, planning, or rational connection; lacking logical sequence. 2. Out of course; by the way; not connected with the subject.
diaphanous: 1. Transparent or translucent; allowing light to pass through; capable of being seen through. 2. Of a fine, almost transparent, texture; gossamer; light and insubstantial.
diatribe: 1. An abusive, bitter, attack or criticism: denunciation. 2. A prolonged discourse.
didactic: 1. A treatise on teaching or education. 2. Instructive or intended to teach or demonstrate, especially with regard to morality.
diffident: 1. Lacking confidence in others; distrustful. 2. Lacking self-confidence; timid; modest
digression: 1. An aside, an act of straying from the main subject in speech or writing. 2. The act of straying from the main subject in speech or writing, particularly for rhetorical effect.
dilatory: 1. Relating to dilation; dilative 2. Intentionally delaying (someone or something), intended to cause delay, gain time, or defer decision.
dilettante: 1. An amateur, someone who dabbles in a field out of casual interest rather than as a profession or serious interest. 2. (sometimes offensive) A person with a general but superficial interest in any art or a branch of knowledge.
dirge: 1. A mournful poem or piece of music composed or performed as a memorial to a dead person. 2. A song or piece of music that is considered too slow, bland or boring.
discern: 1. To detect with the senses, especially with the eyes. 2. To perceive, recognize, or comprehend with the mind; to descry.
discordant: 1. Not in harmony or accord 2. Harsh or dissonant-sounding
discrepancy: 1. An inconsistency between facts or sentiments. 2. The state or quality of being discrepant.
discursive: 1. (of speech or writing) Tending to digress from the main point; rambling. 2. Using reason and argument rather than intuition.
disdain: 1. A feeling of contempt or scorn. 2. That which is worthy to be disdained or regarded with contempt and aversion.
disingenuous: 1. Not honourable; unworthy of honour 2. Not ingenuous; not frank or open
disparage: 1. Inequality in marriage; marriage with an inferior. 2. To match unequally; to degrade or dishonor.
disparate: 1. (chiefly in the plural) Any of a group of unequal or dissimilar things. 2. Composed of inherently different or distinct elements; incongruous.
dissemble: 1. To disguise or conceal something. 2. To feign.
disseminate: 1. To sow and scatter principles, ideas, opinions, etc, or concrete things, for growth and propagation, like seeds. 2. To become widespread.
dissonance: 1. A harsh, discordant combination of sounds. 2. Conflicting notes that are not overtones of the note or chord sounding.
divergent: 1. Growing further apart; diverging. 2. Of a series, not converging; not approaching a limit.
dogmatic: 1. One of an ancient sect of physicians who went by general principles; opposed to the empiric. 2. Adhering only to principles which are true a priori, rather than truths based on evidence or deduction.
dormant: 1. A crossbeam or joist. 2. Inactive, sleeping, asleep, suspended.
ebullient: 1. Enthusiastic; high-spirited. 2. (of a liquid) Boiling or agitated as if boiling.
eclectic: 1. Someone who selects according to the eclectic method. 2. Selecting a mixture of what appears to be best of various doctrines, methods or styles.
efficacy: 1. Ability to produce a desired effect under ideal testing conditions. 2. Degree of ability to produce a desired effect.
effrontery: 1. Insolent and shameless audacity. 2. An act of insolent and shameless audacity.
egalitarian: 1. A person who accepts or promotes social equality and equal rights for all people. 2. Characterized by social equality and equal rights for all people.
egregious: 1. Usually in a negative sense: conspicuous, exceptional, outstanding. 2. Outrageously bad; shocking.
elegy: 1. A mournful or plaintive poem; a funeral song; a poem of lamentation. 2. A composition of mournful character.
elicit: 1. To evoke, educe (emotions, feelings, responses, etc.); to generate, obtain, or provoke as a response or answer. 2. To draw out, bring out, bring forth (something latent); to obtain information from someone or something.
eloquent: 1. Fluently persuasive and articulate 2. Effective in expressing meaning by speech
elucidate: To make clear; to clarify; to shed light upon.
embellish: 1. To make more beautiful and attractive; to decorate. 2. To make something sound or look better or more acceptable than it is in reality; to distort, to embroider.
empirical: 1. Pertaining to or based on experience. 2. Pertaining to, derived from, or testable by observations made using the physical senses or using instruments which extend the senses.
emulate: 1. To attempt to equal or be the same as. 2. To copy or imitate, especially a person.
enervate: 1. To reduce strength or energy; debilitate. 2. To weaken morally or mentally.
engender: 1. To beget (of a man); to bear or conceive (of a woman). 2. To give existence to, to produce (living creatures).
ennui: 1. A gripping listlessness or melancholia caused by boredom; depression. 2. To make bored or listless; to weary.
ephemeral: 1. Something which lasts for a short period of time. 2. Lasting for a short period of time.
equanimity: The state of being calm, stable and composed, especially under stress.
equivocal: 1. A word or expression capable of different meanings; an ambiguous term. 2. Having two or more equally applicable meanings; capable of double or multiple interpretation.
erudite: 1. A learned or scholarly person 2. Learned, scholarly, with emphasis on knowledge gained from books.
esoteric: 1. An esoteric doctrine or treatise; esoteric philosophy. 2. One who believes, or is an initiate, in esoteric doctrines or rites.
eulogy: 1. An oration to honor a deceased person, usually at a funeral. 2. Speaking highly of someone or something; the act of praising or commending someone or something.
euphemism: 1. The use of a word or phrase to replace another with one that is considered less offensive, blunt or vulgar than the word or phrase which it replaces. 2. A word or phrase that is used to replace another in this way.
evanescent: 1. Disappearing, vanishing. 2. Barely there; almost imperceptible.
exacerbate: To make worse (a problem, bad situation, negative feeling, etc.); aggravate; exasperate.
exalt: 1. To honor; to hold in high esteem. 2. To raise in rank, status etc., to elevate.
exculpate: To clear of or to free from guilt; exonerate.
exigent: 1. Extremity; end; limit; pressing urgency. 2. The amount that is required.
exonerate: 1. To relieve (someone or something) of a load; to unburden (a load). 2. Of a body of water: to discharge or empty (itself).
exorbitant: Exceeding proper limits; extravagant; excessive or unduly high.
expedient: 1. A method or means for achieving a particular result, especially when direct or efficient; a resource. 2. Suitable to effect some desired end or the purpose intended.
expedite: 1. To accelerate the progress of. 2. To perform (a task) fast and efficiently.
explicit: 1. Very specific, clear, or detailed. 2. Containing material (e.g. language or film footage) that might be deemed offensive or graphic.
expunge: 1. To erase or strike out. 2. To eliminate completely; annihilate.
extemporaneous: Without preparation or advanced thought; offhand.
extraneous: 1. Not belonging to, or dependent upon, a thing; without or beyond a thing; foreign 2. Not essential or intrinsic
extrapolate: 1. To infer by extending known information. 2. To estimate the value of a variable outside a known range from values within that range by assuming that the estimated value follows logically from the known ones
extricate: 1. To free, disengage, loosen, or untangle. 2. To free from intricacies or perplexity
facetious: 1. Treating serious issues with (often deliberately) inappropriate humour; flippant. 2. Pleasantly humorous; jocular.
fallacious: 1. Characterized by fallacy; false or mistaken. 2. Deceptive or misleading.
fastidious: 1. Excessively particular, demanding, or fussy about details, especially about tidiness and cleanliness. 2. Overly concerned about tidiness and cleanliness.
fatuous: Obnoxiously stupid, vacantly silly, content in one's foolishness.
fawning: 1. To give birth to a fawn. 2. To exhibit affection or attempt to please.
felicitous: 1. Characterized by felicity. 2. Of a sentence or utterance: semantically and pragmatically coherent; fitting in the context.
fervent: 1. Exhibiting particular enthusiasm, zeal, conviction, persistence, or belief. 2. Having or showing emotional warmth, fervor, or passion.
fidelity: 1. Faithfulness to one's duties. 2. Loyalty to one's spouse or partner, including abstention from extramarital affairs.
flagrant: 1. Obvious and offensive; blatant; scandalous. 2. On fire; flaming.
flippant: 1. Glib; speaking with ease and rapidity 2. Nimble; limber.
flout: 1. The act by which something is flouted; violation of a law. 2. A mockery or insult.
foment: 1. Fomentation. 2. To incite or cause troublesome acts; to encourage; to instigate.
forestall: 1. To prevent, delay or hinder something by taking precautionary or anticipatory measures; to avert. 2. To preclude or bar from happening, render impossible.
fortuitous: 1. Happening by chance; coincidental, accidental. 2. Happening by a lucky chance; lucky or fortunate.
fractious: 1. Given to troublemaking. 2. Irritable; argumentative; quarrelsome.
frivolous: 1. Silly, especially at an inappropriate time or in an inappropriate manner. 2. Of little weight or importance; not worth notice; slight.
frugal: Avoiding unnecessary expenditure either of money or of anything else which is to be used or consumed; avoiding waste.
fulminate: 1. Any salt or ester of fulminic acid, mostly explosive. 2. To make a verbal attack.
furtive: 1. Stealthy. 2. Exhibiting guilty or evasive secrecy.
futile: Incapable of producing results; doomed not to be successful; not worth attempting.
gainsay: To say something in contradiction to.
garrulous: 1. Excessively or tiresomely talkative. 2. (of something written or performed) Excessively wordy and rambling.
germane: Related to the topic being discussed or considered.
glib: 1. To make glib. 2. Having a ready flow of words but lacking thought or understanding; superficial; shallow.
gossamer: 1. A fine film or strand as of cobwebs, floating in the air or caught on bushes, etc. 2. A soft, sheer fabric.
grandiloquent: (of a person, their language or writing) given to using language in a showy way by using an excessive amount of difficult words to impress others; bombastic; turgid
gregarious: 1. (of a person) Describing one who enjoys being in crowds and socializing. 2. Of animals that travel in herds or packs.
guile: 1. Astuteness often marked by a certain sense of cunning or artful deception. 2. Deceptiveness, deceit, fraud, duplicity, dishonesty.
hackneyed: 1. To make uninteresting or trite by frequent use. 2. To use as a hackney.
halcyon: 1. A kingfisher said in classical mythology to nest on the sea, thereby calming the waters. 2. A tropical kingfisher of the genus Halcyon, such as the sacred kingfisher (Halcyon sancta) of Australia.
hallowed: 1. To make holy, to sanctify. 2. To shout, especially to urge on dogs for hunting.
hapless: 1. Very unlucky; ill-fated. 2. Devoid of talent or skill.
harangue: 1. An impassioned, disputatious public speech. 2. A tirade, harsh scolding or rant, whether spoken or written.
hegemony: 1. Domination, influence, or authority over another, especially by one political group over a society or by one nation over others. 2. Dominance of one social group over another, such that the ruling group or hegemon acquires some degree of consent from the subordinate, as opposed to dominance purely by force.
heretical: 1. Of or pertaining to heresy or heretics. 2. (of ideas or views) Contrary to mainstream or accepted opinion.
hermetic: 1. (chiefly with capital initial) Pertaining to Hermes Trismegistus or the writings attributed to him. 2. Pertaining to alchemy or occult practices; magical, alchemical.
heterodox: Of or pertaining to creeds, beliefs, or teachings, especially religious ones, that are different from orthodoxy, or the norm, but not sufficiently different to be called heretical.
hierarchy: 1. A body of authoritative officials organized in nested ranks. 2. A social, religious, economic or political system or organization in which people or groups of people are ranked with some superior to others based on their status, authority or some other trait.
hinder: 1. To make difficult to accomplish; to act as an obstacle; to frustrate. 2. To delay or impede; to keep back, to prevent.
histrionic: 1. Of or relating to actors or acting. 2. (by extension) Excessively dramatic or emotional, especially with the intention to draw attention.
homogeneous: 1. Of the same kind; alike, similar. 2. Having the same composition throughout; of uniform make-up.
hubris: Excessive pride, presumption or arrogance (originally toward the gods).
hyperbole: 1. Deliberate or unintentional overstatement, particularly extreme overstatement. 2. An instance or example of such overstatement.
iconoclast: 1. One who destroys religious images or icons, especially an opponent of the Orthodox Church in the 8th and 9th centuries, or a Puritan during the European Reformation. 2. One who opposes orthodoxy and religion; one who adheres to the doctrine of iconoclasm.
idiosyncrasy: 1. A behavior or way of thinking that is characteristic of a person. 2. A language or behaviour that is particular to an individual or group.
illicit: 1. A banned or unlawful item. 2. Not approved by law, but not invalid.
immutable: 1. Something that cannot be changed 2. Unable to be changed without exception.
impartial: Treating all parties, rivals, or disputants equally; not partial; not biased
impeccable: 1. Perfect, without faults, flaws or errors 2. Incapable of wrongdoing or sin; immaculate
impediment: 1. A hindrance; that which impedes or obstructs progress. 2. A disability, especially one affecting the hearing or speech.
imperturbable: 1. Not easily perturbed, upset or excited. 2. Calm and collected, even under pressure.
impetuous: 1. Making arbitrary decisions, especially in an impulsive and forceful manner. 2. Characterized by sudden violence or vehemence.
implacable: 1. Not able to be placated or appeased. 2. Impossible to prevent or stop; inexorable, unrelenting, unstoppable.
implicit: 1. Implied indirectly, without being directly expressed 2. Contained in the essential nature of something but not openly shown
impudence: 1. The quality of being impudent, not showing due respect. 2. Impudent language, conduct or behavior.
inadvertent: 1. Not intentional; not on purpose; not conscious. 2. Inattentive.
inane: 1. That which is void or empty. 2. Lacking sense or meaning (often to the point of boredom or annoyance)
incessant: Without pause or stop; not ending, especially to the point of annoyance.
inchoate: 1. A beginning, an immature start. 2. To begin or start (something).
incisive: 1. Quickly proceeding to judgment and forceful in expression; decisive; forthright. 2. Intelligently analytical and concise.
incongruous: 1. Not similar or congruent; not matching or fitting in. 2. Of two numbers, with respect to a third, such that their difference can not be divided by it without a remainder.
incorrigible: 1. An incorrigibly bad individual. 2. Defective and impossible to materially correct or set aright.
indigenous: 1. Born or originating in, native to a land or region, especially before an intrusion. 2. Innate, inborn.
indigent: 1. A person in need, or in poverty. 2. Poor; destitute; in need.
indolent: 1. Habitually lazy, procrastinating, or resistant to physical labor 2. Inducing laziness
indomitable: Incapable of being subdued, overcome, or vanquished.
ineffable: 1. Beyond expression in words; unspeakable. 2. Forbidden to be uttered; taboo.
inept: 1. Not able to do something; not proficient; displaying incompetence. 2. Unfit; unsuitable.
inexorable: 1. Impossible to prevent or stop; inevitable. 2. Unable to be persuaded; relentless; unrelenting.
infamous: 1. Having a bad reputation, disreputable; notoriously bad, unpleasant or evil; widely known, especially for something bad. 2. Causing infamy; disgraceful.
ingenious: 1. Displaying genius or brilliance; tending to invent. 2. Characterized by genius; cleverly done or contrived.
ingenuous: 1. Naive and trusting. 2. Demonstrating childlike simplicity.
iniquity: 1. Deviation from what is right; gross injustice, sin, wickedness. 2. An act of great injustice or unfairness; a sinful or wicked act; an unconscionable deed.
innocuous: 1. Harmless; producing no ill effect. 2. Inoffensive; unprovocative; not exceptional.
insidious: 1. Producing harm in a stealthy, often gradual, manner. 2. Intending to entrap; alluring but harmful.
insipid: 1. Unappetizingly flavorless. 2. Flat; lacking character or definition.
insolent: 1. A person who is insolent. 2. Insulting in manner or words.
intransigent: 1. A person who is intransigent. 2. Unwilling to compromise or moderate a position; unreasonable
inundate: 1. To cover with large amounts of water; to flood. 2. To overwhelm.
inured: 1. To cause someone to become accustomed to something (usually) unpleasant. 2. To take effect, to be operative.
invective: 1. An expression which inveighs or rails against a person. 2. A severe or violent censure or reproach.
inveterate: 1. To fix and settle after a long time; to entrench. 2. Firmly established from having been around for a long time; of long standing
irascible: Easily provoked to outbursts of anger; irritable.
irresolute: 1. Undecided or unsure how to act 2. Indecisive or lacking in resolution
itinerary: 1. A written schedule of activities for a vacation or road trip. 2. A route or proposed route of a journey.
jeopardize: To put in jeopardy, to threaten.
judicious: Having, characterized by, or done with good judgment or sound thinking.
juxtapose: To place side by side, especially for contrast or comparison.
kinetic: 1. Relating to motion 2. Relating to kinesis or motor function
laconic: Using as few words as possible; pithy and concise.
lament: 1. An expression of grief, suffering, sadness or regret. 2. A song expressing grief.
languid: 1. Lacking enthusiasm, energy, or strength; drooping or flagging from weakness, fatigue, or lack of energy 2. Heavy; dull; dragging; wanting spirit or animation; listless; apathetic.
latent: 1. (forensics) The residue left by a person's finger that can be made visible by a process such as powder dusting; a latent fingerprint. 2. An underlying cause that can be inferred from statistical correlations; factor.
aardvark: 1. The nocturnal, insectivorous, burrowing, mammal Orycteropus afer, of the order Tubulidentata, somewhat resembling a pig, common in some parts of sub-Saharan Africa. 2. A silly or credulous person who is prone to mistakes or blunders.
albatross: 1. Any of various large seabirds of the family Diomedeidae ranging widely in the Southern Ocean and the North Pacific and having a hooked beak and long narrow wings. 2. Any of various African and Asian pierid butterflies of the genus Appias. Some species of this genus are also known as puffins.
armadillo: Any of the burrowing mammals covered with bony, jointed, protective plates, order Cingulata, found in the Americas, especially in South America.
axolotl: A critically endangered salamander found in the elevated lakes of Mexico, Ambystoma mexicanum.
binturong: A large species of civet, Arctictis binturong, of southern Asia.
bushbaby: An small, nocturnal, African primate, similar to a lemur.
capybara: A semi-aquatic South American rodent, Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris, the largest living rodent.
caracal: A type of cat native to Southern Africa, West Asia, and parts of Central and South Asia, Caracal caracal.
cassowary: A large flightless bird of the genus Casuarius that is native to Australia and New Guinea, has a characteristic bony crest on its head, and can be very dangerous.
chinchilla: 1. Either of two small, crepuscular rodents of the genus Chinchilla, native to the Andes, prized for their very soft fur and often kept as pets. 2. The fur of a chinchilla, used for clothing.
coelacanth: 1. Either of two species of deep-water fish, Latimeria chalumnae of the Indian Ocean and Latimeria menadoensis of Indonesia. 2. Any lobe-finned fish in the order Coelacanthiformes, thought until 1938 to have been extinct for 70 million years.
dugong: A plant-eating aquatic marine mammal, of the genus Dugong, found in tropical regions.
echidna: Any of the species of small spined monotremes in family Tachyglossidae, the four extant species of which are found in Australia and southern New Guinea.
fossa: 1. A pit, groove, cavity, or depression. 2. A long, narrow, shallow depression on the body of an extraterrestrial body, such as a planet or moon.
kakapo: A large flightless parrot, Strigops habroptilus, with greenish plumage, that is nocturnal and native to New Zealand.
kinkajou: Potos flavus, a carnivorous mammal of Central America and South America with a long, prehensile tail, related to the raccoon.
macaque: Any of a group of Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae, especially genus Macaca.
narwhal: Monodon monoceros, an Arctic cetacean that grows to about 20 feet (6 meters) long, the male having a single horn-like tusk, a twisted, pointed canine tooth that projects forward.
ocelot: An American feline carnivore (Felis pardalis) covered with blackish ocellated spots and blotches which are variously arranged.
okapi: A large ruminant mammal, Okapia johnstoni, found in the rainforests of the Congo, related to the giraffe, but with a much shorter neck, a reddish brown coat and zebra-like stripes on its hindquarters.
orangutan: An arboreal anthropoid ape genus Pongo consisting of two species, Pongo pygmaeus of Borneo and Pongo abelii of Sumatra, having a shaggy reddish-brown coat, long arms, and no tail.
platypus: A semi-aquatic, egg-laying monotreme mammal with a bill resembling that of a duck, that has a mole-like body, a tail resembling that of a beaver, a waterproof pelt, and flat webbed feet — males have poisonous spurs on the inside of the back legs; Ornithorhynchus anatinus
ptarmigan: Any of three species of small grouse in the genus Lagopus found in subarctic tundra areas of North America and Eurasia.
quetzal: 1. Any trogon of the genus Pharomacrus, especially the resplendent quetzal, Pharomacrus mocinno, which has very long tail feathers and is found in Guatemala and Costa Rica. 2. A monetary unit used in Guatemala, equal to 100 centavos.
salamander: 1. A long, slender, chiefly terrestrial amphibian of the order Caudata, superficially resembling a lizard. 2. A creature much like a lizard that is resistant to and lives in fire (in which it is often depicted in heraldry), hence the elemental being of fire.
serval: A medium-sized African wild cat, Leptailurus serval, formerly Felis serval.
tapir: Any one of the species of large odd-toed ungulates of the taxonomic family Tapiridae with a long prehensile upper lip, of which all four surviving species are in genus Tapirus.
tuatara: Either of two reptiles, Sphenodon punctatus and Sphenodon guntheri, native to New Zealand, that resemble lizards.
laudatory: Of or pertaining to praise, or the expression of praise.
lionize: 1. To treat (a person) as if they were important, or a celebrity. 2. To visit famous places in order to revere them.
lucid: 1. A lucid dream. 2. Clear; easily understood
lugubrious: Gloomy, mournful or dismal, especially to an exaggerated degree.
abolish: 1. To end a law, system, institution, custom or practice. 2. To put an end to or destroy, as a physical object; to wipe out.
abrupt: 1. Something which is abrupt; an abyss. 2. To tear off or asunder.
abundant: 1. Fully sufficient; found in copious supply; in great quantity; overflowing. 2. Richly supplied; wealthy; possessing in great quantity.
accessible: 1. Easy of access or approach. 2. (specifically) Built or designed as to be usable by people with disabilities.
accommodate: 1. To render fit, suitable, or correspondent; to adapt. 2. To cause to come to agreement; to bring about harmony; to reconcile.
accumulate: 1. To heap up in a mass; to pile up; to collect or bring together (either literally or figuratively) 2. To grow or increase in quantity or number; to increase greatly.
acknowledge: 1. To admit the knowledge of; to recognize as a fact or truth; to declare one's belief in 2. To own or recognize in a particular quality, character or relationship; to admit the claims or authority of; to give recognition to.
acquire: 1. To get. 2. To gain, usually by one's own exertions; to get as one's own
adequate: 1. To equalize; to make adequate. 2. To equal.
adjacent: 1. Something that lies next to something else, especially the side of a right triangle that is neither the hypotenuse nor the opposite. 2. Lying next to, close, or contiguous; neighboring; bordering on.
adolescent: 1. A person who is in adolescence; someone who has reached puberty but is not yet an adult. 2. Of, relating to, or at the age of adolescence; at the stage between being a child and an adult
advocate: 1. Someone whose job is to speak for someone's case in a court of law; a counsel. 2. Anyone who argues the case of another; an intercessor.
aggregate: 1. A mass, assemblage, or sum of particulars; something consisting of elements but considered as a whole. 2. A mass formed by the union of homogeneous particles; – in distinction from a compound, formed by the union of heterogeneous particles.

allocate: 1. To set aside for a purpose. 2. To distribute according to a plan, generally followed by the adposition to.

analyze: 1. To subject to analysis. 2. To resolve (anything complex) into its elements.
anticipate: 1. To act before (someone), especially to prevent an action. 2. To take up or introduce (something) prematurely.
apparent: 1. Capable of being seen, or easily seen; open to view; visible to the eye, eyely; within sight or view. 2. Clear or manifest to the understanding; plain; evident; obvious; known; palpable; indubitable.

arrogant: Having excessive pride in oneself, often with contempt or disrespect for others.
assemble: 1. To put together. 2. To gather as a group.
assess: 1. To determine, estimate or judge the value of; to evaluate 2. To impose or charge, especially as punishment for an infraction.

beneficial: 1. Something that is beneficial. 2. Helpful or good to something or someone.

calculate: 1. To determine the value of something or the solution to something by a mathematical process. 2. To determine values or solutions by a mathematical process; reckon.

candidate: 1. A person who is running in an election. 2. A person who is applying for a job.

category: 1. A group, often named or numbered, to which items are assigned based on similarity or defined criteria. 2. commodity: 1. Anything movable (a good) that is bought and sold. 2. Something useful or valuable.
compatible: 1. Something that is compatible with something else. 2. Capable of easy interaction.
compensate: 1. To do (something good) after (something bad) happens 2. To pay or reward someone in exchange for work done or some other consideration.

comprehend: 1. To include, comprise; to contain. 2. To understand or grasp fully and thoroughly.

convenient: 1. Serving to reduce a difficulty, or accessible with minimum difficulty; expedient. 2. Fit; suitable; appropriate.

currency: 1. Money or other items used to facilitate transactions. 2. (more specifically) Paper money.

discipline: 1. A controlled behaviour; self-control. 2. A specific branch of knowledge or learning.

dispute: 1. An argument or disagreement, a failure to agree. 2. Verbal controversy or disagreement; altercation; debate.

distinct: 1. Capable of being perceived very clearly. 2. Different from one another (with the preferable adposition being "from").

cheetah: A distinctive member (Acinonyx jubatus) of the cat family, slightly smaller than the leopard, but with proportionately longer limbs and a smaller head. It is native to Africa and also credited with being the fastest terrestrial animal.
cougar: 1. A mountain lion; Puma concolor. 2. An older woman who actively seeks the casual, often sexual, companionship of younger men, by implication a female “sexual predator”.
coyote: 1. Canis latrans, a species of canine native to North America. 2. A smuggler of undocumented immigrants across the land border from Latin America into the United States of America.
dingo: Canis lupus dingo, a wild dog native to Australia.
flamingo: 1. A wading bird of the family Phoenicopteridae. 2. A deep pink color tinged with orange, like that of a flamingo.
iguana: 1. A green iguana (Iguana iguana), a large tropical American lizard often kept as a pet 2. In zoology, any member of the genus Iguana
jaguar: A carnivorous spotted large cat native to South and Central America, Panthera onca.
koala: A tree-dwelling marsupial, Phascolarctos cinereus, that resembles a small bear with a broad head, large ears and sharp claws, mainly found in eastern Australia.
lemur: 1. Any strepsirrhine primate of the infraorder Lemuriformes, superfamily Lemuroidea, native only to Madagascar and some surrounding islands. 2. Any of the genus Lemur, represented by the ring-tailed lemur (Lemur catta).
leopard: 1. Panthera pardus, a large wild cat with a spotted coat native to Africa and Asia, especially the male of the species (in contrast to leopardess). 2. (inexact) A similar-looking, large wild cat named after the leopard.
llama: A South American mammal of the camel family, Lama glama, used as a domestic beast of burden and a source of wool and meat.
manatee: Any of several plant-eating marine mammals, of family Trichechidae, found in tropical regions.
marmot: Any of several large ground-dwelling rodents of the genera Marmota and Cynomys in the squirrel family.
meerkat: Suricata suricatta, a small carnivorous mammal of the mongoose family, from the Kalahari Desert, known for its habit of standing on its hind legs.
moose: 1. The largest member of the deer family (Alces americanus, sometimes included in Alces alces), of which the male has very large, palmate antlers. 2. An ugly person.
otter: 1. An aquatic or marine carnivorous mammal in the subfamily Lutrinae of the family Mustelidae, which also includes weasels, polecats, badgers, and others. 2. A hairy man with a slender physique, in contrast with a bear, who is more thickset.
panda: 1. The red panda (Ailurus fulgens), a small raccoon-like animal of northeast Asia with reddish fur and a long, ringed tail. 2. Short for giant panda.
panther: 1. Any of various big cats with black fur; most especially, the black-coated leopard of India. 2. Any big cat of the genus Panthera.
pelican: 1. Any of various seabirds of the family Pelecanidae, having a long bill with a distendable pouch. 2. A native or resident of the American state of Louisiana.
penguin: 1. Any of several flightless sea birds, of order Sphenisciformes, found in the Southern Hemisphere, marked by their usual upright stance, walking on short legs, and (generally) their stark black and white plumage. 2. An auk (sometimes especially a great auk), a bird of the Northern Hemisphere.
raccoon: 1. A nocturnal omnivore native to North America, typically with a mixture of gray, brown, and black fur, a mask-like marking around the eyes and a striped tail; Procyon lotor. 2. Any mammal of the genus Procyon.
reindeer: 1. (plural: reindeer) Any Arctic and subarctic-dwelling deer of the species Rangifer tarandus, with a number of subspecies. 2. (plural: reindeers) Any species, subspecies, ecotype, or other scientific grouping of such animals.
seal: 1. A pinniped (Pinnipedia), particularly an earless seal (true seal) or eared seal. 2. A bearing representing a creature something like a walrus.
skunk: 1. Any of various small mammals, of the family Mephitidae, native to North and Central America, having a glossy black with a white coat and two musk glands at the base of the tail for emitting a noxious smell as a defensive measure. 2. A despicable person.
sloth: 1. Laziness; slowness in the mindset; disinclination to action or labour. 2. A herbivorous, arboreal South American mammal of the families Megalonychidae and Bradypodidae, noted for its slowness and inactivity.
toucan: Any of various neotropical frugivorous birds from the family Ramphastidae, with a large colorful beak.
walrus: A large Arctic marine mammal related to seals and having long tusks, tough, wrinkled skin, and four flippers, Odobenus rosmarus.
weasel: 1. The least weasel, Mustela nivalis. 2. Any of the carnivorous mammals of the genus Mustela, having a slender body, a long tail and usually a light brown upper coat and light-coloured belly.
wombat: Any of several herbivorous, burrowing marsupials, of the family Vombatidae, mainly found in southern and eastern Australia.
abandonment: 1. The act of abandoning, or the state of being abandoned; total desertion; relinquishment. 2. The voluntary leaving of a person to whom one is bound by a special relation, as a wife, husband or child; desertion.
abbreviation: 1. The result of shortening or reducing; abridgment. 2. A shortened or contracted form of a word or phrase, used to represent the whole, utilizing omission of letters, and sometimes substitution of letters, or duplication of initial letters to signify plurality, including signs such as +, =, @.
abdicate: 1. To disclaim and expel from the family, as a father his child; to disown; to disinherit. 2. To formally separate oneself from or to divest oneself of.
abduction: 1. Leading away; a carrying away. 2. The act of abducing or abducting; a drawing apart; the movement which separates a limb or other part from the axis, or middle line, of the body.
abstinence: 1. The act or practice of abstaining, refraining from indulging a desire or appetite. 2. The practice of self-denial; self-restraint; forebearance from anything.
abstraction: 1. The act of abstracting, separating, withdrawing, or taking away; withdrawal; the state of being taken away. 2. A separation from worldly objects; a recluse life; the withdrawal from one's senses.
absurdity: 1. That which is absurd; an absurd action; a logical contradiction. 2. The quality of being absurd or inconsistent with obvious truth, reason, or sound judgment.
acceleration: 1. The act of accelerating, or the state of being accelerated; increase of motion or action; as opposed to retardation or deceleration. 2. The amount by which a speed or velocity increases (and so a scalar quantity or a vector quantity).
accessory: 1. Having a secondary, supplementary or subordinate function by accompanying as a subordinate; aiding in a secondary way; being additional; being connected as an incident or subordinate to a principal; contributing or being contributory. Said of people and things, and, when of people, usually in a bad sense 2. Assisting a crime without actually participating in committing the crime itself.
acclaim: 1. To shout; to call out. 2. To express great approval (for).
acclimate: 1. To habituate to a climate not native; to acclimatize. 2. To adjust to a new environment; not necessarily a wild, natural, earthy one.
accomplishment: 1. The act of accomplishing; completion; fulfilment. 2. That which completes, perfects, or equips thoroughly; acquirement; attainment; that which constitutes excellence of mind, or elegance of manners, acquired by education or training.
accordance: 1. Agreement; harmony; conformity; compliance. 2. The act of granting something.
accountability: 1. The state of being accountable; liability to be called on to render an account; accountableness; responsible for; answerable for. 2. The obligation imposed by law or lawful order or regulation on an officer or other person for keeping accurate record of property, documents, or funds. The person having this obligation may or may not have actual possession of the property, documents, or funds. Accountability is concerned primarily with records, while responsibility is concerned primarily with custody, care, and safekeeping.
accuracy: 1. The state of being accurate; being free from mistakes, this exemption arising from carefulness; exactness; correctness 2. Exact conformity to truth, or to a rule or model; degree of conformity of a measure to a true or standard value.
accusation: 1. The act of accusing. 2. A formal charge brought against a person in a court of law.
achievement: 1. The act of achieving or performing; a successful performance; accomplishment 2. A great or heroic deed or feat; something accomplished by valor or boldness
acquisition: 1. The act or process of acquiring. 2. The thing acquired or gained; a gain.
acquittal: 1. The act of fulfilling the duties (of a given role, obligation etc.). 2. A legal decision that someone is not guilty with which they have been charged, or the formal dismissal of a charge by some other legal process.
activation: 1. Making active and effective; bringing into a state of activity. 2. The process of making a radioisotope by bombarding a stable element with neutrons or protons.
adaptation: 1. The process of adapting something or becoming adapted to a situation; adjustment, modification. 2. A change that is made or undergone to suit a condition or environment.
addictive: 1. A drug that causes an addiction. 2. Anything that is very habit-forming.
addition: 1. The act of adding anything. 2. Anything that is added.
adherence: 1. A close physical union of two objects. 2. Faithful support for some cause.
adjustment: 1. The action of adjusting something 2. The result of adjusting something; a small change; a minor correction; a modification or alteration
administer: 1. To cause to ingest (a drug), either by openly offering or through deceit. 2. To apportion out, distribute.
admiration: 1. A positive emotion including wonder and approbation; the regarding of another as being wonderful 2. Wondering or questioning (without any particular positive or negative attitude to the subject).
admission: 1. The act or practice of admitting. 2. Permission to enter, or the entrance itself; admittance; entrance; access
adoption: 1. The act of adopting. 2. The state of being adopted; the acceptance of a child of other parents as if he or she were one's own child.
adornment: 1. A decoration; that which adorns. 2. The act of decorating.
advancement: 1. The act of advancing, ; promotion to a higher place or dignity 2. The state of being advanced
adverse: 1. Unfavorable; antagonistic in purpose or effect; hostile; actively opposing one's interests or wishes; contrary to one's welfare; acting against; working in an opposing direction. 2. Opposed; contrary; opposing one's interests or desire.
advisory: 1. A warning. 2. Able to give advice.
advocacy: 1. The profession of an advocate 2. The act of arguing in favour of, or supporting something
affectionate: 1. (of a person) Having affection or warm regard; loving; fond. 2. (of an action, etc.) Characterised by or proceeding from affection; indicating love; tender.
affiliation: 1. The relationship resulting from affiliating one thing with another. 2. The establishment of a child's paternity or maternity
affirmation: 1. That which is affirmed; a declaration that something is true. 2. The solemn declaration made by Quakers and others incapable of taking an oath.
affliction: 1. A state of pain, suffering, distress or agony. 2. Something which causes pain, suffering, distress or agony.
affluent: 1. Somebody who is wealthy. 2. A stream or river flowing into a larger river or into a lake; a tributary stream; a tributary.
aftermath: 1. A second mowing; the grass which grows after the first crop of hay in the same season. 2. That which happens after, that which follows, usually of strongly negative connotation in most contexts, implying a preceding catastrophe.
aggravate: 1. To make (an offence) worse or more severe; to increase in offensiveness or heinousness. 2. (by extension) To make worse; to exacerbate.
aggregation: 1. The act of collecting together (aggregating). 2. The state of being collected into a mass, assemblage, or sum (aggregated).
agility: 1. The quality of being agile; the power of moving the limbs quickly and easily; quickness of motion 2. A faculty of being agile in body, mind, or figuratively.
agitation: 1. The act of agitating, or the state of being agitated; the state of being moved with violence, or with irregular action; commotion. 2. A stirring up or arousing; disturbance of tranquillity; disturbance of mind which shows itself by physical excitement; perturbation.
agony: 1. Extreme pain. 2. The sufferings of Jesus Christ in the garden of Gethsemane.
agrarian: 1. A person who advocates the political interests of working farmers 2. Of, or relating to, the ownership, tenure and cultivation of land.
airborne: 1. Military infantry intended to be transported by air and delivered to the battlefield by parachute or helicopter. 2. In or carried by the air.
alias: 1. Another name; an assumed name. 2. A second or further writ which is issued after a first writ has expired without effect.
alienation: 1. The act of alienating. 2. The state of being alienated.
alignment: 1. An arrangement of items in a line. 2. The process of adjusting a mechanism such that its parts are aligned; the condition of having its parts so adjusted.
allegation: 1. An assertion, especially an accusation, not necessarily based on facts. 2. The act of alleging.
allegiance: Loyalty to some cause, nation or ruler.
alleviation: 1. The act of alleviating; relief or mitigation. 2. The act of reducing pain or anything else unpleasant; easement
allocation: The process or procedure for allocating things, especially money or other resources.
allotment: 1. The act of allotting. 2. Something allotted; a share, part, or portion granted or distributed
allowance: 1. Permission; granting, conceding, or admitting 2. Acknowledgment.
allusion: An indirect reference; a hint; a reference to something supposed to be known, but not explicitly mentioned
alteration: 1. The act of altering or making different. 2. The state of being altered; a change made in the form or nature of a thing; changed condition.
alternate: 1. That which alternates with something else; vicissitude. 2. A substitute; an alternative; one designated to take the place of another, if necessary, in performing some duty.
altitude: 1. The absolute height of a location, usually measured from sea level. 2. A vertical distance.
amateurish: Suggesting or reflecting the efforts of an amateur; not seeming professional or polished.
ambassador: 1. A minister of the highest rank sent to a foreign court to represent there his sovereign or country. (Sometimes called ambassador-in-residence) 2. An official messenger and representative.
ambition: 1. Eager or inordinate desire for some object that confers distinction, as preferment, honor, superiority, political power, or literary fame; desire to distinguish one's self from other people. 2. An object of an ardent desire.
amendment: 1. An alteration or change for the better; correction of a fault or of faults; reformation of life by quitting vices. 2. In public bodies, any alteration made or proposed to be made in a bill or motion that adds, changes, substitutes, or omits.
amiable: 1. Friendly; kind; sweet; gracious 2. Of a pleasant and likeable nature; kind-hearted; easy to like
ammunition: 1. Articles used in charging firearms and ordnance of all kinds; as powder, balls, shot, shells, percussion caps, rockets, etc. 2. Military stores, or provisions of all kinds for attack or defense.
amortization: 1. The reduction of loan principal over a series of payments. 2. The distribution of the cost of an intangible asset, such as an intellectual property right, over the projected useful life of the asset.
amphibian: 1. An animal of the Amphibia; any four-legged vertebrate that does not have amniotic eggs, living both on land and in water. 2. A vehicle which can operate on land and water. See Wikipedia article on "Amphibious aircraft"
amplification: 1. The act, or result of amplifying, enlarging, extending or adding. 2. The act, or result of independently increasing some quantity, especially voltage, power or current.
amplitude: 1. The measure of something's size, especially in terms of width or breadth; largeness, magnitude. 2. The maximum absolute value of the vertical component of a curve or function, especially one that is periodic.
amusement: 1. Entertainment. 2. An activity that is entertaining or amusing, such as dancing, gunning, or fishing.
analogy: 1. A relationship of resemblance or equivalence between two situations, people, or objects, especially when used as a basis for explanation or extrapolation. 2. The proportion or the equality of ratios.
analytical: 1. Of or pertaining to analysis; resolving into elements or constituent parts 2. Using analytic reasoning as opposed to synthetic.
anatomy: 1. The art of studying the different parts of any organized body, to discover their situation, structure, and economy. 2. The science that deals with the form and structure of organic bodies; anatomical structure or organization.
ancestor: 1. One from whom a person is descended, whether on the father's or mother's side, at any distance of time; a progenitor; a forefather. 2. An earlier type; a progenitor
ancestry: 1. Condition as to ancestors; ancestral lineage; hence, birth or honorable descent. 2. A series of ancestors or progenitors; lineage, or those who compose the line of natural descent.
anecdote: 1. A short account of a real incident or person, often humorous or interesting. 2. An account which supports an argument, but which is not supported by scientific or statistical analysis.
angular: 1. A bone in the base of the lower jaw of many birds, reptiles, and fishes. 2. Relating or pertaining to an angle or angles.
animation: 1. The act of animating, or giving life or spirit. 2. (in the sense of a cartoon) The technique of making inanimate objects or drawings appear to move in motion pictures or computer graphics; the object (film, computer game, etc.) so produced
annexation: 1. Addition or incorporation of something, or territories that have been annexed. 2. A legal merging of a territory into another body.
annihilate: 1. To reduce to nothing, to destroy, to eradicate. 2. To react with antimatter, producing gamma radiation.
annotation: 1. A critical or explanatory commentary or analysis 2. A comment added to a text
announcement: 1. An act of announcing, or giving notice. 2. That which conveys what is announced.
annoyance: 1. That which annoys. 2. An act or instance of annoying.
antagonist: 1. An opponent or enemy. 2. One who antagonizes or stirs.
antecedent: 1. Any thing that precedes another thing, especially the cause of the second thing. 2. An ancestor.
antedate: 1. Prior date; a date antecedent to another which is the actual date. 2. Anticipation
anterior: 1. Before in place. 2. Before or earlier in time; prior to; preceding.
anthology: 1. A collection of literary works, such as poems or short stories, especially a collection from various authors. 2. Of a work or series containing various stories with no direct relation to one another.
anticipation: 1. The act of anticipating, taking up, placing, or considering something beforehand, or before the proper time in natural order. 2. The eagerness associated with waiting for something to occur.
antidote: 1. A remedy to counteract the effects of poison (often followed by "against," "for," or "to"). 2. Something that counteracts or prevents something harmful.
antisocial: 1. An antisocial individual. 2. Unwilling or unable to cooperate and associate normally with other people
antithesis: 1. A proposition that is the diametric opposite of some other proposition. 2. A device by which two contrasting ideas are juxtaposed in parallel form.
anxiety: 1. An unpleasant state of mental uneasiness, nervousness, apprehension and obsession or concern about some uncertain event. 2. An uneasy or distressing desire (for something).
apathetic: 1. Void of feeling; not susceptible of deep emotion 2. Of, or pertaining to apatheism.
aperture: 1. An opening, gap, or hole, usually small and narrow 2. Something which restricts the diameter of the light path through one plane in an optical system.
apologetic: 1. Having the character of apology; regretfully excusing 2. Defending by words or arguments; said or written in defense.
apparatus: 1. The entirety of means whereby a specific production is made existent or task accomplished. 2. A complex machine or instrument.
apparition: 1. An act of becoming visible; appearance; visibility. 2. The thing appearing; a visible object; a form.
appeasement: The state of being appeased; the policy of giving in to demands in order to preserve the peace.
appellate: That can be (legally) appealed to, especially of a court that hears appeals of decisions by a lower court.
appendix: 1. Something attached to something else; an attachment or accompaniment. 2. A text added to the end of a book or an article, containing additional information.
appetite: 1. Desire to eat food or consume drink. 2. Any strong desire; an eagerness or longing.
appetizer: A small, light, and usually savory first course in a meal
application: 1. The act of applying or laying on, in a literal sense 2. The substance applied.
appraisal: 1. The act or process of developing an opinion of value. 2. A judgment or assessment of the value of something, especially a formal one.
appreciable: Large enough to be estimated; perceptible; considerable.
apprehend: 1. To take or seize; to take hold of. 2. To take hold of with the understanding, that is, to conceive in the mind; to become cognizant of; to understand; to recognize; to consider.
apprehensive: 1. Anticipating something with anxiety or fear. 2. Perceptive; quick to learn; capable of understanding using one's intellect.
apprentice: 1. A trainee, especially in a skilled trade. 2. One who is bound by indentures or by legal agreement to serve a tradesperson, or other person, for a certain time, with a view to learn the art, or trade, in which his master is bound to instruct him.
appropriate: 1. To make suitable; to suit. 2. To take to oneself; to claim or use, especially as by an exclusive right.
appropriation: 1. An act or instance of appropriating. 2. That which is appropriated.
approval: 1. An expression granting permission; an indication of agreement with a proposal; an acknowledgement that a person, thing or event meets requirements. 2. An expression of favorable acceptance and encouragement; a compliment that also condones.
approximate: 1. To estimate. 2. To come near to; to approach.
aptitude: 1. Natural ability to acquire knowledge or skill. 2. The condition of being suitable.
aquarium: 1. A tank, often made of glass, for keeping live fish or other aquatic animals. 2. A public place where live fish and other aquatic animals are exhibited.
aquatic: 1. Any aquatic plant. 2. Relating to water; living in or near water, taking place in water.
architecture: 1. The art and science of designing and managing the construction of buildings and other structures, particularly if they are well proportioned and decorated. 2. The profession of an architect.
archive: 1. A place for storing earlier, and often historical, material. An archive usually contains documents (letters, records, newspapers, etc.) or other types of media kept for historical interest. 2. The material so kept, considered as a whole (compare archives).
ardent: 1. Full of ardor; fervent, passionate. 2. Burning; glowing; shining.
argumentation: 1. Inference based on reasoning from given propositions. 2. An exchange of arguments
arid: 1. Very dry. 2. Describing a very dry climate. Typically defined as less than 25 cm or 10 inches of rainfall annually.
arithmetic: 1. The mathematics of numbers (integers, rational numbers, real numbers, or complex numbers) under the operations of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. 2. Of, relating to, or using arithmetic; arithmetical.
arousal: 1. The act of arousing or the state of being aroused. 2. Sexual arousal.
arrangement: 1. The act of arranging. 2. The manner of being arranged.
arrogance: The state of being arrogant; a type of extreme or foolish pride in which someone feels much superior to another
arsenal: 1. A military establishment for the storing, development, manufacturing, testing, or repairing of arms, ammunition, and other war materiel; an armoury. 2. A stock of weapons, especially all the weapons that a nation possesses.
artery: 1. An efferent blood vessel from the heart, conveying blood away from the heart regardless of oxygenation status; see pulmonary artery. 2. A major transit corridor.
artillery: 1. Large cannon-like weapons, transportable and usually operated by more than one person. 2. An army unit that uses such weapons.
ascertain: 1. To find out definitely; to discover or establish. 2. To make (someone) certain or confident about something; to inform.
aspiration: The act of aspiring or ardently desiring; an ardent wish or desire, chiefly after what is elevated or spiritual (with common adjunct adpositions being to and of).

balcony: 1. An accessible structure extending from a building, especially outside a window. 2. An accessible structure overlooking a stage or the like.
ballast: 1. Heavy material that is placed in the hold of a ship (or in the gondola of a balloon), to provide stability. 2. Anything that steadies emotion or the mind.
balloon: 1. An inflatable buoyant object, often (but not necessarily) round and flexible. 2. Such an object as a child’s toy or party decoration.
ballot: 1. Originally, a small ball placed in a container to cast a vote; now, by extension, a piece of paper or card used for this purpose, or some other means used to signify a vote. 2. The process of voting, especially in secret; a round of voting.
bamboo: 1. A grass of the Poaceae family, characterised by its woody, hollow, round, straight, jointed stem, all of which are in the Bambuseae tribe. 2. The wood of the bamboo plant as a material or cane.
bandage: 1. A strip of gauze or similar material used to protect or support a wound or injury. 2. A strip of cloth bound round the head and eyes as a blindfold.
bankrupt: 1. One who becomes unable to pay his or her debts; an insolvent person. 2. A trader who secretes himself, or does certain other acts tending to defraud his creditors.
bankruptcy: A legally declared or recognized condition of insolvency of a person or organization.
banquet: 1. A large celebratory meal; a feast. 2. A dessert; a course of sweetmeats.
banter: 1. Sharp, good-humoured, playful, typically spontaneous conversation. 2. To engage in banter or playful conversation.
baptism: 1. A Christian sacrament, by which one is received into a church and sometimes given a name, generally involving the candidate to be anointed with or submerged in water. 2. A similar ceremony of initiation, purification or naming.
barbarian: 1. A non-Greek or a non-Roman. 2. An uncivilized or uncultured person, originally compared to the hellenistic Greco-Roman civilisation; often associated with fighting or other such shows of strength.
barbaric: Of or relating to a barbarian; uncivilized, uncultured or uncouth
barbecue: 1. A fireplace or pit for grilling food, typically used outdoors and traditionally employing hot charcoal as the heating medium. 2. A meal or event highlighted by food cooked in such an apparatus.
barometer: 1. An instrument for measuring atmospheric pressure. 2. (by extension) Anything used as a gauge or indicator.
barricade: 1. A barrier constructed across a road, especially as a military defence 2. An obstacle, barrier, or bulwark.
barrier: 1. A structure that bars passage. 2. An obstacle or impediment.
barter: 1. An exchange of goods or services without the use of money. 2. The goods or services used in such an exchange.
bashful: 1. Shy; not liking to be noticed; socially timid. 2. Indicating bashfulness.
basics: 1. A necessary commodity, a staple requirement. 2. An elementary building block, e.g. a fundamental piece of knowledge.
basin: 1. A wide bowl for washing, sometimes affixed to a wall 2. A shallow bowl used for a single serving of a drink or liquidy food
basis: 1. A physical base or foundation. 2. A starting point, base or foundation for an argument or hypothesis.
battalion: 1. An army unit having two or more companies, etc. and a headquarters. Traditionally forming part of a regiment. 2. An army unit having two or more companies, etc. and a headquarters; forming part of a brigade.
batter: 1. To hit or strike violently and repeatedly. 2. To coat with batter (the food ingredient).
battery: 1. A device used to power electric devices, consisting of a set of electrically connected electrochemical or, archaically, electrostatic cells. A single such cell when used by itself. 2. The infliction of unlawful physical violence on a person, legally distinguished from assault, which includes the threat of impending violence.
bearing: 1. To endeavour to depress the price of, or prices in. 2. To carry or convey, literally or figuratively.
beastly: 1. Pertaining to, or having the form, nature or habits of, a beast. 2. Similar to the nature of a beast; contrary to the nature and dignity of man
besiege: 1. To beset or surround with armed forces for the purpose of compelling to surrender, to lay siege to, beleaguer. 2. To beleaguer, to vex, to lay siege to, to beset.
beforehand: 1. In comfortable circumstances as regards property; forehanded. 2. (often followed by with) In a state of anticipation or preoccupation.
behemoth: 1. A great and mighty beast God shows Job in Job 40:15–24. 2. (by extension) Any great and mighty monster.
belated: 1. To retard; cause something to be late; delay; benight. 2. Later in relation to the proper time something should have happened.
belittle: To knowingly say that something is smaller or less important than it actually is, especially as a way of showing contempt or deprecation.
benchmark: 1. A standard by which something is evaluated or measured. 2. A surveyor's mark made on some stationary object and shown on a map; used as a reference point.
benefactor: 1. Somebody who gives a gift, often money to a charity. 2. Someone who performs good or noble deeds.
beneficiary: 1. One who benefits or receives an advantage. 2. One who benefits from the distribution, especially of an estate.
benevolence: 1. Disposition to do good. 2. Charitable kindness.
bequest: 1. The act of bequeathing or leaving by will. 2. The transfer of property upon the owner's death according to the will of the deceased.
bereaved: 1. To deprive by or as if by violence; to rob; to strip; to benim. 2. To take away by destroying, impairing, or spoiling; take away by violence.
beseech: 1. A request. 2. To beg or implore (a person)
bestow: 1. To lay up in store; deposit for safe keeping; to stow or place; to put something somewhere. 2. To lodge, or find quarters for; provide with accommodation.
betoken: 1. To signify by some visible object; show by signs or tokens. 2. To foreshow by present signs; indicate something future by that which is seen or known.
beverage: 1. A liquid to consume; a drink, such as tea, coffee, liquor, beer, milk, juice, or soft drinks, usually excluding water. 2. (A gift of) drink money.
bicameral: 1. Being or having a system with two, often unequal, chambers or compartments; of, signifying, relating to, or being the product of such a two-chambered system. 2. Of, having or relating to two separate legislative chambers or houses.
bicker: 1. A skirmish; an encounter. 2. A fight with stones between two parties of boys.
biennial: 1. A plant that requires two years to complete its life-cycle, germinating and growing in its first year, then producing its flowers and fruit in its second year, after which it usually dies 2. An event that happens every two years
bilateral: 1. A meeting between two people or groups. 2. Having two sides.
bilingual: 1. A person who is able to use two languages. 2. Having the ability to speak two languages.
billionaire: Somebody whose wealth is greater than one billion (109) dollars, or other currency.
binoculars: A hand-held device consisting of a series of lenses and prisms, used to magnify objects so that they can be better seen from a distance, and looked at through both eyes.
biography: 1. A person's life story, especially one published. 2. The art of writing this kind of story.
biological: 1. A biological product. 2. Of or relating to biology.
biopsy: 1. The removal and examination of a sample of tissue, cells, or bodily fluid from a living body for diagnostic purposes. 2. To take a sample (a biopsy) for pathological examination.
biosphere: 1. The part of the Earth and its atmosphere capable of supporting life. 2. The totality of living organisms and their environment.
biped: An animal, being or construction that goes about on two feet (or two legs).
birthright: Something owed since birth, due to inheritance.
biscuit: 1. (rare in the US) A small, flat, baked good which is either hard and crisp or else soft but firm: a cookie. 2. A small, usually soft and flaky bread, generally made with baking soda, which is similar in texture to a scone but which is usually not sweet.
bisect: 1. A bisector, which divides into two equal parts. 2. An envelope, card, or fragment thereof showing an affixed cut half of a regular issued stamp, over which one or more postal markings have been applied. Typically used in wartime when normal lower rate stamps may not be available.
bizarre: Strangely unconventional in style or appearance.
blackmail: 1. The extortion of money by threats of public accusation, exposure, or censure. 2. A form of protection money (or corn, cattle, etc.) anciently paid, in the north of England and south of Scotland, to the allies of robbers in order to be spared from pillage.
blacksmith: 1. A person who forges iron. 2. A person who shoes horses.
bovine: 1. An animal of the family, subfamily, tribe, or genera including cattle, buffaloes and bison. 2. Of or pertaining to cattle.
bland: 1. Having a soothing effect; not irritating or stimulating. 2. Lacking in taste, flavor, or vigor.
blasphemy: 1. An act of irreverence or contempt toward a god or toward something considered sacred; an impious act, utterance, view, etc. 2. (by extension) An act of irreverence towards anything considered inviolable; the act of disregarding a convention.
blemish: 1. A small flaw which spoils the appearance of something, a stain, a spot. 2. A moral defect; a character flaw.
blizzard: 1. A large snowstorm accompanied by strong winds and greatly reduced visibility caused by blowing snow. 2. A large amount of paperwork.
blockade: 1. The physical blocking or surrounding of a place, especially a port, in order to prevent commerce and traffic in or out. 2. (by extension) Any form of formal isolation of something, especially with the force of law or arms.
blockage: 1. The state of being blocked. 2. A thing that is blocking; an obstruction.
blueprint: 1. A type of paper-based reproduction process producing white-on-blue images, used primarily for technical and architecture's drawings, now largely replaced by other technologies. 2. A print produced with this process.
blunder: 1. A clumsy or embarrassing mistake. 2. A very bad move, usually caused by some tactical oversight.
blunt: 1. A fencer's practice foil with a soft tip. 2. A short needle with a strong point.
blur: 1. A smear, smudge or blot 2. Something that appears hazy or indistinct
bluster: 1. Pompous, officious talk. 2. A gust of wind.
boast: 1. A brag; ostentatious positive appraisal of oneself. 2. Something that one brags about.
bodyguard: 1. A person or group of persons, often armed, responsible for protecting an individual. 2. To act as bodyguard for (someone); figuratively, to protect.
boisterous: 1. Full of energy; exuberant; noisy. 2. Characterized by violence and agitation; wild; stormy.
boldness: 1. The state of being bold; courage. 2. Presumptuousness
bravado: 1. A swaggering show of defiance or courage. 2. A false show of courage.
bombardment: 1. The act of bombing, especially towns or cities 2. Heavy artillery fire
bondage: 1. The state of being enslaved or the practice of slavery. 2. (by extension) The state of lacking freedom; constraint.
brevity: 1. The quality of being brief in duration. 2. Succinctness; conciseness.
boon: 1. A prayer; petition. 2. That which is asked or granted as a benefit or favor; a gift or benefaction.
boost: 1. A push from behind, as to one who is endeavoring to climb. 2. Something that helps, or adds power or effectiveness; assistance.
boredom: 1. The state of being bored. 2. An instance or period of being bored; A bored state.
borough: 1. A fortified town. 2. A town or city.
botanical: 1. Something derived from a botanical, especially herbal, source 2. Of or pertaining to botany; relating to the study of plants
botany: 1. The scientific study of plants, a branch of biology. Typically those disciplines that involve the whole plant. 2. The plant life of a geographical area; flora.
boulder: 1. A large mass of stone detached from the surrounding land. 2. A particle greater than 256 mm in diameter, following the Wentworth scale
boulevard: 1. A broad, well-paved and landscaped thoroughfare. 2. The landscaping on the sides of a boulevard or other thoroughfare.
breakthrough: 1. An advance through and past enemy lines. 2. Any major progress; such as a great innovation or discovery that overcomes a significant obstacle.
brink: 1. The edge, margin, or border of a steep place, as of a precipice; a bank or edge. 2. The edge or border
breach: 1. A gap or opening made by breaking or battering, as in a wall, fortification or levee / embankment; the space between the parts of a solid body rent by violence 2. A breaking up of amicable relations, a falling-out.
bouquet: 1. A bunch of cut flowers. 2. The scent of a particular wine.
boutique: 1. A small shop, especially one that sells fashionable clothes, jewelry and the like. 2. A small shop located within a larger one.
braille: 1. A system of writing invented by Louis Braille, in which letters and some combinations of letters are represented by raised dots arranged in three rows of two dots each and are read by the blind and partially sighted using the fingertips. 2. To write in, or convert into, the braille writing system.
brace: 1. Armor for the arm; vambrace. 2. A measurement of length, originally representing a person's outstretched arms.
bracelet: 1. A band or chain worn around the wrist as jewelry/jewellery or an ornament. 2. The strap of a wristwatch, used to secure it around the wrist.
bracket: 1. A fixture attached to a wall to hold up a shelf. 2. Any intermediate object that connects a smaller part to a larger part, the smaller part typically projecting sideways from the larger part.
bewitch: 1. To cast a spell upon. 2. To fascinate or charm.
goose: 1. Any of various grazing waterfowl of the family Anatidae, which have feathers and webbed feet and are capable of flying, swimming, and walking on land, and which are bigger than ducks. 2. A female goose (sense 1).
mule: 1. The generally sterile male or female hybrid offspring of a male donkey and a female horse. 2. The generally sterile hybrid offspring of any two species of animals.
guinea pig: 1. A tailless rodent of the family Caviidae and the genus Cavia, with short ears and larger than a hamster; the species Cavia porcellus is often kept as a pet. 2. A rodent of any of several species within the family Caviidae.
hamster: 1. Any of various Old-World rodent species belonging to the subfamily Cricetinae. 2. Other rodents of similar appearance, such as the maned hamster or crested hamster, Lophiomys imhausi, mouse-like hamsters of genus Calomyscus, and the white-tailed rat (Mystromys albicaudatus).
mouse: 1. Any small rodent of the genus Mus. 2. A member of the many small rodent and marsupial species resembling such a rodent.
lion: 1. A big cat, Panthera leo, native to Africa, India and formerly much of Europe. 2. (by extension) Any of various extant and extinct big cats, especially the mountain lion.
tiger: 1. Panthera tigris, a large predatory mammal of the cat family, indigenous to Asia. 2. A representation of a large mythological cat, used on a coat of arms.
warthog: 1. A wild pig of the genus Phacochoerus, native to Africa. 2. A nickname for the A-10 Thunderbolt II air support warplane
buffalo: 1. Any of the Old World mammals of the family Bovidae, such as the Cape buffalo, Syncerus caffer, or the water buffalo Bubalus bubalis. 2. A related North American animal, the American bison, Bison bison.
impala: An African antelope, Aepyceros melampus, noted for its leaping ability; the male has ridged, curved horns.
kudu: A large, striped, African antelope of the species Tragelaphus imberbis (the lesser kudu) or Tragelaphus strepsiceros (the greater kudu).
springbok: A small, fast antelope native to southern Africa, Antidorcas marsupialis.
wolf: 1. The gray wolf, specifically all subspecies of the gray wolf (Canis lupus) that are not dingoes or dogs. 2. A man who makes amorous advances to many women.
caribou: Any of several North American subspecies of the reindeer, Rangifer tarandus.
opossum: Any American marsupial of the family Didelphidae. The common species of the United States is Didelphis virginiana.
chipmunk: 1. A squirrel-like rodent of the genus Tamias, native mainly to North America. 2. To speed up an audio recording, especially a song, to make the voices high-pitched.
groundhog: 1. A red-brown marmot, Marmota monax, native to North America. 2. The aardvark.
anteater: 1. Any of several animals, in suborder Vermilingua, which are noted for eating ants and termites which they catch with their long sticky tongues. 2. Any of some other unrelated species that feed with ants, including pangolin (scaly anteater), echidna (spiny anteater), aardvark and numbat (banded anteater).
vicuna: A South American mammal, Vicugna vicugna, closely related to the alpaca, llama, and guanaco.
peccary: Any of the family Tayassuidae of mammals from the Americas related to pigs and hippos
coati: Any of several omnivorous mammals, of the genus Nasua or Nasuella, in order Carnivora, that live in the range from southern United States to northern Argentina.
kangaroo: 1. A member of the Macropodidae family of large marsupials with strong hind legs for hopping, native to Australia. 2. A hooded jacket with a front pocket, usually of fleece material, a kangaroo jacket.
wallaby: Any of several species of marsupial; usually smaller and stockier than kangaroos
kiwi: 1. A New Zealander. 2. A flightless bird of the genus Apteryx native to New Zealand.
emu: 1. A cassowary (genus Casuarius). 2. A large flightless bird native to Australia, Dromaius novaehollandiae.
kookaburra: Any of several species of kingfishers in the genus Dacelo, known for their laugh-like call.
hawk: 1. A diurnal predatory bird of the family Accipitridae, smaller than an eagle. 2. Any diurnal predatory terrestrial bird of similar size and appearance to the accipitrid hawks, such as a falcon
dove: 1. A pigeon, especially one smaller in size; a bird (often arbitrarily called either a pigeon or a dove or both) of more than 300 species of the family Columbidae. 2. A person favouring conciliation and negotiation rather than conflict.
raven: 1. Any of several, generally large and lustrous black species of birds in the genus Corvus, especially the common raven, Corvus corax. 2. A jet-black colour.
jay: 1. Any one of the numerous species of birds belonging to several genera within the family Corvidae, including Garrulus, Cyanocitta, Aphelocoma, Perisoreus, Cyanocorax, Gymnorhinus, Cyanolyca, Ptilostomus, and Calocitta, allied to the crows, but smaller, more graceful in form, often handsomely coloured, usually having a crest, and often noisy. 2. Other birds of similar appearance and behaviour.
sparrow: 1. The house sparrow, Passer domesticus; a small bird with a short bill, and brown, white and gray feathers. 2. A member of the family Passeridae, comprising small Old World songbirds.
finch: 1. Any bird of the family Fringillidae, seed-eating passerine birds, native chiefly to the Northern Hemisphere and usually having a conical beak. 2. To hunt for finches, to go finching.
woodpecker: 1. Any bird of many-species subfamily Picinae, with a sharp beak suitable for pecking holes in wood. 2. Type 92 heavy machine gun
seagull: 1. Any of several white, often dark backed birds of the family Laridae having long pointed wings and short legs. 2. The symbol ̼ , which combines under a letter as a sort of accent.
swan: 1. Any of various species of large, long-necked waterfowl, of genus Cygnus (bird family: Anatidae), most of which have white plumage. 2. One whose grace etc. suggests a swan.
heron: A long-legged, long-necked wading bird of the family Ardeidae.
crane: 1. Any bird of the family Gruidae, large birds with long legs and a long neck which is extended during flight. 2. Ardea herodias, the great blue heron.
peacock: 1. A male peafowl, especially Pavo cristatus, notable for its brilliant iridescently ocellated tail. 2. A peafowl (of the genus Pavo or Afropavo), either male or female.
pheasant: A bird of family Phasianidae, often hunted for food.
quail: 1. To waste away; to fade, to wither 2. To daunt or frighten (someone)
macaw: Any of various parrots of the genera Ara, Anodorhynchus, Cyanopsitta, Orthopsittaca, Primolius and Diopsittaca of Central and South America, including the largest parrots and characterized by long sabre-shaped tails, curved powerful bills, and usually brilliant plumage.
hummingbird: Any of various small American birds in the family Trochilidae that have the ability to hover.
kingfisher: Any of various birds of the suborder Alcedines (or the family Alcedinidae sensu lato), having a large head, short tail and brilliant colouration; they feed mostly on fish.
turtle: 1. Any land or marine reptile of the order Testudines, characterised by a protective shell enclosing its body. See also tortoise. 2. (specifically) A marine reptile of that order.
alligator: 1. Either of two species of large amphibious reptile, Alligator mississippiensis or Alligator sinensis, in the genus Alligator within order Crocodilia, which have sharp teeth and very strong jaws and are native to the Americas and China, respectively. 2. Dwarf crocodile (Osteolaemus tetraspis)
gecko: 1. Any lizard of the family Gekkonidae. They are small, carnivorous, mostly nocturnal animals with large eyes and adhesive toes enabling them to climb on vertical and upside-down surfaces. 2. To move in the manner of a gecko; to attach to a vertical or upside-down surface.
skink: 1. A shin of beef. 2. A soup or pottage made from a boiled shin of beef.
monitor: 1. Someone who watches over something; a person in charge of something or someone. 2. A device that detects and informs on the presence, quantity, etc., of something.
boa: 1. Any of a group of large American snakes, of the genus Boa, subfamily Boinae, or family Boidae, including the boa constrictor, the emperor boa of Mexico, and the chevalier boa of Peru. 2. (plural "boas") A type of scarf typically made from feathers.
cobra: Any of various venomous snakes of the family Elapidae.
viper: 1. A venomous snake in the family Viperidae. 2. A dangerous, treacherous, or malignant person.
newt: A small lizard-like amphibian in the family Salamandridae that lives in the water as an adult.
caecilian: Any of a group of burrowing amphibians (order Gymnophiona or Apoda) that resemble earthworms or snakes.
chuckwalla: An iguana, of the genus Sauromalus, living in arid regions of the southwestern United States and northern Mexico.
anole: Any of the Anolis genus of arboreal American lizards (such as the American chameleon) from the iguana family which feature a brightly colored dewlap and color-changing ability.
basilisk: 1. A mythical (and heraldic) snake-like dragon type, reputed to be so venomous that its gaze was deadly. 2. A type of dragon used in heraldry.
terrapin: Any of several small turtles, of the families Emydidae and Geoemydidae, that live in fresh or brackish water.
mamba: Any of various venomous snakes of the genus Dendroaspis, native to Africa, that live in trees.
adder: 1. Any snake. 2. A name loosely applied to various snakes more or less resembling the viper; a viper.
whale: 1. Any of several species of large sea mammals of the infraorder Cetacea. 2. Something, or someone, that is very large.
dolphin: 1. A carnivorous aquatic mammal in one of several families of order Cetacea, famed for its intelligence and occasional willingness to approach humans. 2. A fish, the mahi-mahi or dorado, Coryphaena hippurus, with a dorsal fin that runs the length of the body, also known for iridescent coloration.
porpoise: 1. A small cetacean of the family Phocoenidae, related to dolphins and whales. 2. (imprecisely) Any small dolphin.
shark: 1. A scaleless, predatory fish of the superorder Selachimorpha, with a cartilaginous skeleton and 5 to 7 gill slits on each side of its head. 2. To fish for sharks.
stingray: 1. Any of various large, venomous rays, of the orders Rajiformes and Myliobatiformes, having a barbed, whiplike tail. 2. A device that simulates a cell tower, used to intercept cell phone communications.
manta: 1. A kind of fabric or blanket used in Latin America and southwestern United States. 2. Any of several very large pelagic rays of the genus Manta, with winglike pectoral fins, a long tail, and two fins resembling horns that project from the head.
octopus: 1. Any of several marine molluscs of the family Octopodidae, having no internal or external protective shell or bone (unlike the nautilus, squid and cuttlefish) and eight arms each covered with suckers. 2. The flesh of these marine molluscs eaten as food.
squid: 1. Any of several carnivorous marine cephalopod mollusks, of the order Teuthida, having a mantle, eight arms, and a pair of tentacles 2. A fishhook with a piece of bright lead, bone, or other substance fastened on its shank to imitate a squid.
cuttlefish: Any of various squid-like cephalopods (marine mollusks) of the order Sepiida that have eight arms, two retractable tentacles, and a calcareous internal shell, and can eject a dark ink when threatened
jellyfish: An almost transparent aquatic animal; any one of the acalephs, especially one of the larger species, having a jellylike appearance.
